repo_statement: C_X(s)=e^gamma (s-1)L exp[-Ein((s-1)L)] and the corrected product P-check_X=P_X C_X (proof eqs. 13-14; CURRENT_RESULTS section 9)
literature_result: In the smooth-number literature F(s,y):=rho-hat((s-1)log y) zeta(s)(s-1)log y and G(s,y):=zeta(s,y)/F(s,y), with rho-hat(s)=exp(gamma+I(-s)) and I(w)=int_0^w (e^v-1)/v dv. Since I(-z)=-Ein(z), the repository's C_X(s) equals z rho-hat(z) at z=(s-1)L, which is exactly the factor in F. With the q-factor convention D=1/(zeta(1-q^{-s})), the identity is P-check_X(s)=D(s)/G(s,X). The repository's discrepancy is therefore exactly the de Bruijn-Saias ratio G. G is the Mellin-side ratio of Psi(x,y) to de Bruijn's Lambda(x,y).
citation: O. Gorodetsky, 'Smooth integers and de Bruijn's approximation Lambda', arXiv:2212.01949, section 1.1, eq. (1.5) and the definition of G; O. Gorodetsky, 'Smooth integers and the Dickman rho function', arXiv:2211.08973 (J. Anal. Math.), section 2.2 (log G1, log G2); N. G. de Bruijn, Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Proc. Ser. A 54 (1951) 50-60, eqs. (2.6), (2.9); E. Saias, J. Number Theory 32 (1989) 78-99
notes: Object-level identity checked against Gorodetsky's definitions. I also verified numerically (mpmath) that e^gamma z e^{-Ein(z)} = z rho-hat(z). The q=67 factor is a nonvanishing entire factor on Re s>0 and changes nothing. The repository's sources file cites only GHK as context and does not cite this smooth-number lineage.

verification.evidence: Gorodetsky arXiv:2212.01949v3, section 1.1 (read in full text): rho-hat(s)=exp(gamma+I(-s)) with I(s)=int_0^s (e^v-1)/v dv, quoting [14, Lem. 2.6]. G(s,y):=zeta(s,y)/F(s,y), and F(s,y):=rho-hat((s-1)log y)zeta(s)(s-1)log y is eq. (1.5). zeta(s,y)/s and F(s,y)/s are the Mellin transforms of Psi and Lambda, citing de Bruijn p.54. De Bruijn (2.6) is lambda-hat_y=rho-hat K and (2.9) defines lambda_y; both are quoted in the paper. In arXiv:2211.08973v6 section 2.2 ('The function G'), G=G1*G2 with log G1 and log G2 as stated. Algebra check: I(-z)=-Ein(z), so C_X(s)=z rho-hat(z) and F(s,X)=zeta(s)C_X(s). Since q<=X, P_X=1/((1-q^{-s})zeta(s,X)), which gives P-check_X=D/G(s,X) exactly. I independently confirmed numerically that exp(gamma-Ein(z)) matches a method-of-steps Laplace transform of rho at z=0.7, 2 and 0.5+1.5i. Bibliographic data: 2211.08973 is J. Anal. Math. 151 (2023) 139-169; 2212.01949 is Proc. Roy. Soc. Edinburgh (doi 10.1017/prm.2023.115).
verification.correction: Minor attribution point. F(s,y) is the Mellin transform of de Bruijn's Lambda, Saias compared zeta(s,y) with F(s,y), and the ratio G with the split G1*G2 is Gorodetsky's notation. 'Gorodetsky's ratio G (de Bruijn-Saias lineage)' is more accurate than 'the de Bruijn-Saias ratio G'.

repo_statement: Proof eq. (13): int_0^inf e^{-zu}rho(u)du = exp(gamma-Ein(z)), proved via the delay ODE and the normalization 1/z at +infinity
literature_result: Lemma 2.6 (Hildebrand-Tenenbaum 1993): rho-hat(s)=exp(gamma+I(-s)) for all complex s. The proof is the same as the repository's: Laplace-transform the delay equation, then fix the constant e^gamma from the behaviour as s->+infinity.
citation: A. Hildebrand, G. Tenenbaum, 'Integers without large prime factors', J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 5 (1993) 411-484, Lemma 2.6 (numdam JTNB_1993__5_2_411_0); explicit formula quoted in Gorodetsky arXiv:2212.01949 section 1.1 '[14, Lem. 2.6]'; G. Tenenbaum, Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory, 3rd ed., chapter III.5
notes: The HT text and proof outline (ODE, constant C=e^gamma) were read. The displayed formulas in the numdam scan did not extract, so the explicit formula is taken from Gorodetsky's quotation. The repository says 'no claim is made to have independently invented these transforms', which is consistent.

verification.evidence: I rendered page 426 of the HT 1993 numdam scan (JTNB 5 (1993) 411-484) as an image and read it. Lemma 2.6 is eq. (2.16): rho-hat(s)=e^{gamma+E(-s)}, with E as in (2.3). On page 427 the proof Laplace-transforms the delay equation and fixes C=e^gamma from s->+infinity, which is the same route as PROOF.md eq. (13). The same page also has Lemma 2.5: u rho(u)=int_{u-1}^u rho, rho>0, rho'<0, rho<=1/Gamma(u+1). The proof there is a first-zero contradiction followed by induction. This is essentially verbatim the 'elementary proof' of positivity, monotonicity and the factorial bound in PROOF.md DC5.
verification.correction: Evidence is now primary (page image), not via Gorodetsky's quotation. Also cite HT Lemma 2.5 as the source of DC5's positivity/monotonicity/factorial argument.

repo_statement: Proof eq. (6) plus DC5's pointwise cancellation: P_X(1+it)C_X(1+it)=D(1+it)exp(delta_X(t)), |delta_X|<=C(1+|t|)exp(-c sqrt log X)
literature_result: Saias's lemma, reproved as Hildebrand-Tenenbaum 1993 Lemma 3.4: 'the function F(s,y) closely approximates zeta(s,y)'. It gives zeta(s,y)=F(s,y)(1+O(1/L_eps(y))) with L_eps(y)=exp((log y)^{3/5-eps}), uniformly in a region (3.13) around sigma=1 with |tau|<=L_eps(y). The proof evaluates a prime sum via Vinogradov's zero-free region and integrates along the segment from s to 1.
citation: Hildebrand-Tenenbaum 1993 (JTNB 5), Lemma 3.4 and its proof; Saias 1989 (J. Number Theory 32); Gorodetsky arXiv:2211.08973, Lemma 2.9 eq. (2.14), unconditional bound (log G1)(s,x) << x^{1-s}L(x)^{-c} for real s
notes: For the pointwise statement the repository's version is weaker: de la Vallee Poussin-strength error, line sigma=1 only, versus VK strength in a neighbourhood. The repository's (6) is, however, stated for all t, with the high-frequency tail paid separately via (8). The exact region (3.13) and the form 1+O(1/L_eps) were not machine-extracted (scanned formulas), so they are quoted from memory. The lemma's existence, role and the L_eps definition were read. The full-frequency L2/Plancherel packaging (DC5's norm form) was not found in these sources.

verification.evidence: I read page 436 of the HT 1993 scan as an image. Lemma 3.4, eq. (3.12): zeta(s,y)=F(s,y)(1+O(1/L_eps)), uniformly in (3.13): y>=y0(eps), 1-(log y)^{-2/5-eps}<=sigma<=2, |tau|<=L_eps, where L_eps(y)=exp{(log y)^{3/5-eps}}. Its proof uses (3.14)-(3.15), a prime sum evaluated with Vinogradov's zero-free region, then integration along the segment from s to 1. Gorodetsky 2211.08973 Lemma 2.9 (2.14) is stated for real eps-2<=s<=1/eps, as the draft says. Where PROOF.md eq. (6) is nontrivial (|t| up to about e^{c sqrt L}), the HT region contains it, with a VK-strength error. For larger |t|, (6)'s bound exceeds 1. So 'repo_weaker' for the pointwise statement is correct.
verification.correction: The region is now verified from the primary source rather than quoted from memory: kappa=2/5+eps, |tau|<=exp((log y)^{3/5-eps}). Also add Gorodetsky arXiv:2212.01949 Corollary 2.9. It is the complex-s version (|Im s|<=1, Re s in [0,1]) of the unconditional bound (log G1)<<L(y)^{-c}y^{1-Re s}.

repo_statement: DC6: if P-check_X is locally bounded on compacta of Re s>1/2 uniformly in X, Montel plus agreement on Re s>1 continues D, which implies RH; conversely RH implies local uniform convergence P-check_X->D. The proof itself calls this 'a classical completed Euler-product criterion'.
literature_result: Akatsuka, Theorem 2: fix sigma0 in (1/2,1). The following are equivalent: (i) psi(x)=x+O(x^{sigma0}); (ii) for some t0, (log x)^m prod_{p<=x}(1-p^{-s0})^{-1} / exp[lim_{eps->0}(int_{1+eps}^x du/(u^{s0} log u) - log(1/eps))] has a nonzero limit; (iii) the same holds for every t0; (iv) zeta(s)!=0 on Re s>sigma0. The limit is e^{(1-m)gamma}(s0-1)zeta^{(m)}(s0)/m!. Theorem 3 gives the expansion (1.9), with error (psi(x)-x)/(x^{s0}log x)+O(1/(x^{s0-Theta}log x)) when Theta<1.
citation: H. Akatsuka, 'The Euler product for the Riemann zeta-function in the critical strip', Kodai Math. J. 40 (2017) 79-101, Theorems 2 and 3 (J-STAGE full text)
notes: I checked symbolically and numerically (mpmath, s=0.75+3i, X=1e4) that Akatsuka's normalizer exp[reg. integral] equals L e^{-Ein((s-1)L)} = C_X(s)/(e^gamma (s-1)). For m=0, Akatsuka's convergence is exactly P-check_X(s0)->1/zeta(s0) (q-factor aside). Akatsuka's version is pointwise on one vertical line and characterizes each zero-free half-plane; the repository's version is local-uniform (Montel/Vitali). Both characterize RH when sigma0 ranges over (1/2,1).

verification.evidence: I read Kodai Math. J. 40 (2017) 79-101 from the J-STAGE PDF, rendering page 81 as an image. Theorem 2: for fixed sigma0 in (1/2,1), the following are equivalent: (i) psi(x)=x+O(x^{sigma0}); (ii) the quantity (1.7), (log x)^m prod(1-p^{-s0})^{-1}/exp[lim(int_{1+eps}^x du/(u^{s0}log u)-log(1/eps))], has a nonzero limit for some t0; (iii) the same for every t0; (iv) zeta!=0 on Re s>sigma0. The limit is (1.8) e^{(1-m)gamma}(s0-1)zeta^{(m)}(s0)/m!. Theorem 3 has error (psi(x)-x)/(x^{s0}log x)+O(1/(x^{s0-Theta}log x)). The text says the denominator 'is regarded as the contribution of the pole'. I checked by substitution u=e^v that the normalizer equals L e^{-Ein((s-1)L)}=C_X/(e^gamma(s-1)). Numerically at s=0.75+3i, X=1e4 both sides are -0.0851271191-0.2119688881i. The O(x^{sigma0}) in (i) is not a misprint: Akatsuka's Remark 4.3 attributes it to a zero-density argument.

repo_statement: DC6 converse: under RH the corrected product converges to D on Re s>1/2 with tail O_K(X^{1/2-sigma_K}log X), and the cutoff-convention difference is O_sigma(X^{1/2-sigma}log X) (proof section 7)
literature_result: Ramanujan (Highly Composite Numbers, unpublished part, section 68; annotated by Nicolas-Robin 1997). Assuming RH, for real 1/2<s<1: prod_{p<=x}(1-p^{-s})^{-1} = -zeta(s) exp( Li(theta(x)^{1-s}) + 2s x^{1/2-s}/((2s-1)log x) + S_s(x)/log x + O(x^{1/2-s}/log^2 x) ), where S_s(x)=-s sum_rho x^{rho-s}/(rho(rho-s)). Akatsuka Lemma 2.1: the full-local-factor log-product minus sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n)/(n^s log n) is (1/2)log 2+O(1/log x) at sigma=1/2 and O(x^{-(sigma-1/2)}(log x)^{-1}) otherwise.
citation: S. Ramanujan, 'Highly composite numbers' (annotated by J.-L. Nicolas and G. Robin), Ramanujan J. 1 (1997) 119-153, as quoted in I. Kaneko arXiv:1902.04203 section 2.1; Akatsuka 2017, Lemma 2.1 and section 5
notes: Ramanujan's formula is quoted via Kaneko (full text read), not from the primary source. I verified numerically that the repository's single-valued C_X(s) = -exp(li(X^{1-s})) for real s<1 (s=0.7 and 0.9, X=1e4), so the entire Ein form reproduces Ramanujan's minus sign automatically. The repository's O(X^{1/2-sigma}log X) bound on the prime-power tail is weaker by log^2 than Akatsuka's Lemma 2.1.

verification.evidence: Kaneko arXiv:1902.04203 section 2.1 (full text) quotes Ramanujan's RH formula for real 1/2<s<1 exactly as the draft gives it. Akatsuka (section 1) says Ramanujan 'did not give a convincing proof'. Akatsuka Lemma 2.1 concerns the 1/k-weighted tail sum_{p<=x,p^k>x} 1/(k p^{ks}). PROOF.md section 7's cutoff tail is the log p-weighted log-derivative tail sum_{p<=X,k>=2,p^k>X}(log p)p^{-ks}. These are different objects. I computed both up to X=1e7. The log p tail is about X^{1/2-sigma}/(2sigma-1), with ratio 1.01-1.05 at sigma=0.75 and 0.9 and no 1/log X factor. The 1/k tail is about X^{1/2-sigma}/((2sigma-1)log X). DC6's overall RH-conditional rate O_K(X^{1/2-sigma}log X) is the standard order: it matches Gorodetsky 2212.01949 Lemma 2.11 and Cor. 2.9 (log G1<<y^{1/2-Re s}log y under RH), and Akatsuka Thm 3 with von Koch. I confirmed C_X(s)=-exp(li(X^{1-s})) at s=0.7 and 0.9 (X=1e4) to 30 digits.
verification.correction: Relation should be closely_analogous, not repo_weaker. Ramanujan gives a sharper asymptotic expansion, but only for real s and without a rigorous proof. The repository's converse is locally uniform in complex s and has the standard RH rate. The note 'weaker by log^2 than Akatsuka Lemma 2.1' is wrong: Lemma 2.1 bounds the 1/k tail, and the section 7 bound is on the log p tail, whose sharp size is X^{1/2-sigma}/(2sigma-1). The repository is loose there by one log X, not log^2.

repo_statement: Proof eqs. (17)-(18): d/ds log C_X(s)=X^{1-s}/(s-1). The corrected logarithmic derivative -sum_{p<=X} log p/(p^s-1) - X^{1-s}/(s-1) is the 'integrated, causal version of a balanced continuum-tail source'.
literature_result: GHK, Theorem 1 and eq. (13), unconditional for Re s>=0 off zeros and the pole: log zeta(s) = sum_n Lambda(n)v(e^{log n/log X})/(n^s log n) - sum_rho U((s-rho)log X) + U((s-1)log X) - sum_m U((s+2m)log X), where U(z)=int u(x)E1(z log x)dx. For |t|>=2 they bound the pole term U((s-1)log X) as an error, << X^{K+1+max(1-sigma,0)}/(|s|log X)^K, instead of keeping it. Gonek 2012, Theorem 3.1, starts from the Selberg-type explicit formula (Titchmarsh Thm 14.20). That formula contains the pole term (X^{2(1-s)}-X^{1-s})/((1-s)^2 log X), and Z_X contains -F_2((s-1)log X).
citation: S. M. Gonek, C. P. Hughes, J. P. Keating, Duke Math. J. 136 (2007) 507-549, arXiv:math/0511182, Theorem 1 and eqs. (10), (12), (13); S. M. Gonek, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 364 (2012) 2157-2191, arXiv:0704.3448, Theorem 3.1, eqs. (9)-(11)
notes: In the sharp limit u->delta_e, U->E1, so the repository's C_X = exp(-E1((s-1)L)) (made entire via Ein) is exactly the reciprocal of GHK's exponentiated pole term. GHK and Gonek treat it as negligible at height |t|>=2; the repository keeps it exactly for all s, which is what matters near t=0 and at fixed s as X->infinity.

verification.evidence: GHK math/0511182 full text. Theorem 1 holds for sigma>=0, |t|>=2. In (4) U(z)=int u(x)E1(z log x)dx, and Lemma 1 (10) is the Bombieri-Hejhal formula. (12) integrates (10), and (13) contains +U((s0-1)log X), 'for all points in Re s>=0 not equal to the pole or one of the zeros'. The pole term is bounded by X^{K+1+max{1-sigma0,0}}/(|s0|log X)^K. Gonek 0704.3448 full text: Theorem 3.1 starts from Titchmarsh 14.20 with pole term (X^{2(1-s)}-X^{1-s})/((1-s)^2 log X). Z_X in (9) contains -F2((s-1)log X). The draft omits one thing. In his zeta_X* section, Gonek explicitly defines the pole-corrected product P*_X(s)=P_X(s)exp(-F2((s-1)log X)), keeping the pole factor exactly because he needs X much larger than t.
verification.correction: Do not say that 'Gonek treats the pole term as negligible' without qualification. Gonek 2012 also gives P*_X(s)=P_X(s)exp(-F2((s-1)log X)): a pole-corrected (Selberg-weighted, Taylor-kernel F2) finite Euler product. This is the closest literature analogue of P_X/C_X and weakens the 'keeps it exactly for all s' contrast. The sharp limit u->delta_e is outside GHK's hypotheses, so 'closely_analogous' is the right relation.

repo_statement: DC6 Montel/continuation step and the general idea that convergence of a (corrected) Euler product right of 1/2 forces nonvanishing
literature_result: Conrad, Theorem 3.3: for an Euler product holomorphic on Re s>=1/2 (no pole), with |alpha_{p,j}|<=1 and Re s0>1/2, the partial products at s0 have a nonzero limit iff sum_{Np^k<=x} (...)/(k Np^{k s0}) converges; then L continues to Re s>Re s0 with L!=0, and (3.3) holds. Theorem 6.2/1.3: on the critical line, convergence is equivalent to psi_L(x)=o(sqrt x log x). Theorems 1.2 and 5.11: the sqrt 2 factor comes from the second moment. Kaneko (Theorem 1.1, Case III) gives GRH-conditional asymptotics in Re s>1/2 for Dirichlet L and records that convergence for chi!=1 on Re s>1/2 is equivalent to GRH.
citation: K. Conrad, 'Partial Euler products on the critical line', Canad. J. Math. 57 (2005) 267-297, Theorems 1.2, 1.3, 3.3, 5.11, 6.2 (author PDF kconrad.math.uconn.edu/articles/eulerprod.pdf); I. Kaneko, arXiv:1902.04203, Theorem 1.1 and eq. (1.2)
notes: Conrad explicitly excludes L-functions with a pole. Akatsuka (PA4) states that his results 'do not apply to the Riemann zeta-function because of the pole' and fills that case. The repository's C_X plays exactly the role of Akatsuka's 'contribution of the pole'.

verification.evidence: Conrad, Canad. J. Math. 57 (2005), author PDF eulerprod.pdf, full text. Theorem 3.3 holds for Re s0>1/2. A nonzero limit of the partial Euler products is equivalent to existence of lim sum_{Np^k<=x}(...)/(k Np^{ks0}). Then L continues to Re s>Re s0 with L!=0, and (3.3) holds. Theorems 1.2 and 5.11 assume L holomorphic on Re s>=1/2 and tie sqrt 2 to the second moment L2. Theorem 6.2 states the partial Dirichlet series sum b_n/n^{1/2+it}+m_t loglog x converges iff psi_L(x)=o(sqrt x log x). Theorem 6.3 is the Euler-product version; Theorem 1.3 is its elliptic-curve case. Theorem 4.1 and Example 4.2 (Mertens over K) are as cited. Kaneko eq. (1.2) is 'Conrad [2] has shown that GRH is equivalent to (1.2)', and Akatsuka says Conrad's class excludes the pole.
verification.correction: Theorem 3.3 does not assume holomorphy on Re s>=1/2; continuation is part of its conclusion. Its condition simply never holds for zeta below 1. The 'no pole' hypothesis belongs to Theorems 1.2 and 5.11. For the Euler-product equivalence on the critical line, cite Theorem 6.3; Theorem 6.2 is the partial-Dirichlet-series form.

repo_statement: DC6 'second cost': below one the absolute PNT majorant of the discrepancy integral diverges, which is a failure of that bound and not divergence of the signed discrepancy; also the converse tail O(X^{1/2-sigma}log X) under RH
literature_result: Gorodetsky, Lemma 2.11 (2.16): for real s>Theta, log G1(s,x) = -int_x^inf d(psi(t)-t)/(t^s log t). This is the repository's signed discrepancy integral. Lemma 2.9 (2.14): unconditional bound (log G1)(s,x) << x^{1-s}L(x)^{-c} (growing for s<1). (2.15): (log G1)(s,x) = (psi(x)-x+O(x^Theta))/(x^s log x). Proposition 2.12: log G2(s,x) is comparable to x^{max(1-2s,1/2-s)}/max(1,|s-1/2|log x). Corollary 5.4: explicit zero-sum formula log G1(s,x) = -sum_{|Im(rho-s)|<=T} int_0^inf x^{rho-s-t}/(rho-s-t)dt + (trivial zeros) + R0. arXiv:2212.01949, Lemma 2.11: assuming RH, G(s,y)=1+O(y^{1/2-s}log y) for real s in [1/2+eps,1].
citation: O. Gorodetsky, arXiv:2211.08973, Lemmas 2.8, 2.9, 2.11, Proposition 2.12, Corollaries 5.4-5.5; O. Gorodetsky, arXiv:2212.01949, Lemma 2.8, Corollary 2.9, Lemma 2.11
notes: The literature quantifies, two-sidedly and for real s, what the repository states qualitatively in DC6. These are exactly the 'signed discrepancy' objects named in OPEN_CUTS section 6, conditional on Theta.

verification.evidence: Gorodetsky 2211.08973v6 full text: Lemma 2.8, log G1(s,x)=Omega_+-(x^{Theta-s-eps}) for fixed s>-2. Lemma 2.9: (2.14) (log G1)^{(i)}<<(log x)^i x^{1-s}L(x)^{-c} for real eps-2<=s<=1/eps, and (2.15) =(log x)^{i-1}(psi(x)-x+O(x^Theta))/x^s. Lemma 2.11 (2.16): log G1(s,x)=-int_x^inf d(psi(t)-t)/(t^s log t) for real s>Theta. Proposition 2.12 (2.17): log G2 comparable to x^{max(1-2s,1/2-s)}/max(1,|s-1/2|log x) for 1>=s>=eps/log x. Corollary 5.4 is the zero-sum formula for complex s with zeta(s+t)!=0 for t>=0. Gorodetsky 2212.01949: Lemma 2.8 (complex s, condition min|rho-s-t|>>1), Cor. 2.9 and Lemma 2.11 (RH: G=1+O_eps(y^{1/2-s}log y), real s in [1/2+eps,1]). All match the draft.
verification.correction: Minor. The DC6 remark is methodological, so 'repo_weaker' compares a remark with a theorem. Note that Corollary 5.4 and 2212.01949 Lemma 2.8 / Cor. 2.9 already cover complex s.

repo_statement: DC4: the second-scale profile uses 1+Omega(z)=exp(E1(z)) (Buchstab Laplace transform) and the regular derivative r=omega' after removing the jump at u=1
literature_result: Classical Buchstab-Dickman Laplace duality: 1+omega-hat(z) = exp(E1(z)) = 1/(z rho-hat(z)) (Buchstab 1937; de Bruijn 1950; Tenenbaum III.6). In the same circle of ideas, Weingartner relates the error terms of de Bruijn's smooth approximation Lambda(x,y) and of Buchstab-function rough approximations W, V, V* (built from mu_y(u)=int_0^u omega(u-v)y^{-v}dv) via Mobius inversion over y-smooth numbers.
citation: G. Tenenbaum, Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory (3rd ed., AMS GSM 163), chapter III.6 (Buchstab function, Laplace transform); A. Weingartner, 'A link between error terms when counting smooth and rough numbers', arXiv:2604.22058, section 1
notes: I verified the identity numerically (method of steps for omega on [1,40], h=1e-4): 1+Omega(z) vs exp(E1(z)) agrees to about 3e-5 at z=0.5, 1, 2. The book citation is from memory. Weingartner's introduction (read in full text) confirms the smooth/rough Lambda/V pairing, the analogue of the repository's DC1 + DC4 + DC5 structure on counting functions rather than Mobius sums.

verification.evidence: The identity follows directly from verified sources. By HT Lemma 2.6 (read) and E1(z)=Ein(z)-gamma-log z, z rho-hat(z)=exp(-E1(z)) on Re z>0, so 1/(z rho-hat(z))=exp(E1(z)). PROOF.md (12) proves 1+Omega(z)=exp(E1(z)) from the delay equation. Weingartner arXiv:2604.22058 exists (submitted 2026-04-23). Its introduction, read in full text, defines Lambda in (1) via [6, Eq. III.5.81], de Bruijn's W(x,y)=x mu_y(u)Pi(y)e^gamma log y with mu_y(u)=int_0^u omega(u-v)y^{-v}dv, and the variants V and V*. It links Delta=Psi-Lambda with Q=V-Phi through Mobius inversion over S_y. I did not open Tenenbaum's book.
verification.correction: The chapter location (Tenenbaum III.6) and the attributions to Buchstab 1937 / de Bruijn 1950 are unverified here. A checkable primary chain is HT 1993 Lemma 2.6 plus the E1/Ein relation. The evidence level should read 'derivation plus fulltext (Weingartner)', not memory.

repo_statement: Horizon preservation (proof eq. 16; CURRENT_RESULTS section 9): F-check_{X,a}=F_a on 0<=x<log X, with the continuum correction acting only after the horizon
literature_result: de Bruijn's Lambda(x,y)=x lambda_y(u), with lambda_y(u)=int rho(u-v) d(floor(y^v)/y^v), equals floor(x)=Psi(x,y) for x<=y (since rho=1 on [0,1]). It satisfies a continuous Buchstab identity, and its Mellin transform is F(s,y)/s. It is the counting-function analogue (zeta(s,y) side) of the repository's Mobius-side (1/zeta(s,y) side) causal correction: exact before the horizon, Dickman-convolved afterwards.
citation: de Bruijn 1951 (Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Proc. Ser. A 54), eq. (2.9); Gorodetsky arXiv:2212.01949 section 1 (definition of lambda_y, continuous Buchstab identity, Mellin transform F(s,y)/s); Weingartner arXiv:2604.22058 eq. (1)
notes: The repository's I-k* convolution acts on the Mobius side, with kernel -rho' supported after L. The smooth-number literature applies the same Dickman convolution to the counting function. I found no source that states the Mobius-side causal operator and its full-frequency L2 rate verbatim.

verification.evidence: Gorodetsky 2212.01949 section 1 (full text) defines lambda_y(u)=int rho(u-v)d(floor(y^v)/y^v) (de Bruijn (2.9)) and Lambda=x lambda_y(u). It states the continuous Buchstab identity and that F(s,y)/s is the Mellin transform of Lambda. From the definition, for u<1 one has rho(u-v)=1 on v<=u, so lambda_y(u)=floor(x)/x and Lambda(x,y)=floor(x)=Psi(x,y) for x<y. Weingartner eq. (1) has the same Lambda. Structurally, G-1 and 1/G-1 both have Mellin 'support' after the horizon: zeta(s,y)/zeta(s) has coefficients on 1 and on n>y only, and 1/C_y=1+(measure after log y). So de Bruijn's exactness for x<y and the repository's eq. (16) are two faces of one fact.

repo_statement: Proof (6), (9)-(10) and DC3: at Re s=1 the raw products converge, P_X(1+it)->D(1+it) for t!=0, with explicit factor exp(E1(itL)), leading error ~1/(itL) and norm error ~ sqrt(C_g)/log X
literature_result: Mertens (1874): prod_{p<=x}(1-1/p)^{-1} ~ e^gamma log x. Convergence of prod_{p<=x}(1-p^{-1-it0})^{-1} to zeta(1+it0) for t0!=0 is classical (Akatsuka cites Titchmarsh section 3.15). Conrad Example 4.2 gives the Mertens formula over number fields via a Tauberian theorem (Theorem 4.1).
citation: F. Mertens, J. reine angew. Math. 78 (1874) 46-62; Akatsuka 2017, section 1 (citing Titchmarsh section 3.15); Conrad 2005, Theorem 4.1 and Example 4.2
notes: The pointwise convergence is classical. The repository's added content is the identified L2 leading constant (DC3) and the second Buchstab profile (DC4). I found no verbatim prior statement of these, but the search was not exhaustive; see the Alladi / de la Breteche-Tenenbaum check in the recommended actions.

verification.evidence: Akatsuka section 1 cites Mertens [12, p.53] and Titchmarsh section 3.15 for prod(1-p^{-1-it0})^{-1}->zeta(1+it0). Conrad Theorem 4.1 and Example 4.2 are verified in full text. It imports quantitative PNT, which already contains the pointwise convergence, and it neither contains nor implies Mertens' theorem or pointwise convergence for every t!=0. The pointwise rate (9)-(10), exp(J(tL))-1 ~ e^{-itL}/(itL), is the classical sum_{p>X}p^{-1-it} ~ E1(itL).

obstruction: The OPEN_CUTS section 6 target is equivalent to RH, and its sigma0-version is equivalent to the open quasi-RH problem. By Akatsuka Thm 2, for each sigma0 in (1/2,1), convergence of the corrected product to a nonzero limit at even one point of the line Re s=sigma0 (m=0) is equivalent to zeta!=0 on Re s>sigma0, and to psi(x)=x+O(x^{sigma0}). Together with the repository's DC6 Montel argument, local uniform boundedness on compacta of Re s>sigma0 is equivalent to zeta!=0 there.
citation: Akatsuka, Kodai Math. J. 40 (2017), Theorems 2-3; repository PROOF.md DC6 (cdf2f159...)
how_it_constrains: No contribution to section 6 can be unconditional unless it proves a zero-free half-plane; even Theta<1 is open. Any claimed 'signed discrepancy estimate with explicit dependence on distance from the critical line' at fixed s with sigma<1 is either conditional on a zero-location hypothesis or proves quasi-RH. The section 6 target should not be listed as a bounded contribution.

obstruction: There are Omega-plus/minus lower bounds for the corrected-product discrepancy. For fixed real s>-2, log G1(s,x) = Omega-plus/minus(x^{Theta-s-eps}) (Landau's oscillation theorem). Combined with Littlewood's psi(x)-x = Omega-plus/minus(sqrt x logloglog x) and (2.15), log G1(s,x) = Omega-plus/minus(x^{1/2-s} logloglog x/log x); the arXiv text of Cor. 2.10 prints 'log log x'.
citation: Gorodetsky arXiv:2211.08973, Lemma 2.8, Corollary 2.10, eq. (2.15); Littlewood via Montgomery-Vaughan Thm 15.11
how_it_constrains: Even under RH, no bound for log(D/P-check_X) better than about X^{1/2-sigma}logloglog X/log X is possible. The repository's RH-conditional rate O(X^{1/2-sigma}log X) is optimal up to roughly log^2 X. If Theta>1/2, the discrepancy is unbounded at real s<Theta.

verification.evidence: Gorodetsky 2211.08973 Lemma 2.8 is Omega_+-(x^{Theta-s-eps}) for fixed s>-2. Corollary 2.10 prints 'Omega_+-(x^{1/2-s} log log x/log x)'; Littlewood's psi(x)-x=Omega_+-(sqrt x logloglog x) is cited as [23, Thm. 15.11]. Combined with (2.15), the logloglog version follows, so the printed 'log log' is a typo or extraction artifact, as the draft flags. Since log G2 is about X^{1/2-sigma}/((sigma-1/2)log X) (Prop. 2.12), the Omega bound transfers from log G1 to log G=log(D/P-check_X). Under RH, Gorodetsky 2212.01949 Lemma 2.11 gives O(y^{1/2-s}log y), so the gap is about log^2 X/logloglog X, for fixed real s.

obstruction: The Dickman/pole correction is a low-height device. Since e^{-E1(z)} = 1 - e^{-z}/z(1+O(1/|z|)), C_X(sigma+it) = 1+O(X^{1-sigma}/(|t| log X)) once |t| log X >> X^{1-sigma}. By GHK eq. (13) (sharp limit) and Gorodetsky Cor. 5.4, the whole remaining discrepancy log(D/P-check_X) is the zero sum sum_rho E1((s-rho)log X) plus trivial-zero and prime-power terms.
citation: GHK arXiv:math/0511182 eq. (13); Gorodetsky arXiv:2211.08973 Corollary 5.4; DLMF 6.12 (E1 asymptotics); derivation is elementary
how_it_constrains: The causal correction exactly removes the pole contribution and carries no information about zeros. Any half-plane progress must control sum_rho E1((s-rho)L), the classical explicit-formula zero sum. Positivity of nu=-rho' cannot help there.

verification.evidence: From Gorodetsky Cor. 5.4, -int_0^inf x^{rho-s-t}/(rho-s-t)dt=E1((s-rho)log x) by substitution. So log G1 = sum_rho E1((s-rho)L) + sum_k E1((s+2k)L) + R0 (+ the half-weight term), and log G2 is the prime-power part. This matches GHK (13) in the sharp limit, with the pole term cancelling against C_X. The bound C_X=1+O(X^{1-sigma}/(|t|log X)) when X^{1-sigma}=O(|t|log X) is Gorodetsky 2212.01949 (2.2), s rho-hat(s)=1+O(e^{-sigma}/|t|) for sigma<0, at z=(s-1)L.
verification.correction: The zero sum is not absolutely convergent at sharp cutoff. State it in Gorodetsky's truncated form (|Im(rho-s)|<=T plus R0), or in GHK's smoothed form.

obstruction: Zero-counting obstruction to uniform approximation. Finite Euler products have no zeros in Re s>0. C_X = e^gamma z e^{-Ein(z)} vanishes only at s=1, so P-check_X is zero-free on Re s>0 except at s=1, while D has poles at the zeros of zeta.
citation: Gonek, Trans. AMS 364 (2012), arXiv:0704.3448, remark after Theorem 3.5
how_it_constrains: Convergence P-check_X->D can hold at best locally on Re s>1/2. There is no uniform approximation on any region meeting the critical line, and the boundary line requires a DRH-type pointwise statement (O6).

verification.evidence: P_X(s)=prod(1-p^{-s}) vanishes only on Re s=0. C_X=e^gamma z e^{-Ein(z)} vanishes only at z=0, i.e. s=1. D has poles at the zeta zeros. In Gonek 0704.3448 (full text), the converse after Theorem 3.5 uses |zeta P_X^{-1}-1|<=B log^{(1-C)/2}tau to exclude zeros. That is exactly the 'finite Euler products are zero-free' mechanism.

obstruction: D=1/(zeta(s)(1-q^{-s})) is unbounded on every vertical line Re s=sigma in (1/2,1]. Bohr-Courant: zeta(sigma+it) is dense in C for 1/2<sigma<=1. Quantitative Omega results: Montgomery 1977 under RH; resonance/Diophantine lower bounds for the Selberg class (Aistleitner-Pankowski).
citation: H. Bohr, R. Courant, J. reine angew. Math. 144 (1914); H. L. Montgomery, Comment. Math. Helv. 52 (1977); C. Aistleitner, L. Pankowski, 'Large values of L-functions from the Selberg class', arXiv:1507.06066 (J. Math. Anal. Appl. 2017)
how_it_constrains: Any explicit-dependence estimate must be local in height (compact K), with constants growing at least as fast as extreme values of 1/zeta. A bound uniform on vertical lines is false.

repo_statement: L-106212.3: 1-x/2=prod_m(1-x^m)^{gamma_m}, gamma_m=(1/m)sum_{d|m}mu(d)2^{-m/d}
literature_result: Cyclotomic (necklace) identity: 1/(1-kz)=prod_{j>=1}(1-z^j)^{-M_j(k)}, where M_n(k)=(1/n)sum_{d|n}mu(d)k^{n/d} is Moreau's necklace polynomial. It is a polynomial identity in k, so it can be specialized at k=1/2. Then gamma_m=M_m(1/2), and inverting gives exactly L-106212.3.
citation: C. Moreau, Nouv. Ann. Math. (2) 11 (1872) 309-331; N. Metropolis & G.-C. Rota, 'Witt vectors and the algebra of necklaces', Adv. Math. 50 (1983) 95-125, doi:10.1016/0001-8708(83)90035-X; statement checked on the Wikipedia 'Necklace polynomial' page (cyclotomic identity section)
notes: I checked by exact rational power-series arithmetic that prod_{m<=16}(1-x^m)^{gamma_m} = 1 - x/2 + O(x^17) (gamma_1..gamma_6 = 1/2,-1/8,-1/8,-3/64,-3/32,3/128). The repository's proof (logarithms plus divisor inversion) is the standard proof. At alpha=q, M_m(q) counts monic irreducibles of degree m in F_q[T].

verification.evidence: L-106212 source (gh API, @86cac1d6) states gamma_m=(1/m)sum_{d|m}mu(d)2^{-m/d}, sum_{m|n} m gamma_m = 2^{-n}, and 1-x/2=prod(1-x^m)^{gamma_m}. That is exactly the cyclotomic identity 1/(1-kz)=prod(1-z^j)^{-M(k,j)} at k=1/2, inverted; gamma_m=M(1/2,m). I re-derived it by logarithms. By hand I checked gamma_2=gamma_3=-1/8, gamma_4=-3/64, gamma_5=-3/32 and gamma_6=3/128. zbMATH 0545.05009 confirms Metropolis-Rota, Adv. Math. 50 (1983) 95-125, including M(alpha;n)=(1/n)sum mu(n/d)alpha^d. Numdam NAM_1872_2_11__309_0 gives Moreau, 'Sur les permutations circulaires distinctes', Nouv. Ann. Math. (2) 11 (1872), pp. 309-314.
verification.correction: The Moreau page range is 309-314, not 309-331. Everything else stands.

repo_statement: L-106212.4: an Euler product prod_P(1-chi(P)u^{deg P}/2) factors as a tower prod_m L(u^m,chi^m)^{-gamma_m} (the 'Witt tower of L-functions')
literature_result: Ramaré's Theorem 2 expresses -sum_{p = a mod q, p>=P} log(1-p^{-s}) as a Mobius-weighted combination sum_l sum_{d|l} (mu(d)/l) sum_chi chi(a)... log L_P(ls,chi^d). The paper explicitly uses Witt's generalized necklace identity (Lemma 11) to write Euler products of polynomials in p^{-s} as products of powers of L(ms,chi^d). Earlier work: Moree's 'Approximation of singular series and automata'; Ettahri-Ramaré-Surel.
citation: O. Ramaré, 'Accurate computations of Euler products over primes in arithmetic progressions', arXiv:1911.10991, Thm 2 and Lemma 11 (citing E. Witt, J. Reine Angew. Math. 177 (1937) 152-160); S. Ettahri, O. Ramaré, L. Surel, arXiv:1908.06808; P. Moree, manuscripta math. 101 (2000)
notes: Same technique (necklace/Witt expansion of a local factor, then Euler products of L-functions at m*s). Ramaré works in number fields with real s>1, not in function fields with the alpha=1/2 'Boolean' factor. The function-field specialization with its resonance classification (principal constituents at m divisible by ord chi) is a direct corollary. I did not find it stated in exactly this form.

verification.evidence: I read arXiv:1911.10991v1 in full text. Theorem 2 writes -sum_{p=a[q],p>=P} log(1-1/p^s) as sum_l (1/(l phi(q))) sum_{d|l} mu(d) sum_chi chi(a) log L_P(ls,chi^d). Lemma 11 is Witt's multivariable generalized necklace identity with integer exponents M(m_1..m_k), citing Witt, J. Reine Angew. Math. 177 (1937) 152-160. Ramaré's references [6] and [8] confirm Ettahri-Ramaré-Surel arXiv:1908.06808 and Moree, manuscripta math. 101 (2000) 385-399. The technique (Witt/necklace expansion of a local factor, then products of L-functions at ms) is the one behind L-106212.4. 'closely_analogous' is right: Ramaré's Lemma 11 has integer coefficients and integer exponents, while the repository's 1-x/2 with rational exponents gamma_m is the cyclotomic identity at alpha=1/2 (PA01).

literature_result: Afshar-Porritt Proposition 3.1: for chi nonprincipal mod d with deg d = m, |z| <= A and n >= 1, D_z(n,chi) := [T^n]L(T,chi)^z satisfies |D_z(n,chi)| <= q^{n/2} binom(n+Am-(A+1), n) <= q^{n/2} binom(n+Am, n). The proof uses L(T,chi)=prod_{j<=m-1}(1-alpha_j T) with |alpha_j| in {0,1,sqrt q} (Weil) and the binomial majorant.
citation: A. Afshar & S. Porritt, 'The function field Sathe-Selberg formula in arithmetic progressions and short intervals', arXiv:1709.01963 (Acta Arith. 2019), Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 2
notes: With z=-1/2 and A=1/2, the Afshar-Porritt bound is q^{n/2} binom(n+m/2-3/2, n), which equals the repository's majorant at r=m-1. The bound is explicit and uniform in the conductor degree m. Their Theorem 2 uses it in the range m <= (1/2 - (1+log(1+A/2))/log q) n.

verification.evidence: I read arXiv:1709.01963v4 in full text; zbMATH gives Acta Arith. 187 (2019), no. 2, 101-124. Proposition 3.1: for chi != chi_0, |z|<=A and n>=1, |D_z(n,chi)| <= q^{n/2} binom(n+Am-(A+1),n). Here D_z(n,chi) is the coefficient of T^n in L(T,chi)^z, and L(T,chi) is a product of m-1 factors (1-alpha_j T) with |alpha_j| in {0,1,sqrt q} (Rosen Prop. 4.3 plus Weil). The proof majorizes by (1-sqrt(q)T)^{-A(m-1)}. Proposition 3.1 has no A>1 restriction. At A=1/2 the bound is q^{n/2} binom(n+m/2-3/2,n) = q^{n/2}[u^n](1-u)^{-(m-1)/2}. That is the repository's L-106213.2 at r=m-1, proved the same way. The Theorem 2 range m <= (1/2-(1+log(1+A/2))/log q) n is quoted correctly.

repo_statement: L-106213 as a whole: complete nonprincipal half-source degree shells have square-root size at fixed q and conductor
literature_result: Function-field Selberg-Delange / Sathe-Selberg method. The generating function C(T,z)=M(T,z)zeta(T)^z, with character twists L(T,chi)^z bounded through Weil's RH for curves, gives asymptotics and square-root error terms for z^{omega(f)}-weighted counts over F_q[T], including arithmetic progressions.
citation: Afshar & Porritt, arXiv:1709.01963, Sections 2-3; number-field prototype: Selberg-Delange method (Tenenbaum, Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory, Ch. II.5)
notes: The repository's z=-1/2 squarefree-twisted series with the m>=2 tower isolated is a specific instance of the same method. The principal quadratic resonance (1-qu^2)^{-1/8} corresponds to the zeta(T^2)-type factor appearing in M(T,z) for quadratic chi.

verification.evidence: Afshar-Porritt section 3.2 defines A(T,z,chi)=sum mu^2(f) z^{omega(f)} chi(f) T^{deg f} = prod_p(1+z chi(p)T^{deg p}). With coefficients A_z(n,chi), Proposition 3.3 (A>1, |z|<=A, n>=2, chi nonprincipal mod d, deg d=m) gives |A_z(n,chi)| <= q^{n/2} binom(n+Am,n) n^{c_A}. By Lemma 3.2 and Prop. 2.5, c_A depends only on A, not on q or chi. At z=-1/2, A_{-1/2}(n,chi) is exactly the repository's H_{chi,n}: compare L-106212.1, sum mu^2(F)(-1/2)^{omega(F)}chi(F)u^{deg F}.
verification.correction: The relation is stronger than 'closely_analogous'. Afshar-Porritt Prop. 3.3 is a bound for the same object, and it is uniform in q and conductor degree m. Its polynomial factor binom(n+Am,n)n^{c_A} (A>1) is weaker than the repository's (n+1)^{r/2+2} at fixed chi,q, so neither statement contains the other. But the conductor-uniform complete-shell bound that the draft's TT01 proposes to build already exists. What B-027 still needs is only the U-rough stopped shells and masks. Afshar-Porritt do not isolate a quadratic resonance: the zeta(T^2)-type factor sits inside their F(T,z,chi)=prod(1+chi(p)zT^{deg p})(1-chi(p)T^{deg p})^z and is handled by Lemma 3.2. The 'corresponds to the zeta(T^2)-type factor' remark is the draft's interpretation, not a statement in Afshar-Porritt.

repo_statement: L-106000.8/.10: principal-character Euler restoration L(s,chi_0)=zeta(s)(1-ell^{-s}); coefficient identity b(n)-1_{ell|n}b(n/ell)=mu(n)

notes: The repository already treats this as an elementary case split. The non-classical content of L-106000 is the source typing (the marked-67 filter and applying the completion only after linear recombination) and the B-022 caveat.

Chapter pointers (Davenport Ch. 4-5 on induced characters, Montgomery-Vaughan section 4.3) are from memory and immaterial. The source-typing caveat (B-022) is described correctly.

The principal term psi(x)-x needs the zeta zero-free region (PNT) separately. (b) Iwaniec-Sarnak (zbMATH review): in the level aspect, 'the percentage exceeds fifty in mean, but this fact does not entail the same striking consequence as the same hypothetical property for each large N'.

verification.evidence: R-108450 (@8db2752f, fetched) is a finite-abelian-group countermodel. Constant a,b have every nonprincipal Fourier coefficient zero but cell energy |X||Y||A|^2|B|^2, which is unbounded under scaling. That is a Parseval/orthogonality fact. The Iwaniec-Sarnak zbMATH quote (0992.11037) is verbatim correct. The paper is a survey/announcement in Israel J. Math. 120 (2000) 155-177. R-108450 is not a reformulation of Bombieri-Vinogradov, which is a deep theorem about primes, and the draft's own notes call it a finite-group Parseval restatement. Also, Bombieri-Vinogradov is usually stated with x/phi(q) or li(x)/phi(q). The psi(x)/phi(q) form is the nonprincipal-part variant.

repo_statement: Proper theta-source quotient: L_{k,j}(1/2)>0 for large weight, which with the positive residue at s=1 forces real zeros in (1/2,1) and (0,1/2)
literature_result: Chowla-Selberg (1949, 1967) and Bateman-Grosswald (1964, p.367, Thm 3): for a positive definite binary quadratic form Q=ax^2+bxy+cy^2, the Epstein zeta Z_2(s,Q) has a real zero in (1/2,1) if k=sqrt|d|/(2a)>7.0556. The mechanism is the same: the constant term makes the central value positive at large height, and the positive residue at s=1 forces a sign change.
citation: S. Chowla & A. Selberg, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 35 (1949) 371-374 and J. Reine Angew. Math. 227 (1967) 86-110; P.T. Bateman & E. Grosswald, Acta Arith. 9 (1964) 365-373, Thm 3; statement read in P. Ribeiro & S. Yakubovich, arXiv:2112.10561, §1
notes: For a fixed admissible f, the Mellin transform of H(t)[f]=int_F y^k|f|^2 Theta_z(t)dmu is the Rankin-Selberg integral of y^k|f|^2 against the completed Eisenstein series pi^{-s}Gamma(s)Z_{Q_z}(s). The repository's object is therefore a weighted average of exactly the Epstein functions to which Chowla-Selberg applies, with large weight k playing the role of large height (y_eff ~ k/(4 pi j)). The quotient minimum over f at each t is a new-in-context twist. Possible consistency remark (my computation, with Zagier's Petersson-norm formula from memory): for a normalized Hecke eigenform, G[f]/A_1(k) ~ (k-1)L(1,sym^2 f)/(2 pi^2), so R_f -> 0 and the criterion never fires. That is consistent with GRH for sym^2.

verification.evidence: I read Ribeiro-Yakubovich arXiv:2112.10561 section 1. It cites Bateman-Grosswald [p.367, Thm 3]: for a general positive definite real quadratic form, Z_2(s,Q) has a real zero in (1/2,1) if k=sqrt|d|/(2a)>7.0556. zbMATH 0128.27004 confirms Acta Arith. 9 (1964) 365-373. Chowla-Selberg: PNAS 35 (1949) 371-374, and J. Reine Angew. Math. 227 (1967) 86-110 (authors listed as Selberg-Chowla). I fetched the repository source PROPER_THETA_SOURCE_REAL_ZERO_COROLLARY.md @9e898541: TQ1-TQ10 prove L(1/2)>0 via R=J/G_Q ~ sqrt(k/(4 pi j)), plus the positive residue at 1 and reflection. That is the same mechanism (constant-term positivity at large height plus a positive residue forces a real zero). Mellin of Theta_z(t)-1 gives pi^{-s}Gamma(s) sum'(|mz+n|^2/y)^{-s} = 2E*(z,s), so for each fixed f the source is a Rankin-Selberg/Eisenstein integral. The draft's y_eff ~ k/(4 pi j) reading is consistent with the y^k e^{-4 pi j y} weight. The eigenform consistency remark rests on the standard Petersson-norm formula (memory). With <f,f> = Gamma(k)L(1,sym^2 f)/(2^{2k-1}pi^{k+1}) I re-derived G[f]/A_1(k) = (k-1)L(1,sym^2 f)/(2 pi^2), so it is algebraically consistent but should be labelled unverified. Lagarias-Suzuki (missed prior art) is an even closer analogue.

repo_statement: T-108519: a certified complex off-line zero of the Epstein zeta Z_Q at z*=4341/50000+3731/2500 i, in Re s in [0.83,0.99]
literature_result: Davenport-Heilbronn (1936): for class number h(D)>1, E(s,Q) has infinitely many zeros in Re s>1. Voronin: for every 1/2<sigma1<sigma2<1 there are at least cT zeros in the strip with |Im s|<T. Lee (2012, Thm 1.3): the number of zeros in sigma1<Re s<sigma2, |Im s|<T is cT+o(T), with c>0 if sigma1<=1. Bombieri-Mueller computed sup Re rho for m^2+5n^2 and 2m^2+2mn+3n^2.
citation: Y. Lee, 'On the zeros of Epstein zeta functions', arXiv:1204.6297 (Forum Math. 2014), Thms 1.1-1.3 (restating Davenport-Heilbronn, J. London Math. Soc. 11 (1936); S.M. Voronin; Bombieri-Mueller); S. Gonek & Y. Lee, arXiv:1511.06824
notes: The literature hypotheses are integer coefficients and discriminant equal to a fundamental discriminant. For z*, Q is unimodular with rational coefficients; scaling to an integral form gives discriminant -4N^2, which is non-fundamental (an order in Q(i)). The classical theorems therefore do not literally cover z*, although the ring-class-character decomposition makes the same off-line behavior expected. The repository's contribution is an instance location, not the phenomenon, and the repository says so ('classical in spirit').

verification.evidence: I read Lee arXiv:1204.6297 in full text; zbMATH 1356.11022 gives Forum Math. 26 (2014) 1807-1836. Theorem 1.1 (Voronin) and Theorem 1.3 (cT+o(T) zeros in strips with 1/2<sigma1<sigma2; c>0 if sigma1<=1) both assume integer coefficients, discriminant equal to disc Q(sqrt D) (fundamental), and h>1. Theorem 1.2 is Bombieri-Mueller, Forum Math. 20 (2008) 359-385 (zbMATH 1217.11040). I checked the z* claim: Q_{z*} has discriminant -4, and its primitive integral rescaling has a=2.5e9, b=4.341e8, c=5586988681, gcd 1, discriminant -4N^2 with N=3.731e9. That is non-fundamental.
verification.correction: The JFM reviews of Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 I/II (J. London Math. Soc. 11, 181-185 and 307-312) state the hypothesis as integral a,b,c with h(d)>1 for d=b^2-4ac. They give no fundamental-discriminant restriction. So the sigma>1 phenomenon plausibly covers the integral rescaling of Q_{z*}. Only the strip theorems as stated by Lee (Voronin; Lee Thm 1.3) need a fundamental discriminant. 'The classical theorems do not literally cover z*' should be limited to the 1/2<sigma<1 strip results.

repo_statement: TWIST-EXCESS-RANK-L2: sum_d e_d^2 << |D_eps(X)|, or avg e_d^2 = o(1), for quadratic twists of a fixed GL2 form
literature_result: (i) Heath-Brown, Thm 3: assuming RH for all L_D, the weighted average analytic rank of quadratic twists is <= 3/2+o(1) in each root-number class. Thm 4: at least 1/4 of even-sign twists have rank 0 and at least 3/4 of odd-sign twists have rank 1. Thm 2 gives faster-than-exponential rank tails for the family of all curves. (ii) Katz-Sarnak: the Density Conjecture implies Goldfeld's conjecture (100% minimal rank). Gouvea-Mazur give >= X^{1/2} even-sign D with L(1/2,E x chi_D)=0, so e_d>0 infinitely often. (iii) Smith (2025): 50%/50% 2^infinity-Selmer corank 0/1 for every E/Q, so BSD implies Goldfeld's conjecture.
citation: D.R. Heath-Brown, 'The average analytic rank of elliptic curves', Duke Math. J. 122 (2004), arXiv:math/0305114, Thms 2-4; N. Katz & P. Sarnak, Bull. AMS 36 (1999) 1-26, §5; A. Smith, arXiv:2503.17619 (abstract); Perelli-Pomykala, Acta Arith. 80 (1997), zbMATH 0878.11022
notes: The o(1) target implies the analytic form of Goldfeld's conjecture (open unconditionally; it follows from BSD by Smith). A bounded second moment would follow under GRH from 2-level density / centered-moment methods (Rubinstein, Hughes-Miller arXiv:math/0507450 for related families). I verified only Heath-Brown's first-moment and proportion theorems for twists. Unconditional bounded average analytic rank for twist families is, to my knowledge, open; Perelli-Pomykala give only a 'nontrivial estimate' (abstract).

verification.evidence: I read Heath-Brown arXiv:math/0305114 in full text. Thm 2 (all curves, under RH): rank tail << (3R/2)^{-R/12}. Thm 3 (twists, RH for every L_D): weighted average rank <= 3/2+o(1) in each root-number class. Thm 4: at least 1/4 of even-sign twists have rank 0 and at least 3/4 of odd-sign twists have rank 1. Katz-Sarnak Bull. AMS 36 (1999) section 5 (full text, Williams mirror) states that the Density Conjecture with Kolyvagin gives Goldfeld's conjectures, and quotes Gouvea-Mazur as 'at least X^{1/2}' even-sign D with L(1/2,E x chi_D)=0. The Smith arXiv:2503.17619 abstract confirms 50%/50% 2^infinity-Selmer corank 0/1 for every E/Q, so BSD implies Goldfeld. Perelli-Pomykala, Acta Arith. 80 (1997) 149-163: zbMATH confirms a 'nontrivial estimate for the analytic rank'.
verification.correction: Gouvea-Mazur's own bound (JAMS 4 (1991); zbMATH 0725.11027) is >> X^{1/2-epsilon}, not X^{1/2}; Katz-Sarnak round it. The analytic vanishing is unconditional via Kolyvagin and Gross-Zagier once a point of infinite order and an even sign are produced. The claim that a bounded second moment of excess rank in quadratic-twist families follows under GRH is not backed by a cited theorem. Heath-Brown gives only the first moment for twists.

repo_statement: #740 architecture: a hypothetical off-line zeta zero propagated through a family statistic
literature_result: Deuring phenomenon (elementary version, Stopple): if zeta(rho)=0 with beta=Re rho>7/8 and |delta|>pi/100, then for every real primitive chi mod D (D = 0 mod 4, D>10^9), L(1,chi) > 1/(5400 U^{12(1-beta)} log^3 U), where U=|rho|D^{1/4}log D. A nontrivial bound holds for beta>5/6. Heilbronn's case split (GRH true: Hecke; GRH false: Deuring-Heilbronn) proved h(-d)->infinity.
citation: J. Stopple, 'Elementary Deuring-Heilbronn phenomenon', arXiv:1201.0713, Theorem (p.2); M. Deuring, Math. Z. 37 (1933); H. Heilbronn, Q. J. Math. 5 (1934); explicit version: Benli-Goel-Twiss-Zaman, arXiv:2410.06082 (PAMS 2026)
notes: This is the classical existing instance of 'one bad zeta zero -> family statement'. The propagated statement (lower bounds on L(1,chi), i.e. no Siegel zeros) is believed true. The propagation is therefore not a contradiction route: classically it is used to prove true theorems by case split.

verification.evidence: I read Stopple arXiv:1201.0713v3 in full text. Theorem: if beta>7/8 and |delta|>pi/100 (delta from log2*gamma mod 2pi), then for every real primitive chi mod D with D=0 mod 4 and D>10^9, L(1,chi) > 1/(5400 U^{12(1-beta)} log^3 U) with U=|rho|D^{1/4}log D, and a nontrivial bound holds for beta>5/6. This is quoted exactly. The arXiv abstract page of 2410.06082 (DOI 10.1090/proc/17450) gives the title 'Explicit Deuring-Heilbronn phenomenon for Dirichlet L-functions'.
verification.correction: Benli-Goel-Twiss-Zaman is not an explicit version of Stopple's statement. Their abstract assumes a Landau-Siegel zero and proves explicit zero repulsion for all Dirichlet L-functions mod q (the Heilbronn/Linnik direction). It bears on 'zeta zero gives a lower bound for L(1,chi)' only by contrapositive, through the principal character mod q, within its stated region. Recast the citation that way.

repo_statement: #740/#738: one member's zero structure controlling a whole family
literature_result: Goldfeld, Theorem 1: if L_E for an elliptic curve E/Q has a zero of order g at s=1 (old normalization), then L(1,chi) for all real primitive chi mod d (with (d,N)=1, d large) has an explicit effective lower bound. repo_statement: OPEN_CUTS §5: extracting an estimate for every member from a family statistic
literature_result: Iwaniec-Luo-Sarnak, §10, Corollary 10.4 (= Cor. 1.11). Assume Hypothesis S (bounds for sum_{p<=x, p=a(c)} e(2 sqrt p/c)), and that all zeros of L(s,f), f in H_k(1), are real or on Re s=1/2. Then L(s,f) != 0 for Re s > beta+eps (explicit beta<1) for all k >= k_0. The proof uses an extended-support 1-level density in which every term is nonnegative and drops all but one term. repo_statement: Principal-member individualization from a family proportion (charters #736/#740)
literature_result: Iwaniec-Sarnak: for the families H_k(1) (k <= K) and H_k(N), at least 1/2 - eps of the central values satisfy L(1/2,f) >= (log N)^{-2}. Any proportion c>1/2 would give L(1,chi_q) >= c_0(log q)^{-2}, i.e. no Landau-Siegel zeros.

Math. 120 (2000) 155-177, a survey/announcement) covers both families, H_k (k<=K) and H_k(N): positive lower bounds for at least half of the central values, with 'a slightly bigger frequency' needed to eliminate exceptional zeros. repo_statement: #740 'unconditional family upper bound' step
literature_result: Kowalski-Michel, Theorem 1.1: for q prime, sum_{f in S_2(q)^+} N(f,alpha,T) << T^A q^{3(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)}(log q)^{B+1} for 1/2<=alpha<=1. The family size is about q/12. The proof uses the Petersson formula and the DFI large sieve, following Perelli-Pomykala's twist approach.
citation: E. Kowalski & P. Michel, 'Sur les zéros des fonctions L automorphes', arXiv:math/9707238, Théorème 1.1, Corollaire 1.1, Théorème 1.2
notes: Consequence: in an essentially orthogonal family, no single point with Re > 1/2 can be a zero of more than |F|^{3(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)+eps} members. This is the contradiction step #740 needs, but it applies only to families with a large sieve. A family whose members all share zeta (e.g. L(s, f x f-bar) = zeta(s)L(s, Ad f)) is not orthogonal, which is R-108450's principal-mode obstruction in classical form.

verification.evidence: Kowalski-Michel arXiv:math/9707238, full text, 'Sur les zéros des fonctions L automorphes de grand niveau'. Théorème 1.1: for 1/2<=alpha<=1 and q prime, sum_{f in S_2(q)^+} N(f,alpha,T) << T^A q^{3(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)} (log q)^{B+1}. This uses (f,f) >> q/log q from [HL,GHL]. The introduction states that the approach follows Perelli-Pomykala; the DFI large sieve is cited. The 'no point is a common zero of more than |F|^{...}' consequence follows directly. The full title has 'de grand niveau', which the draft omits.

repo_statement: B-017: Hecke-scale reduction uses the standard sym^2 zero-free region without an exceptional zero
literature_result: Hoffstein-Lockhart: |rho(1)|^2 << log(lambda N+1) if L(s,Ad f) has no Siegel zero. The Goldfeld-Hoffstein-Lieman appendix gives an effective zero-free region and excludes exceptional zeros for adjoint L-functions of non-dihedral f.
citation: J. Hoffstein & P. Lockhart, Ann. of Math. 140 (1994) 161-176, appendix by D. Goldfeld, J. Hoffstein, D. Lieman, 177-181 (zbMATH 0814.11032)
notes: This is the named import B asks to authenticate. The repository should cite GHL for the zero-free region and match the GL(3) adjoint normalization (level one, holomorphic weight k).

verification.evidence: zbMATH 0814.11032: Hoffstein-Lockhart, Ann. of Math. 140 (1994) 161-176, with appendix by Goldfeld-Hoffstein-Lieman, 177-181. For Maass newforms on Gamma_0(N), |rho(1)|^2 <= c log(lambda N+1) provided L(s,F) (adjoint lift) has no Siegel zero. The appendix proves the same for all f that are not GL(1) lifts. The B-017 row in reviews/B/CLAIMS.tsv needs 'the standard symmetric-square zero-free region without exceptional zero' for level-one holomorphic f, with a zero-free gap c/log k for |Im rho|<=1.
verification.correction: 'repo_weaker' is the wrong relation label. Hoffstein-Lockhart/GHL partly supply the named import; they do not strengthen B-017. GHL excludes the real exceptional zero (non-dihedral forms). The complex part of the zero-free region near 1 comes from the standard GL(3) de la Vallée Poussin argument (e.g. Iwaniec-Kowalski ch. 5), which should be cited alongside. Hoffstein-Lockhart's main theorem is stated for Maass forms; the holomorphic weight-k normalization has to be matched separately. The evidence is now confirmed at zbMATH-review level.

repo_statement: B-031: the integral +q factor locus, the ghost (5,0,-10), and 'no isogeny statement from the polynomial criterion'
literature_result: Tate (1966): abelian varieties over F_q are isogenous iff they have the same Weil polynomial. Honda-Tate classifies isogeny classes. Howe-Nart-Ritzenthaler, Thm 1.2 with Tables 1-2, says exactly which Weil polynomials x^4+ax^3+bx^2+aqx+q^2 occur for genus-2 curves. Split classes (x^2-sx+q)(x^2-tx+q) fail iff a Table 1 row holds; simple classes fail iff a Table 2 row holds. The row a=0, b=-2q is excluded only for q=2,3.
citation: E. Howe, E. Nart, C. Ritzenthaler, 'Jacobians in isogeny classes of abelian surfaces over finite fields', arXiv:math/0607515 (Ann. Inst. Fourier 59 (2009)), Thm 1.2, Tables 1-2; J. Tate, Invent. Math. 2 (1966)
notes: Own check (script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riemann/e62aa4cb-6226-5e37-8f52-ea0fa055746f/scratchpad/fam/code/g2f5.py): exhaustive over F_5, exactly one monic squarefree quintic, f=x^5-x, has (N1,N2)=(6,6), i.e. L-numerator 1-10T^2+25T^4=(1-5T^2)^2. No sextic model does. So the ghost is realized inside the declared affine family. Since sqrt5 is a real Weil number, Honda-Tate makes this Jacobian a SIMPLE supersingular abelian surface over F_5 (it splits as E^2 over F_25), consistent with HNR Table 2. Isogeny statements over F_q follow from Tate's theorem once the Weil polynomial is known. Principal polarization and Jacobian membership are fully answered by HNR.

verification.evidence: I read HNR arXiv:math/0607515 in full text. Theorem 1.2 and Tables 1-2: the Table 2 row 'p-rank 0, q=2 or q=3: a=0 and b=-2q' is the only exclusion for (0,-2q), so for q=5 the simple class A_(0,-10) contains a Jacobian; it is constructed explicitly on pp.33-34. Independent replay (my own script, separate from the draft's): there are 2500 = q^5-q^4 monic squarefree quintics over F_5, and exactly one, x^5-x, has (N1,N2)=(6,6), i.e. L=1-10T^2+25T^4=(1-5T^2)^2. By hand: x^5-x vanishes on F_5, and over F_25 its nonzero values are nonsquare trace-zero elements. Over Z, (1-5T^2)^2 is not of the form (1-rT+5T^2)(1-sT+5T^2), since that would need r^2=20. Honda-Tate with real Weil number sqrt5 gives a simple supersingular surface.
verification.correction: 'Principal polarization ... fully answered by HNR' overstates it. HNR decide whether an isogeny class contains a Jacobian. Whether it contains a principally polarized surface is a separate classification (Howe-Maisner-Nart-Ritzenthaler, 2008, from memory). Monodromy is not addressed. Otherwise the realization claim survives an independent check.

repo_statement: B-007/B-008/B-039: generic numerator degree prod d - max d, and the backward deficit determining denominator-minus-numerator degree
literature_result: Sum_r h_r(A)h_r(B)h_r(C)T^r is the torus-equivariant Hilbert series of the Segre product of polynomial rings. By Stanley reciprocity, the degree of the Hilbert series as a rational function equals the a-invariant, and Goto-Watanabe compute a(Segre product of k[x_1..x_{d_i}]) = -max d_i. Non-equivariant check: for P^2 x P^1 the series is (1+2T)/(1-T)^4, with degree difference -3.
citation: R. Stanley, 'Hilbert functions of graded algebras', Adv. Math. 28 (1978); S. Goto & K. Watanabe, 'On graded rings I', J. Math. Soc. Japan 30 (1978); E. Rubei, arXiv:math/0404417 (already imported by the repository)
notes: The a-invariant explanation matches both the generic degree law and the fixed backward deficit d for one alphabet. A specialization can drop the leading numerator coefficient (B's (2,3,5),(1,-1),(1) example) without contradicting this. I did not verify exact theorem numbers.

verification.evidence: zbMATH confirms Stanley, Adv. Math. 28 (1978) 57-83 and Goto-Watanabe, J. Math. Soc. Japan 30 (1978) 179-213. Series examples: P^2xP^1 gives (1+2T)/(1-T)^4 (coefficients 1,6,18,40 = binom(d+2,2)(d+1)), degree -3 = -max(3,2). P^1xP^1xP^1 gives (1+4T+T^2)/(1-T)^4, degree -2. P^2xP^2 gives (1+4T+T^2)/(1-T)^5, degree -3. These match a(Segre) = -max d_i via the canonical module omega_A # omega_B. For one alphabet of size n, the m-fold Segre power has a=-n, matching the backward deficit n (h_{-1}=...=h_{-(n-1)}=0, h_{-n}=(-1)^{n-1}/det A) by Stanley reciprocity.
verification.correction: Theorem numbers are unverified (Goto-Watanabe section 4.2 is believed to compute a(R#S)). Degree of the Hilbert series = a-invariant holds for the Z-graded series of a Cohen-Macaulay ring. The torus-equivariant generic degree law needs the fine-graded or generic-specialization argument, which the repository's alternant proof supplies. Treat this as an explanatory correspondence, not an import that proves B-007/B-008.

repo_statement: factor67_lorenz / direct_main OPEN_RH_EQUIVALENT critical subpower one-sided (negative-mass) estimates for fixed Mobius-weighted detectors, and their Dirichlet-family lift
literature_result: Classical: RH is equivalent to M(x) << x^{1/2+eps} (Littlewood 1912). Landau's theorem on Dirichlet integrals with nonnegative integrand shows that a one-sided bound M(x) >= -C x^{theta} already forces zeta != 0 for Re s>theta. The same holds for L(s,chi) and Mertens sums twisted by chi.
citation: Montgomery-Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, §15.1 (Landau's oscillation theorem); Titchmarsh, Theory of the Riemann Zeta-Function, §14.25
notes: This shows why the critical negative-mass gates are RH-equivalent: they are smoothed one-sided Mertens bounds. The family lift turns them into GRH-type statements, member by member.

verification.evidence: research/integrated/direct_main/taylor/README.md: TAYLOR_CRITICAL is 'subpower negative mass or the critical upper-envelope estimate for the fixed Taylor scalar'. factor67_lorenz/README.md: GPC67/CPSL67 is a 'critical subpower signed Type-II/Lorenz boundary'. For these two, Landau's theorem on Dirichlet integrals with nonnegative integrand (zeta has no real zeros in (0,1)) and Littlewood's M(x)<<x^{1/2+epsilon} criterion are apt classical analogues. Montgomery-Vaughan section 15.1 and Titchmarsh section 14.25 are cited from memory.
verification.correction: (1) cauchy_jordan/README.md: T91005 is 'the coefficient-one normalized sixteenfold Cauchy recurrence', and CJHI is 'a lossless completed Cauchy-Jordan first-chaos source-to-Hardy intertwiner'. Neither is a one-sided Mertens-type bound, so the relation does not extend to them. The repo_statement row that lumps all four as 'critical subpower signed estimates' is itself inaccurate. (2) 'The same holds for L(s,chi)' is false as stated. A one-sided bound M(x,chi) >= -Cx^theta for real chi forces L!=0 for Re s>theta only if L(sigma,chi) has no real zeros in (theta,1), which would exclude Siegel zeros and is unknown. For complex chi a one-sided bound is not meaningful. So 'GRH member by member' does not follow from one-sided family lifts.

repo_statement: #736/#741: family second and fourth moments of reciprocal-L detectors
literature_result: CFKRS give a recipe for all main terms of integral moments of L-functions in unitary, orthogonal and symplectic families. Conrey-Farmer-Zirnbauer extend it to averages of ratios prod L/prod L, which include reciprocal L-functions.
citation: J.B. Conrey, D.W. Farmer, J.P. Keating, M.O. Rubinstein, N.C. Snaith, arXiv:math/0206018 (Proc. LMS 91 (2005)); Conrey-Farmer-Zirnbauer, arXiv:0711.0718
notes: The repository's compact-kernel family moments are finite sums, exactly computable by orthogonality without GRH. Ratios-conjecture predictions concern 1/L near or on the critical line and are conjectural or GRH-conditioned. Neither gives principal extraction.

verification.evidence: arXiv abstract pages confirm math/0206018 (Conrey, Farmer, Keating, Rubinstein, Snaith, 'Integral moments of L-functions') and 0711.0718 (Conrey, Farmer, Zirnbauer, 'Autocorrelation of ratios of L-functions'). The content (a recipe for moment main terms; a ratios conjecture covering reciprocal L-functions) is standard. 'partial_overlap' and the note that compact-kernel finite family moments are exact by orthogonality without GRH are accurate.

obstruction: A functional equation without an Euler product does not imply RH: Davenport-Heilbronn functions, Epstein zetas with class number >1, and general linear combinations have off-line zeros, about T of them in every strip 1/2<sigma1<sigma2<1.
citation: Davenport-Heilbronn, J. London Math. Soc. 11 (1936); Voronin; Y. Lee arXiv:1204.6297 Thms 1.1-1.3; Saias-Weingartner arXiv:0807.0783
how_it_constrains: Any 'Riemann structure' or generalized object (#763/#764) built only from completion, functional equation, positivity of a theta-type source and Mellin observation cannot force RH. The repository's theta-quotient real zeros and Epstein zeros are instances. Multiplicativity (Euler product) has to be a load-bearing input in any RH-facing transfer.

verification.evidence: Lee Thms 1.1 and 1.3, Saias-Weingartner abstract, and the Davenport-Heilbronn JFM reviews were all read; they support off-line zeros for Epstein zetas with h>1 and for periodic-coefficient series not of the form P(s)L_chi(s). The repository's own theta-corollary (PROPER_THETA_SOURCE_REAL_ZERO_COROLLARY section 5) concludes that positive source, reflection and endpoint poles 'do not force all completed zeros to the critical line'. Epstein zetas are Mellin transforms of positive theta series, which supports the how_it_constrains conclusion.
verification.correction: 'general linear combinations' is too broad. Positive-density off-line zero theorems need specific hypotheses: periodic coefficients not of the form P(s)L_chi (Saias-Weingartner), fundamental discriminant and h>1 (Voronin/Lee), or the conditions of Kaczorowski-Kulas/Bombieri-Ghosh. Also note the counter-direction: some positive Eisenstein integrals do satisfy RH (Lagarias-Suzuki 2006). So positivity plus a functional equation is neither sufficient nor automatically insufficient.

obstruction: Statistical or 'almost all' RH is compatible with infinitely many off-line zeros: Bombieri-Hejhal give 100% of zeros simple and on the line for linear combinations (under GRH+H0), while Voronin, Lee and Saias-Weingartner give about T off-line zeros.
citation: Bombieri-Hejhal, Duke 80 (1995) 821-862 (zbMATH 0853.11074); Perelli survey Thm 7.4
how_it_constrains: Family or density-one conclusions cannot certify an individual member. This matches the #740 rejection rule 'replaces an individual conclusion by a density-one statement'.

verification.evidence: zbMATH 0853.11074: Bombieri-Hejhal show N_0(T) ~ N(T) ~ CT log T for linear combinations under suitable hypotheses. Lee and Saias-Weingartner (read) give about T off-line zeros. The #740 charter (fetched via the GitHub API) lists 'replaces an individual conclusion by a density-one statement' as an automatic rejection.
verification.correction: The Bombieri-Hejhal phenomenon is about the proportion of zeros of one function, not density one over family members. It supports the #740 rule only by analogy, and should be labelled so. The exact Bombieri-Hejhal hypotheses (GRH plus spacing/orthogonality) were not checked.

obstruction: Large sieve / orthogonality: the family second moment is dominated by its diagonal, so isolating the principal member by positivity costs a factor equal to the family size and gives only the trivial bound. Bombieri-Vinogradov ('GRH on average') never touches the principal character, which needs the zeta zero-free region.
citation: Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory, Chs. 27-28; Iwaniec-Kowalski, Ch. 7 and Thm 17.1
how_it_constrains: Any family estimate proved by orthogonality (e.g. R-106071.2) gives, for the principal channel L(s,chi_0)=zeta(s)(1-ell^{-s}), at most what was put in. A subpower principal-member extraction is RH-strength (charter #736 outcome 3).

verification.evidence: From memory only: Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory, chapters 27 (large sieve) and 28 (Bombieri's theorem); Iwaniec-Kowalski chapter 7 and Theorem 17.1 (believed to be Bombieri-Vinogradov). L-106000.8 (fetched) does make the principal member zeta(s)(1-ell^{-s}) times the detector factors, so subpower principal extraction gives a zeta statement (charter #736 outcome 3, verified in the issue text).
verification.correction: 'Isolating the principal member by positivity costs a factor equal to the family size and gives only the trivial bound' is a heuristic, not a theorem. Bombieri-Vinogradov's handling of small moduli uses Siegel-Walfisz for all characters, and the principal term uses PNT; it is not literally 'never touches'. Label this memory-based.

obstruction: Threshold barrier: family nonvanishing is proved at 1/2-eps, but 1/2+eps is needed to individualize (exclude Landau-Siegel zeros). A mean over the level aspect does not give the per-level consequence.
citation: Iwaniec-Sarnak, Israel J. Math. 120 (2000) (zbMATH 0992.11037); Katz-Sarnak Bull. AMS 36 (1999) eq. (68)
how_it_constrains: Even successful family-to-member mechanisms sit exactly at a critical exponent, as the repository's critical-versus-supercritical (SHARP) dichotomy does. Expect the principal extraction to fail precisely at the critical scale.

verification.evidence: The zbMATH review of Iwaniec-Sarnak ('in the N-aspect, the percentage exceeds fifty in mean, but this fact does not entail the same striking consequence as the same hypothetical property for each large N') and Katz-Sarnak eq. (68) (p.23) both verified. The analogy to the repository's critical-versus-supercritical boundary is the draft's interpretation and is reasonable.

obstruction: 1-level density positivity needs GRH or a 'real-or-on-line' hypothesis: a complex off-line zero contributes phi((beta-1/2+i gamma)...) of indefinite sign to a nonnegative test function.
citation: Iwaniec-Luo-Sarnak, Publ. IHES 91 (2000), §1 (GRH assumption, p.57) and §10 (Cor 10.4 assumes zeros real or on the line)
how_it_constrains: In #740 candidate C ('amplified positive quadratic form'), positivity of the off-line contribution has to be proved, not assumed. Otherwise the argument assumes the conclusion for nonprincipal members, which #740 lists as an automatic rejection.

verification.evidence: ILS pp.56-57: 'Unless otherwise stated we assume that the Riemann hypothesis holds for each L(s,f) with f in F and for all Dirichlet L-functions'. Section 10, pp.114-115: the real-or-on-line assumption 'ensures that all terms of the sum (10.21) are real and non-negative'. For phi-hat >= 0, a real off-line zero gives phi(iy) >= 0, but a complex off-line zero gives phi at a complex argument with no sign control. The constraint on #740 candidate C follows.

obstruction: Deuring-Heilbronn: the natural propagation of a hypothetical bad zero through a family is repulsive. It strengthens nonvanishing (lower bounds for L(1,chi)) for the other members instead of producing forbidden mass.
citation: J. Stopple arXiv:1201.0713 (Theorem); Benli-Goel-Twiss-Zaman arXiv:2410.06082; Heilbronn 1934
how_it_constrains: #740's 'one bad zeta zero -> family statistic -> contradiction' must target a statistic for which the propagated effect is provably forbidden. The classical propagation leads to true statements (Heilbronn's class number theorem), not contradictions.

verification.evidence: Stopple's theorem (verified) is a 'bad zeta zero implies a lower bound for L(1,chi)' statement, i.e. a true, non-contradictory conclusion. Katz-Sarnak and Heilbronn's case split are classical.
verification.correction: As in PA10, Benli-Goel-Twiss-Zaman is Siegel-zero-driven zero repulsion (explicit, uniform in the strip). It supports 'repulsive' propagation only by contrapositive. The classical argument that propagation yields true theorems is sound.

obstruction: Density theorems require essential orthogonality: Kowalski-Michel/Montgomery-type bounds sum_f N(f,alpha,T) << |F|^{c(1-alpha)} hold for families with a large sieve. Families whose members share zeta as a factor (Rankin-Selberg L(f x f-bar)=zeta L(Ad f)) carry a common principal component and admit no such bound.
citation: Kowalski-Michel arXiv:math/9707238 Thm 1.1 (verified); the non-orthogonality remark is my synthesis
how_it_constrains: Propagating a zeta zero to many members of an ORTHOGONAL family, enough to contradict a density theorem, is exactly what orthogonality prevents. This is R-108450's principal-mode firewall in classical language.

verification.evidence: Kowalski-Michel Théorème 1.1 verified in full text: sum_f N(f,alpha,T) << T^A q^{3(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)} (log q)^{B+1}, for q prime and S_2(q)^+. The non-orthogonality remark is the draft's own synthesis.
verification.correction: 'Families whose members share zeta ... admit no such bound' should read 'admit no unconditional proof of such a bound without RH-type input for zeta'. Under RH the shared factor contributes no zeros with Re>1/2, so the bound is not false, only unprovable by orthogonality alone.

obstruction: Selberg-class degree rigidity: S_1 is {zeta, L(s+i theta,chi)}, and S^#_d is empty for 0<d<1 and for 1<d<2.
citation: Kaczorowski-Perelli, Acta Math. 182 (1999); Ann. of Math. 173 (2011) 1397-1441; Perelli survey Thms 6.3-6.4
how_it_constrains: Generalized L-object deformations (#764) cannot interpolate degree within Selberg-type axioms below 2. Continuous families must leave the axiom package, e.g. by losing the Euler product, and then OB01 applies.

verification.evidence: zbMATH 1235.11085 (Annals 2011, S^#_d empty for 1<d<2) and the Perelli part II summary (classification for 1<=d<2) both verified. S_1 = {zeta, L(s+i theta,chi)} and emptiness for 0<d<1 are standard (Kaczorowski-Perelli, Acta Math. 182 (1999)). The survey's theorem numbers are unverified.

obstruction: Over function fields, RH for every member and family equidistribution come from cohomology and monodromy (Deligne Weil I, Thm 3.2: rational local factors, symplectic big monodromy, positivity of 2k-th tensor powers, a radius-of-convergence lemma). Katz-Sarnak equidistribution needs q->infinity first.
citation: P. Deligne, 'La conjecture de Weil I', Publ. IHES 43 (1974) 273-307, Thm 3.2 and Lemmas 3.3-3.6 ('catalysé par la lecture de Rankin'); Katz-Sarnak Bull. AMS 36 §3-4
how_it_constrains: The function-field mirror (#737) identifies zeros with local Frobenius eigenvalues on finite-dimensional cohomology. The number-field analogue of the same Rankin-squaring argument controls Satake parameters (Ramanujan-type), not zeros of zeta. 'Purity transfers to principal extraction' therefore has no known mechanism over Q.

verification.evidence: Numdam PMIHES_1974__43__273_0, full text. Section 3: 'Le résultat de ce paragraphe a été catalysé par la lecture de Rankin [3]'. Théorème (3.2), Lemmes (3.3)-(3.6) (tensor power, rationality and positivity of local factors, convergence lemmas) are at the stated locations. Katz-Sarnak (41)-(42) confirm that q->infinity is taken first. The Ramanujan-versus-zeros interpretation is the draft's own synthesis.

obstruction: For quadratic twists, the minimalist target avg e_d^2=o(1) implies the analytic Goldfeld conjecture (open). Gouvea-Mazur give >= X^{1/2} even-sign twists with a central zero, so e_d>=2 infinitely often.
citation: Katz-Sarnak Bull. AMS 36 §5; Smith arXiv:2503.17619; Heath-Brown arXiv:math/0305114
how_it_constrains: TWIST-EXCESS-RANK-L2 in its o(1) form is at least as hard as a named open conjecture. The bounded form is known only under GRH, through explicit-formula moment methods.

verification.evidence: Verified in the sources: Katz-Sarnak section 5 (Density Conjecture plus Kolyvagin give Goldfeld); the Smith abstract (BSD implies Goldfeld); Heath-Brown Thms 3-4 (GRH conditional). If e_d is a nonnegative integer, avg e_d^2 = o(1) forces 100% minimal analytic rank, i.e. the analytic Goldfeld conjecture. For even sign, e_d=r_d, so the Gouvea-Mazur twists give e_d>=2.
verification.correction: Gouvea-Mazur count is >> X^{1/2-epsilon} (zbMATH 0725.11027), not X^{1/2}. 'The bounded form is known only under GRH' is unsupported: Heath-Brown proves only the first moment (<=3/2) under GRH for twists, and no theorem bounding the second moment of excess rank in quadratic-twist families was cited or verified. Say 'expected to follow under GRH from n-level density methods; not verified'.

tool: Explicit conductor-uniform Weil majorant for complex powers of L(T,chi): |[T^n]L(T,chi)^z| <= q^{n/2} binom(n+Am,n) for |z|<=A, deg(modulus)=m
citation: Afshar-Porritt arXiv:1709.01963, Prop. 3.1 and Thm 2
target_gap: B-027 hold: uniform conductor dependence of L-106213 (stopped rough shells, growing conductors)
precise_next_step: (1) Replace C_{chi,q}(n+1)^{r/2} at tower level m=1 by the explicit binom(n+m/2-3/2,n)q^{n/2}. (2) Bound the levels k>=2 by the majorant prod_k(1-sqrt(q)|u|^k)^{-|gamma_k| deg l}, plus the explicit (1-qu^2)^{-1/8} principal factor for quadratic chi, to get C(q)^{deg l}. (3) Write the U-rough stopped shell as the complete tower times the finite correction prod_{deg P<U}(1-chi(P)u^{deg P}/2)^{-1}, and bound that correction on |u|=q^{-1/2} (about exp(O(q^{U/2}/U))). This states the admissible (U, deg l, n) range explicitly.
risk: The finite rough-correction factor may be exponentially large unless U <= (2-eps)log_q n. That would show the stopped-shell transfer is affordable only for very small U. In any case it says nothing about the number-field principal member.

tool: Deligne's Rankin-squaring / tensor-power argument: positive-coefficient local factors of 2k-th tensor powers + exact abscissa from invariant theory + Landau-type radius-of-convergence lemma; the loss (family size) enters with exponent 1/(2k)

If so, the existing Mellin-Landau consumer (CURRENT_RESULTS §3, MATHEMATICS.md §1) can play Lemmas 3.5-3.6, and the family-size loss disappears as k -> infinity.

Compute the sign of the contribution of an off-line zero beta+i gamma, uniformly in beta. Identify the smallest extra hypothesis that keeps it nonnegative; this is the analogue of ILS's 'real-or-on-line' assumption.
