repo_statement: finite-robin-foundations.md sections 2-3: H(n)<=n, I(H(n))>=I(n), and every violator n>5040 yields a canonical violator H(n)>5040 (equivalence of existence of violators in all integers vs Hardy-Ramanujan canonical integers).
literature_result: CLMS section 5 'Reduction to Hardy-Ramanujan integers' uses the same object and name. For an exponent pattern e, m(e)=prod p_i^{e_i} is the least integer with that pattern (Lemma 9: max of sigma(n)/n over the pattern is attained at m(e)). Lemma 8 is the swap: for q>p and f>e, sigma(p^f q^e)/(p^f q^e) > sigma(p^e q^f)/(p^e q^f), via Lemma 7. Lemma 10(1): if sigma(n)/n >= e^g loglog n then m(e) satisfies the same. Proposition 1: if Robin holds for all HR integers in [5041,x], it holds for all integers in [5041,x]. HR integers <= x number exp((1+o(1)) 2pi sqrt(log x/(3 loglog x))) (Hardy-Ramanujan 1917).
citation: Y.-J. Choie, N. Lichiardopol, P. Moree, P. Sole, 'On Robin's criterion for the Riemann hypothesis', J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 19 (2007) (journal-ref on arXiv v2: 351-366); arXiv:math/0604314v2, Section 5, Proposition 1, Lemmas 7-10.
notes: Same map (m(e)=H(n)), same Hardy-Ramanujan name, same 5040 threshold, nonstrict violation convention. Lemma 10(1) is the repo's pointwise transfer. In the arXiv text, the Proposition 1 proof only invokes Lemma 10(2). It does not explicitly treat an n>=5041 whose minimal representative m(e)<=5040 is itself one of the 5040-or-below exceptions. The repo's 5583-threshold barrier closes exactly that case. Alternatively, such an n must share 5040's pattern (4,2,1,1), and every n != 5040 with that pattern has I(n) <= I(7920) ~ 3.66 < e^g loglog5041 ~ 3.817. This is a presentational gap, not an error in the statement. Recommend the repo cite this as the source of sections 2-3.

verification.evidence: I read arXiv:math/0604314v2 section 5 in full. The text matches the draft exactly: HR integers are defined as prod p_i^{e_i} with e_1>=...>=e_s>=0; Proposition 1 is stated as a range result for [5041,x]; the HR count is exp((1+o(1))2pi sqrt(log x/(3 loglog x))); Lemma 7 is the strictly decreasing (1-x^-e)/(1-x^-f); Lemma 8 is the swap; Lemma 9 is the max over a pattern attained at m(e); Lemma 10(1) and (2) are as stated. The one-line proof of Proposition 1 invokes only Lemma 10(2), so the gap the draft flags is real. I checked the draft's alternative closure exactly. Only m=5040 among m<=5040 has I(m)>=e^g loglog5041=3.81692. Among pattern-(4,2,1,1) integers other than 5040, the largest I is I(7920)=3.66364, followed by 8400 (3.66095). The repo files cite none of this literature (grep found no Choie, Akbary, Vojak, Morrill or Briggs).
verification.correction: Citation: the article is J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 19 (2007), no. 2, 357-372; numdam JTNB_2007__19_2_357_0 and zbMATH 1163.11059 agree. The arXiv journal-ref '351-366' is wrong. Qualify the gap note: CLMS do treat the m(e)<=5040 case explicitly in the proof of their Theorem 5 (5-free case: omega<=5, then a MAPLE check). It is omitted only from the proof of Proposition 1. Also, Proposition 1 is a range statement for every x. The repo's theorem is its x->infinity union plus the pointwise transfer n->H(n) (CLMS Lemma 10(1)). 'Identical' is acceptable for this mathematical content.

repo_statement: Sections 2-3 (same transform, even the same letter H) and the reduction 'Robin for all canonical h>5040 implies Robin for all n>5040'.
literature_result: Theorem 2.3 (Multiplicity Permutation): swapping exponents a<b of primes p<q decreases n and increases s(n)=sigma(n)/n. Vojak defines A(n) (sort exponents) and H(n) (first primes, sorted exponents), proves H(n)<=n and s(H(n))>=s(n), and states Theorem 2.4: if Robin holds for all Hardy-Ramanujan numbers >5040, it holds for all integers >5040.
citation: R. Vojak, 'On numbers satisfying Robin's inequality, properties of the next counterexample and improved specific bounds', arXiv:2005.09307v1 (2020; zbMATH lists it as a preprint), Theorems 2.3 and 2.4.
notes: The statement is the contrapositive of the repo's (1)=>(2). The printed proof ('If H(n) satisfies Robin's inequality, so does n') likewise leaves the case H(n)<=5040 implicit. The repo's barrier makes it explicit. The paper appears to be unrefereed.

verification.evidence: I read arXiv:2005.09307v1 in full. Theorem 2.3 (Multiplicity Permutation) is as described, for exponents a,b>=1 of prime divisors p<q. Equations (2)-(3) define A(n) and H(n) with the same letter H. The text proves H(n)<=A(n)<=n and s(H(n))>=s(A(n))>=s(n). Theorem 2.4: if Robin holds for all HR numbers >5040, it holds for all integers >5040. The printed argument ('If H(n) satisfies Robin's inequality, so does n') leaves H(n)<=5040 implicit. Vojak defines 'satisfies Robin' to include n>=5041, so the case is not covered. zbMATH lists the paper only as arXiv:2005.09307, with no journal version.

repo_statement: Section 3: existence of a canonical (Hardy-Ramanujan) violator whenever a violator exists.
literature_result: Theorem 3: if there is any counterexample to Robin's inequality, the least one is superabundant. Proof: no counterexample exists in 5040<n<=10080 (known computation, and 10080 is SA). For a least counterexample n>10080 that is not SA, take k with 10080<=k<n and sigma(k)/k>=sigma(n)/n; k is then a smaller counterexample. SA numbers have nonincreasing exponents on consecutive primes (Alaoglu-Erdos 1944, Theorem 1), so SA is a subset of HR.
citation: A. Akbary, Z. Friggstad, 'Superabundant numbers and the Riemann hypothesis', Amer. Math. Monthly 116 (2009) 273-275, Theorem 3 (author copy www.cs.uleth.ca/~akbary/07-0300.pdf; zbMATH 1229.11116).
notes: As an existence statement the repo's reduction is implied by AF plus Alaoglu-Erdos, with SA a much thinner subset of HR. AF's finite barrier [5041,10080] plays the same role as the repo's [5041,5582]. The repo's pointwise statement (every violator n gives the violator H(n)) is not implied by AF, which concerns only the least violator.

verification.evidence: I read the author copy (cs.uleth.ca/~akbary/07-0300.pdf) in full. Theorem 3 and its proof are exactly as described: no counterexample in 5040<n<=10080, 10080 is SA, and the replacement-k argument. The paper lists the first 20 SA numbers, which include 5040 and 10080. Crossref gives Amer. Math. Monthly 116(3) (2009) 273-275, DOI 10.1080/00029890.2009.11920937, and zbMATH gives 1229.11116. The SA subset of HR (via nonincreasing exponents) is confirmed by CNS 2012 eq. (5). The 'repo_weaker' relation holds for the existence statement, and the draft correctly notes that AF does not imply the repo's pointwise transfer.

repo_statement: Section 3 boundary: 'Canonical does not mean colossally abundant'; the canonical search domain is complete but infinite.
literature_result: Robin 1984, Proposition 1 of Section 3: if 3<=N<=n<=N' with N,N' consecutive colossally abundant numbers, then G(n)=sigma(n)/(n loglog n) <= max(G(N),G(N')). Hence if any Robin counterexample exists, a CA counterexample exists. The proof is elementary: log I is bounded by a linear function of log n via the CA inequality with the common parameter eps, and -log(log t) is convex. Robin also checked G(N)<e^g numerically for all 5041<N<55440 and for every CA N>=55440 with P+(N)<20000.
citation: G. Robin, 'Grandes valeurs de la fonction somme des diviseurs et hypothese de Riemann', J. Math. Pures Appl. (9) 63 (1984) 187-213 (zbMATH 0516.10036), Section 3, Proposition 1. Restated in Nazardonyavi-Yakubovich arXiv:1211.2147 (eq. 4.23), Lagarias arXiv:math/0008177 section 2, Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944 section 1.
notes: CA numbers form a one-parameter family; the number <= x is about log x/loglog x. HR integers grow like exp(c sqrt(log x/loglog x)). As a reduction for finite certification, the CA route is exponentially more efficient than canonical-tree traversal. The original JMPA text was not accessible; the statement is consistent across three independent secondary sources.

verification.evidence: Robin's JMPA original was not accessible to me either. Three secondary sources agree with the draft. Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944 (lines 183-189): N'<n<N'' implies G(n)<=max(G(N'),G(N'')), with a numerical check of G(N)<e^g for 5041<N<55440 and for CA N>=55440 with P+(N)<20000. Nazardonyavi-Yakubovich arXiv:1211.2147 states (4.23) as Robin [26] Proposition 1. Lagarias arXiv:math/0008177 cites '[18, Proposition 1 of Section 3]'. The draft's convexity sketch is mathematically sound: with a common parameter eps, log I(n) <= const + eps log n, and -log log u is convex. I did not confirm that this is Robin's own proof.
verification.correction: 'Hence if any Robin counterexample exists, a CA counterexample exists' needs the same boundary care the draft demands of CLMS. For 5040<n<55440 the bracketing CA pair is (5040,55440), and G(5040)>e^g, so the interpolation gives no information there. Robin's numerical check to 55440 is what closes this case. State the result as an existence-only (not pointwise) reduction, and keep evidence_level at secondary_source.

repo_statement: Finite barrier: no Robin violation in [5041,5582], with I(5040)=403/105 the unique maximum on [1,5040].
literature_result: Robin 1984 checked all integers 5041<N<55440 numerically (per Nicolas-Sondow). Akbary-Friggstad cite no counterexample in 5040<n<=10080. Vojak Theorem 3.5 covers none in 5041<n<=116144. Briggs 2006 checked CA numbers up to 10^(10^10). Morrill-Platt Theorem 13 proves Robin's inequality for all 5040<n<=10^(10^13.11485) by re-implementing Briggs's CA algorithm in 100-bit interval arithmetic, using Robin's CA interpolation. The unique-maximum fact is equivalent to 5040 being superabundant (OEIS A004394; it is in AF's list of the first 20 SA numbers).
citation: Morrill & Platt, 'Robin's inequality for 20-free integers', Integers 21 (2021) A28 (arXiv:1809.10813v4), Theorem 13 and Corollary 14. Briggs, 'Abundant numbers and the Riemann hypothesis', Experiment. Math. 15 (2006) 251-256 (zbMATH 1149.11041). Nicolas-Sondow, Contemp. Math. 627 (2014) 145-156 (arXiv:1211.6944). Akbary-Friggstad 2009, proof of Theorem 3.
notes: Range comparison is fulltext_read for Morrill-Platt and AF. Robin's 55440 check is secondary (Nicolas-Sondow). Briggs is secondary: the original expmath.org link is now a spam domain and the Project Euclid PDF was not retrievable. The repo's value is a self-contained exact/directed certificate of a small fragment, plus the exact 5582/5583 threshold. I reproduced the maxima with exact rationals and the thresholds in double precision (3.838090 < 3.838095 < 3.838127); this was not directed arithmetic.

verification.evidence: I read Morrill-Platt arXiv:1809.10813v4. Theorem 13 is Robin for all 5040<n<=10^(10^13.11485). Its proof implemented Briggs's algorithm with 100-bit extended precision and interval arithmetic, and the final checked n has the stated primorial form. Corollary 14 is as stated. zbMATH 1468.11205 gives Integers 21 (2021) A28. The AF and Nicolas-Sondow range statements are confirmed. The expmath.org Briggs URL is now a casino spam page, so I could not check Briggs either. I recomputed with exact rationals: the unique max on [1,5040] is 403/105 at 5040, and on [5041,5582] it is 224/65 at 5460. 50-digit mpmath interval evaluation gives e^g loglog n minus the constant as +0.37076 (n=5041), -5.5149e-6 (n=5582) and +3.1466e-5 (n=5583). This is not a fully directed certificate, because Euler's constant entered as a point value. The unique maximum on [1,5040] is by definition the statement that 5040 is SA.
verification.correction: Morrill-Platt never mention Robin's CA interpolation. They say only that the proof 'rests on Briggs' work on the colossally abundant numbers'. The use of interpolation is an inference through Briggs and should be labelled as such. Vojak's 5041<n<=116144 claim appears in the proof of Theorem 3.5 ('Numerical computations confirm'). It is not the statement of that theorem, which concerns omega(n)<=4.

repo_statement: Section 2 proof: G(t)=F_b(t)/F_a(t) is increasing on t>0 for b>a (exponent-inversion removal); sorted exponents on consecutive primes maximize I for a given exponent multiset.
literature_result: Alaoglu-Erdos 1944 Theorem 1: a superabundant n = 2^{k2} 3^{k3} ... p^{kp} has k2>=k3>=...>=kp, with kp=1 except n=4,36. Ramanujan 1915 proves the analogous monotonicity for highly composite numbers. CLMS Lemma 7: (1-x^-e)/(1-x^-f) is strictly decreasing on (1,inf) for e>f>0, which is the same function as the repo's G evaluated at t=1/x.
citation: L. Alaoglu, P. Erdos, 'On highly composite and similar numbers', Trans. AMS 56 (1944) 448-469 (zbMATH 0061.07903), Theorem 1. S. Ramanujan, 'Highly composite numbers', Proc. LMS (2) 14 (1915) 347-409. CLMS 2007, Lemmas 7-8.
notes: CLMS Lemmas 7-8 were fulltext_read and match the repo's lemma exactly. The Alaoglu-Erdos PDF at ams.org was blocked by a bot check; Theorem 1 is quoted from Caveney-Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1112.6010 eq. (5) and Akbary-Friggstad.

verification.evidence: CLMS Lemmas 7-9 were read in full. Lemma 7 is (1-x^-e)/(1-x^-f) strictly decreasing on (1,inf) for e>f>0. Lemma 8 is the swap for q>p and f>e. Lemma 9 says the pattern maximum is attained at m(e). Alaoglu-Erdos Theorem 1 is confirmed only second-hand: CNS 2012 eq. (5) cites '[1, Theorems 1 and 3]' for nonincreasing exponents together with kp=1 except for 4 and 36.
verification.correction: The identification needs an index shift and a domain restriction. The repo's G(t)=F_b(t)/F_a(t)=(1-t^{b+1})/(1-t^{a+1}) equals CLMS g_{e,f}(1/t) with e=b+1 and f=a+1, and only t in (0,1) is used. 'Identical' holds for CLMS Lemmas 7-9. Alaoglu-Erdos Theorem 1 (SA numbers only) is a consequence of the exchange principle. Ramanujan 1915 (d(n), highly composite numbers) is an analogue, not an identical result. The kp=1 clause is attributed by CNS to Theorems 1 and 3 jointly. The evidence level for the CLMS part is fulltext_read.

repo_statement: Section 4: nested prefix-level encoding l_r=#{i:b_i>=r}, with N_tail=R prod_r Q_{l_r}.
literature_result: The classical representation of CA numbers as products of primorials: N(eps) = prod_{k=1}^{K} prod_{p<x_k(eps)} p, where x_k is defined by F(x_k,k)=eps ('N is a product of primorials'). Morrill-Platt write their final checked n as 29996208012611# * 7662961# * ... * (3#)^10 * 2^19. The level lengths are the conjugate partition of the exponent partition.
citation: Caveney, Nicolas, Sondow, 'On SA, CA, and GA numbers', Ramanujan J. 29 (2012) 359-384 (arXiv:1112.6010), eqs. (7)-(11). Morrill-Platt 2021, proof of Theorem 13.
notes: The repo's g_{i,r}=(q^{r+1}-1)/(q(q^r-1)) equals 1+1/(q+...+q^r), so log g_{i,r}/log q_i = F(q_i,r), exactly the Alaoglu-Erdos/Robin critical-parameter function.

verification.evidence: CNS arXiv:1112.6010 eqs. (7)-(11) confirmed: F(t,k)=log(1+1/(t+...+t^k))/log t, decreasing in both t and k, and N=prod_{k=1}^K prod_{p<x_k} p. Crossref confirms Ramanujan J. 29(1) 359-384. The Morrill-Platt primorial form of their last checked n is confirmed. Algebraically, g_{q,r}=(q^{r+1}-1)/(q(q^r-1))=1+1/(q+...+q^r), so log g/log q=F(q,r) exactly.
verification.correction: CNS (10)-(11) describe CA numbers only. The general statement the repo uses (every HR/canonical integer is uniquely a product of primorials, with level lengths given by the conjugate partition) is classical folklore; see OEIS A025487, 'least integer of each prime signature; products of primorials'. Cite that as the general identification, and CNS as the CA special case.

repo_statement: Section 5 / R6: powered envelope I(...)^d <= (I_P I(R))^d M0^a V, with V a nested backward DP over levels with certified caps.
literature_result: The colossally abundant inequality: for every eps>0, sigma(n)/n^{1+eps} <= sigma(N_eps)/N_eps^{1+eps}, maximized by Alaoglu-Erdos/Ramanujan's explicit product. Equivalently I(n) <= I(N_eps)(n/N_eps)^eps, which is the Lagrangian relaxation of max I(n) subject to n<=B. Robin 1983 treats the analogous problem for d(n) (highly composite numbers) with three tools: Lagrangian relaxation (PR)_lambda, whose solutions are the superior HC numbers (Everett's theorem); a dynamic programme over primes with an exponent upper-bound vector ('vecteur majoration', i.e. caps); and Nicolas's 'benefit' method to fill gaps between relaxation solutions.
citation: G. Robin, 'Methodes d'optimisation pour un probleme de theorie des nombres', RAIRO Inform. Theor. 17(3) (1983) 239-247 (numdam ITA_1983__17_3_239_0), sections 1-3. H. Everett, Oper. Res. 11 (1963) 399-417. J.-L. Nicolas, Asterisque 24-25 (1975) 325-333 and 38-39 (1976) 169-182. Alaoglu-Erdos 1944, Theorem 10 (via Lagarias 2002 eq. (2.3)).
notes: With eps=a/d, the repo's envelope is the Everett/Lagrangian dual bound localized to a fixed-prefix, capped subtree, in exact rationals. Robin 1983 was fulltext_read; the Alaoglu-Erdos CA formula is via Lagarias and CNS. My own derivation, checked exactly: since F(q,r) decreases in both q and r, w_{i,r}=g_{i,r}^d/q_i^a>1 holds on an initial segment of i that shrinks with r. The nesting constraint therefore never binds, and V = prod_{r=2}^{A} prod_{i<=n_r} max(1, g_{i,r}^d q_i^{-a}), i.e. the classical separable CA solution. Exact-rational comparison of the DP and this closed form on 300 random instances: 0 mismatches. On the R6 fixture: V~91.216, U^{1/64}~3.8985 < 3.9.

verification.evidence: Robin, RAIRO Inform. Theor. 17 (1983) 239-247 (numdam ITA_1983__17_3_239_0; zbMATH 0531.10012) was read. The abstract and sections 1-3 contain dynamic programming, the Lagrangian relaxation (PR)_lambda, Everett's theorem, the 'vecteur majoration' cap vector (section 2.4), and Nicolas's 'methode des benefices' to fill gaps (section 3). The Alaoglu-Erdos Theorem 10 exponent formula is confirmed via Lagarias eq. (2.3). I independently re-implemented the backward DP and the closed form V=prod_{r=2}^A prod_{i<=n_r} max(1, g_{i,r}^d q_i^{-a}). On 300 random instances (consecutive primes, random nonincreasing caps, random (a,d)) I found 0 mismatches. The R6 fixture gives M0=5, V=91.21613, U^{1/64}=3.89853, and both U<(39/10)^64 and U<(12493/3150)^64 hold. The proof sketch is sound: by monotonicity of F in q and r, the positive sets are prefixes nonincreasing in r, so the nesting constraint is slack. 'Closely_analogous' is the right relation.

repo_statement: OPEN_CUTS section 2: control the canonical class with unbounded prime support and exponents.
literature_result: Robin 1984 Theorem 1 (RH <=> Robin for n>5040), combined with the canonical reduction (CLMS Proposition 1 / repo section 3), gives: RH <=> Robin's inequality holds for every Hardy-Ramanujan integer h>5040. Equally, RH <=> Robin holds on all SA numbers >5040 (Akbary-Friggstad) <=> on all CA numbers >5040 (Robin Proposition 1).
citation: Robin 1984, Theoreme 1. CLMS 2007, Proposition 1. Akbary-Friggstad 2009. Caveney-Nicolas-Sondow, Integers 11 (2011) A33 (arXiv:1110.5078), discussion after Definition 2.
notes: The 'unbounded canonical tail' is RH itself, not a smaller cut. Only parameter-restricted subclasses are genuinely smaller problems.

verification.evidence: This follows from Robin's equivalence, cited as stated in Lagarias, Morrill-Platt Theorem 1 and AF Theorem 2, plus CLMS Proposition 1 / the repo theorem. CNS 2011 (arXiv:1110.5078, after Definition 2) says AF 'combined with Robin's theorem ... implies the RH is true iff G(s)<e^g for all SA numbers s>5040'. The Integers 11 (2011) A33 journal-ref is confirmed by arXiv. The CA version needs Robin's numerical check below 55440 (see PA4). The conclusion that the unbounded canonical tail is RH itself is correct.

repo_statement: OPEN_CUTS section 2 requested output: 'a lemma with explicit dependence on support, exponent ... parameters, showing where an existing bound remains uniform'.
literature_result: Exponent-cap results, uniform in (unbounded) support: Robin holds for all t-free n>5040 with t=5 (CLMS Theorem 5), t=7 (Sole-Planat), t=11 (Broughan-Trudgian), t=20 (Morrill-Platt Theorem 2) and t=21 (Axler Theorem 1.2). Hence RH <=> Robin for all 21-full n (Axler Corollary 2.5). Single-prime valuation conditions: Robin holds for n>5040 if v2(n)<=19 (Hertlein Theorem 1), or if v2(n)<=20, or v5(n)<=8, or vp(n)<=4 for some prime 11<p<=19, <=3 for some 19<p<=41, <=2 for some 41<p<=139, or =1 for some 139<p<=1777 (Axler Theorem 1.4). CLMS also covers odd n>9, squarefree n not in {2,3,5,6,10,30}, and squarefull n beyond a finite list.
citation: Morrill-Platt, Integers 21 (2021) A28, Theorem 2. C. Axler, 'On Robin's inequality', Ramanujan J. 61 (2023) 909-919 (arXiv:2110.13478), Theorems 1.2 and 1.4. A. Hertlein, Integers 18 (2018) A71 (arXiv:1612.05186), Theorems 1-3. Broughan-Trudgian, Integers 15 (2015) A12. Sole-Planat, Integers 12 (2012) 301-309. CLMS 2007, Theorems 1, 2, 4, 5.
notes: These are existing instances of exactly the requested output type. In canonical language, any canonical violator has b_1>=21, and by monotonicity all exponents up to 1777 satisfy Axler's floors. The constraints rest on explicit prime-counting inputs (Dusart; Platt-Trudgian RH verification to 3*10^12) and must be labelled as imported.

verification.evidence: Axler arXiv:2110.13478 is Ramanujan J. 61(3) (2023) 909-919 (zbMATH 1532.11010). Theorem 1.2 (21-free), Corollary 2.5 (RH iff Robin for all 21-full n) and the six bullet conditions of Theorem 1.4 are confirmed verbatim. Hertlein arXiv:1612.05186v2 Theorem 1 (v2(n)<=19) is confirmed; zbMATH 1450.11096 gives Integers 18 (2018) A71. Morrill-Platt Theorem 2 (20-free), Broughan-Trudgian Integers 15 A12 (zbMATH 1316.11088), Sole-Planat Integers 12(2) 301-309 (zbMATH 1266.11106) and CLMS Theorems 1, 2, 4 and 5 are confirmed.
verification.correction: Two fixes to the canonical-language gloss. First, for 139<p<=1777 Axler only excludes v_p(n)=1, so it is not a floor unless p divides n. Second, the claim that every canonical violator has v_p>=2 for all p<=1777 needs the support to extend past 1777. That follows from the known range (Morrill-Platt) plus the support-size bound, not from exponent monotonicity alone. Hertlein Theorem 2's floors on v3, v7 and v11 (12, 6, 5) should be listed too. Constraints relying on Dusart and the Platt-Trudgian RH height must be labelled as imported.

repo_statement: Section 3 boundary 'support size and exponents remain unbounded'; OPEN_CUTS support-dependence.
literature_result: Vojak Theorem 1.4 / Corollary 1.5: with M(k)=exp(e^-g f(N_k)) - log N_k (where f(N_k)=N_k/phi(N_k) and N_k is the k-th primorial), an n with omega(n)=k satisfies Robin if some a_i >= 1+M(k)/log q_i, and every such n satisfies Robin if M(k)<=0. Theorem 1.6: the least counterexample c is SA, has omega(c)>=969,672,728, fewer than omega(c)/14 non-unit exponents, and p_{omega(c)}<log c. CLMS Lemma 11: the least t-free counterexample has P(n)<log n.
citation: Vojak, arXiv:2005.09307, Theorems 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, Corollary 1.5, Theorem 3.5. CLMS 2007, Lemma 11.
notes: Elementary consequence: since I(h) < N_k/phi(N_k) when omega(h)=k, any violator with support k has log h < exp(e^-g N_k/phi(N_k)). So each fixed-support canonical class contains only finitely many candidates; e.g. k=4 gives h<~1.16*10^5, matching Vojak's 116144. The unboundedness lies only in support size. M(k)<=0 is exactly failure of Nicolas's inequality at N_k. Vojak's omega(c) bound used Briggs's 10^(10^10). Rerunning his inequality with Morrill-Platt's range gives log p_omega > ~31.0, omega(c) >~ 10^12 (my floating-point extrapolation, not certified).

verification.evidence: Vojak Theorem 1.4 (M(k)=exp(e^-g f(N_k))-log N_k and M_k(q)=1+M(k)/log q), Corollary 1.5 and Theorem 1.6 items 1-5 (SA; omega(c)>=969,672,728; fewer than omega(c)/14 non-unit exponents; p_omega(c)/log c<1) are all confirmed verbatim. Vojak's proof of item 2 uses Briggs's c>10^(10^10). CLMS Lemma 11 (least t-free counterexample has P(n)<log n) is confirmed. I recomputed the elementary support bound log h<exp(e^-g N_k/phi(N_k)): k=4 gives log h<11.6626, i.e. h<~1.16e5, matching Vojak's 116144; k=10 gives 10^15.19, k=25 gives 10^46.18 and k=30 gives 10^57.86. M(k)<=0 is exactly nonstrict failure of Nicolas's inequality at N_k. The omega(c)>~1e12 figure is, as the draft itself says, an uncertified extrapolation.

repo_statement: Arithmetic route organization (prime support plus exponent pattern; canonical reduction as the sigma-analogue of a minimal-n reduction).
literature_result: Nicolas 1983: RH <=> N_k/phi(N_k) > e^g loglog N_k for all primorials N_k (k>=1). If RH is false, the inequality holds for infinitely many k and fails for infinitely many k. For n/phi(n), which depends only on the prime support, the minimal-n representative of a support size is the primorial, so the criterion collapses to a one-parameter family. For sigma the analogous one-parameter family is the CA numbers.
citation: J.-L. Nicolas, 'Petites valeurs de la fonction d'Euler', J. Number Theory 17 (1983) 375-388 (zbMATH 0521.10039). Restated in Nazardonyavi-Yakubovich arXiv:1211.2147 (eq. 1.5) and Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944.
notes: The original JNT text was not fetched.

verification.evidence: Nicolas, J. Number Theory 17 (1983) 375-388 (zbMATH 0521.10039) exists. NY arXiv:1211.2147 eq. (1.5) restates it: under RH, N_k/(phi(N_k) loglog N_k)>e^g for all k>=2; if RH is false, the inequality holds for infinitely many k and fails for infinitely many k. The original was not read.
verification.correction: Nicolas's criterion is stated for k>=2. For k=1, loglog 2<0 and the quotient form is meaningless. Keep evidence_level as secondary_source.

repo_statement: Section 3: equivalent search domains for a Robin violation.
literature_result: Further RH-equivalent thin subsequences. Extremely abundant (XA) numbers: the least counterexample, if any, is XA; RH <=> XA is infinite (NY Theorems 2.3-2.4). Extraordinary (GA1 and GA2) numbers: RH <=> 4 is the only extraordinary number, and if RH fails, the least N>5040 attaining max G is extraordinary (CNS 2011). Wu: RH <=> Robin for all CA2 numbers >5040 (a subset of CA). Lagarias: RH <=> sigma(n) <= H_n + exp(H_n) log H_n for all n.
citation: Nazardonyavi-Yakubovich, arXiv:1211.2147 (J. Integer Seq. 17 (2014) Art. 14.2.8, zbMATH 1342.11009). Caveney-Nicolas-Sondow, Integers 11 (2011) A33 (arXiv:1110.5078). X. Wu, arXiv:1903.03490 (preprint), Corollary 4. J. C. Lagarias, Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002) 534-543 (arXiv:math/0008177), Theorem 1.1.
notes: All of these are stronger thinnings than HR. NY and CNS were fulltext_read. Wu was only partially read (main corollary) and is an unrefereed preprint.

verification.evidence: NY arXiv:1211.2147 is confirmed: Theorem 2.3 (least counterexample is XA) and Theorem 2.4 (RH iff #XA=infinity). CNS 2011 is confirmed: Theorem 5 (RH iff 4 is the only extraordinary number) and Corollary 1 (if RH is false, the least N>5040 with G(N)=max is extraordinary). The Wu arXiv:1903.03490 abstract and Corollary 4 (RH iff Robin for all CA2 numbers >5040) are confirmed, unrefereed. Lagarias Theorem 1.1 is confirmed, with journal-ref Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002) 534-543.
verification.correction: The JIS 17 (2014) Art. 14.2.8 version (zbMATH 1342.11009) is titled 'Extremely abundant numbers and the Riemann hypothesis'. The arXiv v3 title differs ('Superabundant numbers, their subsequences and the Riemann hypothesis'), and the theorem numbers quoted come from the arXiv text. 'Extraordinary' is CNS 2011 Definition 1; the GA1/GA2 terminology is from CNS 2012.

obstruction: If RH is false, Robin's inequality fails for infinitely many n, by a secondary-term margin. There exist 0<beta<1/2 (any 1-b<beta<1/2, with b=Re(rho)>1/2) and C>0 such that sigma(n) >= e^g n loglog n + C n loglog n/(log n)^beta infinitely often.
citation: Robin 1984, Section 4, Proposition 1, as restated in Lagarias, arXiv:math/0008177, Proposition 3.2.
how_it_constrains: A theorem covering the whole unbounded canonical tail is RH itself. No 'complete infinite pruning argument' weaker than RH can exist. Any proposed unconditional tail theorem must contain RH-strength analytic input, i.e. a bound on prime counts at the scale x^{1/2+o(1)}.
evidence_level: fulltext_read (Lagarias restatement; Robin original not accessed)

verification.evidence: Lagarias arXiv:math/0008177 Proposition 3.2 is confirmed verbatim. If RH is false, there exist 0<beta<1/2 and C>0 with sigma(n)>=e^g n loglog n + C n loglog n/(log n)^beta for infinitely many n. Here 1-b<beta<1/2 with b=Re(rho)>1/2, and Lagarias attributes it to Robin [18] Section 4 Proposition 1. The 2026 Zimov preprints use the same Omega-result.
verification.correction: The constraint 'a theorem covering the whole canonical tail is RH' follows directly from Robin's equivalence (Theoreme 1) plus the canonical reduction. The Omega-result is the ingredient of the 'Robin implies RH' direction, not an extra obstruction. 'No complete pruning argument weaker than RH can exist' is tautological: any such argument is a proof of RH. 'Prime counts at scale x^{1/2+o(1)}' is the draft's interpretive gloss, not a cited statement. The Omega-result also gives violations a quantified margin, which helps a search rather than hindering it.

obstruction: Under RH the Robin margin on the extremal (SA/CA) numbers tends to zero: limsup (sigma(n)/n - e^g loglog n) sqrt(log n) <= -e^g(2sqrt2 - 4 - g + log 4pi) ~ -1.393 (Ramanujan, assuming RH). The explicit form is sigma(n)/n <= e^g(loglog n - 2(sqrt2-1)/sqrt(log n) + S_1(log n) + O(...)), where S_1 is a sum over zeta zeros.
citation: S. Ramanujan, 'Highly composite numbers', annotated by J.-L. Nicolas and G. Robin, Ramanujan J. 1 (1997) 119-153 (zbMATH 0917.11043), sections 59-71; restated in Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944 section 1, CNS arXiv:1110.5078 Proposition 1, Axler arXiv:2110.13478 final remark.
how_it_constrains: Finite pruning and envelopes with a fixed relative margin cannot close the tail. The margin shrinks like (log n)^{-1/2} and oscillates with the zeros through S_1.

verification.evidence: Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1211.6944 (lines 150-160) gives limsup (sigma_{-1}(n)-e^g loglog n) sqrt(log n) <= -e^g(2sqrt2-4-g+log4pi) = -1.393... under RH. Axler arXiv:2110.13478 (final Remark) quotes Ramanujan [p.143]: sigma(n)/n <= e^g(loglog n - 2(sqrt2-1)/sqrt(log n) + S_1(log n) + O(1)/(sqrt(log n) loglog n)), with S_1(x)=sum_rho x^{rho-1}/|rho|^2. The Ramanujan J. 1 (1997) 119-153 citation is confirmed by Crossref (DOI 10.1023/a:1009764017495). The original was not read, so this rests on secondary sources.

obstruction: For every fixed n0, limsup_{a->inf} G(a n0) = e^g. Any subtree with a fixed prefix and an unrestricted continuation has no margin. A margin exists only once continuation exponents are capped, and with cap A the asymptotic margin is about a factor prod(1-p^{-A-1}), which tends to 1 as A grows.
citation: Caveney-Nicolas-Sondow, Ramanujan J. 29 (2012) 359-384 (arXiv:1112.6010), Fact 2 (citing CNS 2011, Lemma 10).
how_it_constrains: A subtree tail lemma must be stated per (prefix, cap A). Uniformity in A is equivalent to RH, because every n is t-free for some t.

verification.evidence: CNS 2012 Fact 2 is confirmed: limsup_{a->inf} G(a n0)=e^g. Its citation of '[3, Lemma 10]' is correct for the published Integers 11 A33 version, which I fetched and where it is Lemma 10; the arXiv v2 numbers it Lemma 1. The cited result is right, but the inference drawn from it is not. Fact 2 concerns all multiples a*n0, where a may raise the exponents of n0's primes. In the repo's canonical tree, a prefix fixes the exponents b_1..b_m of p_1..p_m exactly. For such an exact-prefix subtree, Mertens gives limsup of I(h)/(e^g loglog h) <= prod_{i<=m}(1-p_i^{-b_i-1}) < 1, even with unrestricted tail exponents. With tail cap A, the bound is multiplied by prod_{p>p_m}(1-p^{-A-1}).
verification.correction: Replace 'any subtree with a fixed prefix and unrestricted continuation has no margin; a margin exists only once exponents are capped'. The correct statement: every exact-prefix canonical subtree has an unconditional asymptotic margin factor prod_{i<=m}(1-p_i^{-b_i-1})·prod_{p>p_m}(1-p^{-A-1}) < 1, so it contains only finitely many potential violators. The real obstruction is nonuniformity: the margin tends to 1, and the finite remainder before the asymptotic regime blows up, as prefix exponents and A grow. Fact 2 applies to the 'multiples of n0' class, not to exact-prefix subtrees. The draft's last sentence (uniformity in A is equivalent to RH) stands.

obstruction: The t-free (Sole-Planat Psi_t) method stalls with current explicit inputs. Morrill-Platt report that both their finite-range and asymptotic bounds exceed 1 at t=21. Axler reached t=21 only with improved Mertens-product estimates. The method's margin e^g(1-1/zeta(t)) ~ e^g 2^{-t} must dominate explicit prime-counting errors.
citation: Morrill-Platt 2021, Section 5 'Comments'. Axler 2023, Theorem 1.2.
how_it_constrains: Exponent-uniform 'tail lemmas' are capped by the precision of explicit PNT and Mertens bounds. Pushing t up by one requires better explicit inputs; no t-free argument reaches unbounded exponents.

verification.evidence: Morrill-Platt section 5 'Comments' is confirmed verbatim: g_B(29996208012611;21)>1 and g_inf(B;21)>1, 'so one would need improvements in both'. Axler's introduction says Theorem 1.2 comes from applying 'recently improved estimates for the product in (1.2) to Sole and Planat's method'. The t-free limsup is e^g/zeta(t), so the margin is e^g(1-1/zeta(t)) ~ e^g 2^{-t}, as the draft says.

obstruction: Size of the canonical search domain: HR integers <= x number exp((1+o(1)) 2pi sqrt(log x/(3 loglog x))) (Hardy-Ramanujan 1917). SA numbers <= x number between (log x)^{1+5/48} for large x (Erdos-Nicolas 1975) and exp(O((loglog x)^2)) (Alaoglu-Erdos). CA numbers form a one-parameter family.
citation: Hardy-Ramanujan, Proc. LMS 16 (1917) 112-132 (via CLMS 2007 Proposition 1). Erdos-Nicolas, Bull. SMF 103 (1975) 65-90. Akbary-Friggstad 2009, p. 2 (quoting Alaoglu-Erdos).
how_it_constrains: Not an obstruction to truth, but to the computational route. Canonical-tree traversal (the frozen 10^54/10^100 deposit) is super-polylogarithmically larger than SA or CA certification of the same range. Published CA-based certification already reaches 10^(10^13.11) (Morrill-Platt Theorem 13).

verification.evidence: The HR count is confirmed from CLMS Proposition 1. AF p.2 quotes Alaoglu-Erdos (log S(x)/(loglog x)^2 bounded) and Erdos-Nicolas (liminf log S(x)/loglog x >= 1+5/48). The Morrill-Platt range is confirmed.
verification.correction: Erdos-Nicolas gives S(x) >= (log x)^{1+5/48-o(1)} for large x, not exactly (log x)^{1+5/48). The super-polylogarithmic size comparison applies to an unpruned canonical traversal. The size of the repo's pruned (envelope) traversal is not determined by the HR count, so 'canonical-tree traversal is super-polylogarithmically larger' should be stated for exhaustive enumeration only.

tool: Robin's CA interpolation lemma combined with Briggs's CA-number algorithm, run in directed or interval arithmetic (as Morrill-Platt did)
citation: Robin 1984, Section 3, Proposition 1. Briggs, Exp. Math. 15 (2006). Morrill-Platt 2021, Theorem 13 (100-bit interval arithmetic).
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS arithmetic-tail 'exact finite certificate restricted to a clearly declared range', and RESULTS_INDEX 'Larger Robin certificate programme' (unreplayed 10^54/10^100 canonical traversals).
precise_next_step: Enumerate consecutive CA pairs (N,N') up to X by ordering the critical values F(p,k)=log(1+1/(p+...+p^k))/log p. Certify G(N)<e^g at each N with the repo's existing directed atanh/harmonic/exp enclosures. Then cover every n in [N,N'] via the elementary convexity proof of Robin's Proposition 1. To avoid four-exponential ties, use rational eps=a/d slightly off each critical value; the repo's powered envelope with an empty prefix is exactly this rational-eps CA bound. That gives a second, independent backend for the [5041,5582] barrier and a route to any declared range.
risk: The interpolation needs a complete, correctly ordered CA list, so tie handling at critical eps must be certified. The result only re-certifies ranges already published (Morrill-Platt). Its value is independent exact replay, not new mathematics.

tool: Akbary-Friggstad least-counterexample-is-SA, combined with Alaoglu-Erdos exponent relations for SA numbers
citation: Akbary-Friggstad 2009, Theorem 3. Alaoglu-Erdos 1944, Theorem 2 (k_r in {beta-1, beta, beta+1}, beta=floor(k_q log q/log r)) and q^{k_q} < 2^{k_2+2}, as restated in Nazardonyavi-Yakubovich arXiv:1211.2147, Proposition 4.3 and Remark 4.8. NY Theorem 4.4: floor(log p/log q) <= k_q.
target_gap: R6 'certified caps' for bounded subtrees when the goal is 'no violation <= B'.
precise_next_step: For range statements, restrict candidates to SA numbers (valid because the least violator <= B would be SA). Derive certified caps and floors from Alaoglu-Erdos Theorem 2 relative to the prefix exponents and the largest prime. Feed them into the R6 contract as m_i, together with Axler Theorem 1.4 floors as imported constraints.
risk: These caps are valid only for SA candidates, not for every admissible completion. They must not be inserted into the pointwise envelope theorem, only into a separately stated range-certificate theorem. The Alaoglu-Erdos original was only seen via secondary sources.

tool: The Sole-Planat generalized Dedekind function Psi_t, with explicit Mertens-product and theta bounds, adapted to fixed-prefix, capped canonical subtrees
citation: Sole-Planat, Integers 12 (2012). Morrill-Platt 2021, sections 1-3. Axler 2023, Lemma 2.4 and Theorem 1.3. Dusart 2018 explicit bounds.
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS arithmetic-tail 'a lemma with explicit dependence on support, exponent ... parameters'.
precise_next_step: Fix a prefix P=prod_{i<=m} p_i^{b_i} and a tail cap A. Bound I(h) <= I(P) prod_{m<i<=k}(1-p_i^{-A-1})/(1-p_i^{-1}) and log h >= log P + theta(p_k) - theta(p_m). Using explicit Mertens bounds, prove Robin for all k >= k0(P,A) with explicit k0, leaving a finite remainder for the envelope or a CA check. Empty P with A=t-1 recovers the t-free theorems.
risk: The margin prod_{p not dividing P}(1-p^{-A-1}) tends to 1 as A grows (O3/O4). This yields bounded contributions only, never the tail, and current explicit inputs already stall near A=20.

tool: Support-size finiteness bound (elementary), linked to Nicolas's criterion
citation: Vojak arXiv:2005.09307, Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5. Nicolas, J. Number Theory 17 (1983).
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS arithmetic-tail support dependence; packet section 3 'support size and exponents remain unbounded'.
precise_next_step: State and prove natively: if omega(h)=k and h violates Robin, then log h < exp(e^-g N_k/phi(N_k)), so the class omega=k is finite. Certify the bound B_k with directed enclosures; floating-point estimates give B_10~10^15.2, B_25~10^46.2, B_30~10^57.9. Then any replayed and authenticated finite certificate to B would yield the infinite-class theorem 'Robin holds for all n>5040 with omega(n)<=k0(B)'. Note that M(k)<=0 exactly when Nicolas's inequality fails at N_k.
risk: The resulting theorems are much weaker than what Morrill-Platt's range already implies (omega up to about 10^12). This is useful as a correctly quantified bounded contribution, not as progress on RH.

tool: Closed form for the envelope DP: separable Lagrangian (CA-type) solution
citation: Monotonicity of F(t,k) in both t and k: Caveney-Nicolas-Sondow arXiv:1112.6010, eqs. (7)-(9); Alaoglu-Erdos 1944. Lagrangian framing: Robin, RAIRO 1983, section 1.
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS 'Bounded contributions: independent exact finite arithmetic'; R6 envelope second backend.
precise_next_step: Add the lemma V_2(n) = prod_{r=2}^{A} prod_{i<=n_r} max(1, g_{i,r}^d / q_i^a). Proof: w_{i,r}>1 iff F(q_i,r)>a/d. F decreases in q and r, so the positive set is a prefix L_r that is nonincreasing in r, and min(L_r,n_r) is a nested maximizer. Use this as an independent exact check of every DP value. Choose (a,d) with a/d near the CA parameter matched to the budget (eps ~ F(x,1) with x ~ log B).
risk: Low. This is my own derivation, verified only by exact-rational comparison on 300 random instances and the R6 fixture (0 mismatches). It needs the usual review before integration.

tool: Nicolas 'benefit' method and Everett's generalized Lagrange multipliers for filling gaps between relaxation optima
citation: Robin, RAIRO 1983, section 3 (benefit B(n) relative to the bracketing superior HC numbers). Nicolas, Asterisque 24-25 (1975) and 38-39 (1976). Everett, Oper. Res. 11 (1963).
target_gap: Efficient complete enumeration of near-extremal (SA) numbers between consecutive CA numbers for range certificates. AF note there is no known guaranteed fast algorithm for listing all SA numbers below a bound.
precise_next_step: Define the benefit of n relative to the bracketing CA pair, ben(n) = eps log(n/N) - log(I(n)/I(N)) >= 0. Bound the benefit any SA number in [N,N'] can carry, and enumerate only completions with benefit below that bound, using the repo's nested-level encoding as the enumeration skeleton.
risk: The benefit bounds for sigma (as opposed to d(n)) must be derived and certified. The method is classical for HC numbers, but I did not find a published certified implementation for SA numbers.

repo_statement: L-99613: all-x positivity of the smoothed signed sum H^{[m]}, m>=2 (effective Dirichlet exponent sigma=(m+1)/2>=3/2).
literature_result: For every integer q>=1, real sigma>=1, integer k>=1 and X>=1: 0 <= sum_{n<=X,(n,q)=1} mu(n) n^{-sigma} log^k(X/n) <= 1.00303 (q/phi(q)) (k+(sigma-1)log X)(log X)^{k-1}. The case k=1, sigma=1 is Lemma 4.1: 0 <= sum mu(n)/n log(X/n) <= 1.00303 q/phi(q). The paper attributes the sigma=1 non-negativity to Pólya (1919) and Turán (1948, §25). The sigma>1 case is deduced by expanding X^eps into log-moments, which transfers positivity upward in sigma.
citation: O. Ramaré and S. Zuniga Alterman, 'Möbius function and primes: an identity factory with applications', arXiv:2312.05138v3, Theorem 1.2 (p.2-3), Lemma 4.1 and proof of Thm 1.2 (p.9-10); G. Pólya, Jahresber. DMV 28 (1919) 31-40; P. Turán, Danske Vid. Selsk. Mat.-Fys. Medd. 24 (1948).
notes: Both are all-X positivity statements for smoothed Möbius sums. In both, the limiting main term is strictly positive and the remainder decays, so neither touches RH scale. The literature result sits closer to the critical line in sigma (sigma=1, log-Riesz kernel) than SHARP m=2 (sigma=3/2). The kernel T^m and the 67-modified beta differ, so the relation is not 'identical'. The RZA transfer runs from sigma=1 to sigma>1, the opposite of the m=2 -> m=1 descent the repo needs.

verification.evidence: RZA arXiv:2312.05138v3 checked in full text. verification.evidence: The ratio was re-derived. A(y)=12sqrt y+C_0+E(y): the ramp integral is 6sqrt x(log4+2-log4)=12sqrt x, and C_0 matches §8. So F/M tends to prod_{p<=61}(1-1/p)/(1+1/p)=0.0283981=1/35.21, inside [1/42,1/8]. However, R25 (reviews/D-pass4/PROOFS_AND_REPAIRS.md, line 28) says 'The conclusion is the same repaired theorem as L-97400, not a claim of mathematical novelty'. In context this means the replacement certificate does not claim a new theorem beyond L-97400. It is not a disclaimer of literature novelty. Legendre's identity sits in Tenenbaum §I.4 (sieve of Eratosthenes) rather than §III.6.
verification.correction: Drop 'R25 already disclaims novelty' here and in novelty_assessment (c). State instead that R25 says the repair reproduces L-97400's theorem. Keep 'repo_stronger' (explicit all-real constants plus a directed certificate).

obstruction: Ingham's theorem (1942) applies to critical Möbius-type sums with a constant bias. If M(x)/sqrt x or L(x)/sqrt x is bounded on one side, then RH holds, the zeros are simple, and the zero ordinates satisfy infinitely many Z-linear relations. If there are no, or only finitely many, such relations, liminf = -infinity and limsup = +infinity. Mossinghoff-Trudgian and Humphries adapt the argument to L_1 (alpha=1, Turán's function).
citation: A. E. Ingham, Amer. J. Math. 64 (1942) 313-319 (zbMATH 0063.02974 review); the adaptation to alpha in [0,1/2) and alpha=1 is summarised in P. Humphries, arXiv:1108.1524, §1, and M. J. Mossinghoff and T. S. Trudgian, arXiv:2007.14537, §1.
how_it_constrains: H_1 has constant apparent bias b_H ≈ 1.8033. Its zero coefficients have size about 1/(gamma|zeta'(rho)|), and their absolute sum appears to diverge like the Mertens sum (1.674 after 400 zeros). Eventual nonnegativity of H_1 would imply RH (L-99943) and, by the Ingham argument, Q-linear dependence of the ordinates; it is therefore expected false under LI. The adaptation to H_1 has not been checked line by line. The repo's negative-mass formulation of OPEN.ARITH.CV avoids this obstruction. Any route needing pointwise H_1>=0 (or a fixed-p deep-root sign with constant bias) should be treated as LI-obstructed.
evidence_level: abstract_only (Ingham review) + fulltext_read (summaries in Humphries and Mossinghoff-Trudgian) + analyst computation (h1coef.py)

verification.evidence: The zbMATH 0063.02974 review of Ingham 1942 matches. Either conjecture implies RH and simple zeros, and the ordinates must be linearly dependent. With no or finitely many integer relations, liminf x^{-1/2}M=-inf and limsup=+inf, and likewise for L. The MT arXiv:2007.14537 §1 and Humphries §1/Thm 2.8 full texts confirm the alpha=1 (Turán) and 0<=alpha<1/2 adaptations. For H_1, c_rho ~ (1-67^{-rho})/(gamma zeta'(rho)) with |1-67^{-rho}|>=1-67^{-1/2}. Divergence of sum|c_rho| therefore follows from the Mertens case, and the numerics were reproduced (1.6742 against 1.6368). The H_1 adaptation is still unwritten, as the draft says. A Tanaka/MMT-Thm-3 first-zero argument should additionally give, unconditionally, that H_1-b_H changes sign infinitely often (my derivation).

obstruction: Finite positivity is unreliable at critical scale. Turán's T(x)=sum lambda(n)/n has positive apparent bias (sqrt x T(x) has bias -1/zeta(1/2)=0.685), yet it is first negative at x=72,185,376,951,205. Pólya's L(x) first changes sign at 906,150,257.
citation: C. B. Haselgrove, Mathematika 5 (1958) 141-145 (zbMATH 0085.27102); Borwein-Ferguson-Mossinghoff, Math. Comp. 77 (2008), as quoted in Angelo-Xu, arXiv:2205.05822, eq. (1.1); Tanaka, as quoted in Humphries §1.
how_it_constrains: H_1>=1 on [1,1e7] (analyst exploratory computation) is not evidence for the critical estimate. H_1's bias is 2.6 times Turán's, so any negative values are expected only at astronomically large x.

verification.evidence: Angelo-Xu arXiv:2205.05822 eq. (1.1) gives N_0=72,185,376,951,205, attributed to Borwein-Ferguson-Mossinghoff (Math. Comp. 77 (2008) 1681-1694, Zbl 1198.11090). Humphries §1 gives Tanaka's 906,150,257. The Haselgrove review (Zbl 0085.27102) confirms the Ingham-inequality disproof. -1/zeta(1/2)=0.684765 and b_H/0.6848=2.63. Caveat: comparing biases alone says little without the oscillation amplitudes; 'astronomically large' is a qualitative expectation.

obstruction: Parity problem. Sieve axioms based on level of distribution (Type I, axiom R) cannot determine signed Möbius/prime sums, even at level x^{1-eps} (Selberg; Bombieri's asymptotic sieve). A bilinear hypothesis exploiting sign changes of mu(mn) is required.
citation: J. Friedlander and H. Iwaniec, 'Asymptotic sieve for primes', Ann. of Math. 148 (1998) 1041-1065, arXiv:math/9811186, §1 (pp.1041, 1044-1045); E. Bombieri, 'The asymptotic sieve', Mem. Accad. Naz. XL 1/2 (1976) 243-269.
how_it_constrains: The dynamic critical Bellman block (fixed/small least prime) cannot be closed by propagating positivity through Buchstab/Bellman recursions fed only with rough-number densities, Dickman/Buchstab profiles or sieve bounds. A source-specific bilinear (Type II) Möbius input is unavoidable. Even such an input yields only log-power savings, not the x^{-1/2+eps} scale this RH-bearing root needs.

verification.evidence: FI arXiv:math/9811186 §1, full text. The parity problem is attributed to [S],[B]: 'with (R) alone one cannot capture the primes, even for D(x)=x^{1-eps}, which is the case treated by Bombieri'. Selberg's example satisfies (R) but fails (B), and the cancellation in (B) comes from sign changes of mu(mn). The Bombieri citation format matches FI's own reference list. Two problems remain. First, the claim 'Type II inputs yield only log-power savings' is inaccurate: unconditional Möbius cancellation reaches VK-type savings exp(-c(log x)^{3/5}(loglog x)^{-1/5}), which beat every log power. Second, applying parity to the Bellman block is a heuristic principle, not a theorem about that object.
verification.correction: Say 'at best sub-power (VK-type) savings, never x^{-1/2+eps}'. Label the Bellman-block constraint as a heuristic parity barrier. The binding obstruction at fixed least prime is RH-scale, not parity.

obstruction: RH-equivalence of the smooth-number asymptotic at y ≈ (log x)^{2+eps} (Hildebrand 1984).
citation: A. Hildebrand, Mathematika 31 (1984) 258-271 (zbMATH 0544.10042).
how_it_constrains: Uniform growing-P control with relative margins once P extends to primes up to about (log X)^2 and beyond lives where the smooth-number analogue is RH-equivalent. At z near x, the P61-type object becomes the full critical detector. A bounded-envelope or Rankin-type argument cannot cross this threshold.

verification.evidence: The Hildebrand 1984 statement was verified (zbMATH review; HT survey p.416). As an obstruction for the repo object it is an analogy. A-audit F14 says the kappa=1/2 boundary is the loss of a Rankin/bounded-remainder proof margin, not a proved failure. Hildebrand's theorem concerns Psi(x,y), not the signed P-cube. The draft's 'cannot cross this threshold' is credible for bounded-envelope arguments but is not a theorem.
verification.correction: Downgrade to a heuristic barrier with a common square-root-scale origin, and record that F14 itself proves no failure at kappa=1/2.

obstruction: Pretentious/Halász ceiling. For general multiplicative f with |f|<=1, one-sided bounds on sum f(n)/n are only of size (log log x)^{-3/5} to 1/log x, and negative values of size -c/log x are attained by some f in F1.
citation: Granville and Soundararajan, arXiv:math/0508361, Theorems 1-2.
how_it_constrains: Any argument that uses only multiplicativity, |f|<=1 and prime-sum data cannot reach the power saving required by OPEN.ARITH.CV or FCHD67. Power savings need zero-free-strip information, i.e. RH-strength.

verification.evidence: GS full text. Theorem 1 gives delta(x)>=-(loglog x)^{-3/5} for all f in F, and some f in F1 has sum f(n)/n<=-c/log x (§2 construction via Haselgrove). Theorem 2 covers F*. The inference that class-level (multiplicativity, |f|<=1) arguments cannot yield power savings is a sound heuristic consequence, not a stated theorem.

obstruction: Limit of the subunit-mass method. The labelled-level contraction needs sum_p p^{-(m+1)/2}+67^{-(m+1)/2}<1, i.e. m>m*≈1.80207. At m=1 the relevant mass is the divergent prime-harmonic series (Mertens).
citation: Analyst computation (mpmath primezeta, h1bias.py); L-99613 §5 and R-99611 as quoted there.
how_it_constrains: No variant of the Euler-cube/level-mass proof can reach m=1 without genuine cancellation input. The gap between m*≈1.80 and m=1 is structural, consistent with the repo's 'critical wall'.

verification.evidence: Recomputed: sigma*=1.4010342689 (P(sigma)+67^{-sigma}=1), m*=1.8020685377. L-99613 §5 (sharp_src) states the prime-harmonic divergence at exponent one and cites R-99611. The restriction applies to this proof technique; positivity of H^{[m]} for 1<m<m* is neither proved nor refuted (it is eventually positive by PA3).

obstruction: Unsmoothed partial sums sum_{n<=X} mu(n) and sum_{n<=X} mu(n)/n change sign infinitely often (Kaczorowski-Pintz). Log-smoothed sums at sigma=1 are nonnegative (Pólya/Turán/RZA).
citation: J. Kaczorowski and J. Pintz, 'Oscillatory properties of arithmetical functions I', Acta Math. Hungar. (1986), Cor. 4, as cited in arXiv:2312.05138 p.3.
how_it_constrains: Sign targets must keep enough smoothing. Removing the ramp or kernel smoothing from a detector can turn a plausible sign statement into a false one.

verification.evidence: RZA p.3 (full text) states that partial sums of mu(n) and mu(n)/n oscillate infinitely often, proved for instance by Kaczorowski-Pintz [15, Cor. 4]. The reference list gives Acta Math. Hung. 48 (1986) 173-185. The smoothed sum is non-negative by Theorem 1.2. Kaczorowski-Pintz itself was not opened (secondary source). The constraint fits the PA1 observation that T^m does not vanish at the endpoint.

tool: Legendre/Tao identity plus standard sieve lower bounds, giving an explicit and jointly uniform margin for prime-interval prefixes.
citation: Tao, arXiv:0908.4323, proof of Thm 1.1 and Thm 1.1 (|A_P|<=1); Phi(x,y)<<x/log y and the Fundamental Lemma (Halberstam-Richert, Sieve Methods, Thm 2.5; Friedlander-Iwaniec, Opera de Cribro §6); uniform Dickman asymptotics for bounded u (Hildebrand-Tenenbaum 1993 survey).
target_gap: Required fix of ARITH.DICKMAN.FIXED_EXPONENT_INTERVALS (L-101220/L-101221, CONDITIONAL_EXACT): joint uniformity in endpoint ratio, moving u, continuity points, tails and positive margin.
precise_next_step: Step 1: for x>=p, write A_{p,q}(x) >= N_P(x)/x - C/log p - 1/p. Step 2: bound N_P(x)/x below. For x<=q^K use N_P(x)>=Psi(x,p)>=x rho(KA)/2 for p>=p_1(K,A). For x>=q^K use the Fundamental Lemma with level sqrt x, giving N_P(x)>=x prod_{p<l<q}(1-1/l)(1-O(e^{-K/2})) >= x/(2A). Step 3: conclude A_{p,q}(x) >= min(rho(KA)/2, 1/(2A)) - C/log p for all real x>=1. Step 4: by Tao's bound, the L-101221 compensation terms are at most p^{-1/2}+q^{-1/2}+(pq)^{-1/2} <= 3p^{-1/2}, so B_{p,q}(x)>0 for p>=p_0(A) with an explicit margin, and the subsequence argument is no longer needed.
risk: Low to moderate. The uniformity constants in the Fundamental Lemma for sieving an interval of primes, and the Psi lower bound for bounded u, must be pinned to exact cited statements. Making p_0(A) effective requires explicit sieve constants. This tool does not touch the fixed/small-prime deep root.

tool: All-X, all-q non-negativity of log-smoothed Möbius sums: 0 <= sum_{n<=X,(n,q)=1} mu(n)/n log(X/n) <= 1.00303 q/phi(q). Also Tao's uniform bound |sum_{n<=x,(n,P)=1} mu(n)/n| <= 1.
citation: Ramaré and Zuniga Alterman, arXiv:2312.05138, Theorem 1.2 and Lemma 4.1; Tao, arXiv:0908.4323, eq. (9).
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS §2: uniform growing-prime control of rough/smooth Möbius prefixes in the native rough state (L-98040/T-98050).
precise_next_step: Integrate the L-98040 Stieltjes transfer by parts once more in log coordinates. With l_z(t)=sum_{m<=e^t,(m,P_{<z})=1} mu(m)/m log(e^t/m), which lies in [0, 1.00303 prod_{p<z}(1-1/p)^{-1}], this gives F(Y,z)/sqrt Y = l_z(log Y)h'(0+) + int l_z(log Y - v) dh'(v). Then record exactly which sign of the second log-derivative measure of the base would give positivity, and in which (Y,z) ranges.
risk: High for the RH-bearing part. The critical information sits in l_z - K_z, which is signed and of size Y^{-1/2+eps} under RH. dh' is not one-signed when h is bounded, so positivity cannot follow from l_z>=0 alone. The tool mainly supplies uniform-in-z bounds and a cleaner bookkeeping of the base.

tool: Explicit-formula bias classification of fixed detectors (apparent/persistent bias; Ingham versus log-biased regimes).
citation: Martin-Mossinghoff-Trudgian, arXiv:2112.05227 §1 and Thm 3; Humphries, arXiv:1108.1524, Thms 1.5-1.6; Mossinghoff-Trudgian 2012.
target_gap: Sign branches of OPEN.ARITH.ROWS23_NATIVE, FCHD67 and the Bellman deep root, as distinct from their negative-mass branches (OPEN_CUTS §1).
precise_next_step: For each fixed detector (H_1; rows 2,3; the 5:3 scalar; the deep root U(Y,p) at fixed p), compute the residue at s=0 of N(s)/zeta(s+1/2) and the size of the zero coefficients. For H_1 the analyst gets b_H=1.8033 with coefficients ~1/(gamma zeta'(rho)), which is the Ingham regime. For a log-ramp row with a double pole the bias grows like log x, the Humphries alpha=1/2 regime, where the sign is plausibly RH-equivalent rather than LI-obstructed. For the deep root, if b(x)=a_*sqrt x+c_*+O(x^{-3/2}) as in L-98040.6, the RH-conditional constant term of F(Y,p) is c_*/(zeta(1/2) prod_{l<p}(1-l^{-1/2})), whose sign is -sign(c_*). Record which sign targets are expected false and which are plausibly RH-equivalent.
risk: These are conditional (RH, simple zeros, LI or Gonek-Hejhal) heuristics and classifications, not estimates. The deep-root bias formula depends on the exact base expansion and endpoint conventions, which the analyst could not check locally (c_* is not numerically given in the resident files).

tool: Haselgrove / Odlyzko-te Riele / Hurst lattice-reduction disproof template for one-sided bounds, using Ingham's Fejér-kernel inequality with finitely many zeros.
citation: Haselgrove 1958 (zbMATH 0085.27102); G. Hurst, 'Computations of the Mertens function and improved bounds on the Mertens conjecture', Math. Comp. 87 (2018), arXiv:1610.08551 (abstract: liminf M/sqrt x < -1.837625, limsup > 1.826054).
target_gap: Firewall for sign-type versions of the critical SHARP detector, so that no future route relies on 'H_1 eventually >= 0'.
precise_next_step: Compute c_rho=(1-67^{-rho})(rho+1)/(zeta'(rho)(rho-1)(rho-1/2)) for the first few thousand zeros. Use LLL/Kronecker search to find y with b_H + sum_{|gamma|<T} k(gamma/T)·2Re(c_rho y^{i gamma}) < 0. If found, then by Ingham's inequality and L-99943, 'H_1 eventually >= 0' is unconditionally false.
risk: Borderline feasibility. b_H=1.803 is just below Hurst's Mertens record 1.837, and the H_1 coefficient sums track the Mertens ones (1.674 versus 1.637 after 400 zeros). A computation may fail to produce a witness. The outcome is a firewall only and does not affect the negative-mass target.

tool: PNT-strength bounds for Möbius sums over smooth numbers (Alladi; Hildebrand's transfer inequality; VK), together with Rankin's trick.
citation: Hildebrand, Monatsh. Math. 97 (1984) 119-124; Alladi 1982; Rankin's trick (e.g. Tenenbaum §III.5); Hildebrand-Tenenbaum 1993 survey.
target_gap: §8 open item 'uniform growing-P control' for F_z(x)=sum_{d|P(z)} mu(d)A(x/d)/sqrt d.
precise_next_step: Decompose F_z = 6 sum_{(N,P(z))=1} H_x(N)/sqrt N - 6S(x) + (9/sqrt2)S(x/2) - (3/2)S(x/4), where S(y)=sum_{d|P(z)} mu(d)d^{-1/2}H_y(d). The first term is a positive rough count, about 12 sqrt x prod_{p<z}(1-1/p) by the Fundamental Lemma. Bound S(y) by partial summation from sum_{d<=t,P^+(d)<z} mu(d): Rankin/trivial bounds for u >= log log x, Hildebrand's inequality for intermediate u, and PNT/VK savings (<< t/log^A t) for bounded u and z <= x/K. This should give positivity of F_z(x) for x >= x_0(K) uniformly in z <= x/K. State explicitly that z >~ x/K turns F_z into the full critical detector. For that detector the analyst computes, under RH, a constant bias log4·(6-1.136/zeta(1/2)) ≈ 9.40 with zero coefficients O(1/(gamma^2|zeta'(rho)|)); this regime remains RH-bearing.
risk: Moderate. A uniform smooth-Möbius saving across all u must be pinned to an exact published theorem (Alladi, Hildebrand 1987, or de la Bretèche-Tenenbaum 2005, none verified here). Constants are ineffective unless explicit VK is used. The top regime z ≈ x stays open.

tool: Rubinstein-Sarnak/Ng limiting-distribution machinery.
citation: N. Ng, arXiv:math/0310381; Humphries, arXiv:1108.1524, §§3-5.
target_gap: OPEN.ARITH.CV: quantify, conditionally, what the true size of the critical negative mass is.
precise_next_step: Under RH and J_{-1}(T)<<T, adapt Ng's weak-Mertens argument to show int_1^X (H_1-b_H)^2 dx/x << log X, hence N(X) << log X. Under LI in addition, compute the logarithmic density of {H_1<0}, which should be tiny and positive. Record this as the conditional benchmark the subpower target must match.
risk: Purely conditional. It produces no unconditional progress and must never be presented as evidence for the estimate.

tool: Friedlander-Iwaniec bilinear-form (Type II) hypothesis and asymptotic-sieve combinatorics.
citation: Friedlander and Iwaniec, Ann. of Math. 148 (1998), arXiv:math/9811186, §1, hypotheses (R) and (B).
target_gap: Dynamic critical Bellman block (OPEN_CUTS §2): the parity-breaking input.
precise_next_step: State the native analogue of hypothesis (B), cancellation of sum_m sum_n alpha_m beta_n mu(mn) over a range N in (Delta^{-1}D, delta^{-1}sqrt x), for the literal rough source. Determine which Bellman descendants it would control.
risk: High. FI-type inputs give asymptotics with log-power savings, whereas the fixed-least-prime root requires RH-scale control. The tool clarifies what is missing but cannot by itself close the block.

repo_statement: Imported RH-necessity interface: under RH, Re F>0 on Re s>1/2, so all finite Pick matrices of F=xi'/xi are PSD; a strict negative Pick matrix contradicts RH (xi/derivative-free-pick-loewner.md; finite-pick-controls.md 'Relationship to RH').
literature_result: RH holds iff Re(xi'/xi)(s)>0 for every s with Re s>1/2 (Theorem 1.1). The same paper shows inf_t Re(xi'/xi)(sigma+it)=(xi'/xi)(sigma) for sigma>10, i.e. on far-right vertical lines the real axis is the minimizer.
citation: J. C. Lagarias, On a positivity property of the Riemann xi-function, Acta Arith. 89 (1999) 217-234, Thm 1.1; correction Acta Arith. 116 (2005) 293-294. Restated in Goldstein-Grigutis arXiv:2201.08599 section 1 and in Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski arXiv:1205.2773 section 2.
notes: Already cited by the repo. The inf-over-t statement for sigma>10 (extended by Garunkstis to zero-free half-planes) is relevant to choosing the real s-axis as the 'safe axis'.

verification.evidence: zbMATH Zbl 0928.11035 (Acta Arith. 89 (1999) 217-234) review: RH is equivalent to Re(xi'/xi)>0 on Re s>1/2 by logarithmic differentiation of the product. Thm 1.1 generalizes this to a product class. Thm 1.3 proves, under RH, Re(xi'/xi)(sigma+it) >= (xi'/xi)(sigma) for every sigma>1/2. Thm 1.2 proves the same inequality unconditionally for xi_K when sigma >= 1+9 n_K^{-1/3}, which is sigma>=10 for Q. The Garunkstis review (Zbl 1026.11070, Lith. Math. J. 42 (2002) 140-145) confirms 'sigma>10' unconditionally and extends it to any zero-free half-plane sigma>a. Goldstein-Grigutis (2201.08599, section 1) and MSZ (1205.2773, section 2) restate both results. Repo derivative-free-pick-loewner.md imports Thm 1.1 together with the 2005 correction.
verification.correction: 'identical' holds only for the scalar interface (Re F>0 on Re s>1/2 iff RH). The further step 'so all finite Pick matrices (F(s_i)+conj F(s_j))/(s_i+conj s_j-1) are PSD' is the classical Caratheodory/Nevanlinna-Pick consequence, which Hinkkanen 1997 uses. It is not part of Lagarias Thm 1.1, so for the matrix statement the relation is 'standard consequence / repo_is_special_case'. Attribute the inf-at-t=0 result precisely: unconditional for sigma>10 (via Thm 1.2 with K=Q; Garunkstis 2002 extends it to zero-free half-planes, including sigma>=1), and conditional on RH for all sigma>1/2 (Thm 1.3). Evidence can be upgraded from secondary_source to zbMATH review.

repo_statement: Finite Pick-matrix RH criterion (complex Pick boxes; all-order real-node criterion L-91904 / OPEN.OPERATOR.XI.PICK_ORDER4_PLUS).
literature_result: Using the classical Pick interpolation theorem, RH is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of an explicit sequence of matrices A_n, n=1,2,... (zbMATH review). MSZ 2014 credits the same paper with the equivalence RH <=> Re(xi'/xi)>0 on sigma>1/2, which predates Lagarias 1999.
citation: A. Hinkkanen, On functions of bounded type, Complex Variables Theory Appl. 34 (1997) 119-139, DOI 10.1080/17476939708815042; zbMATH 0905.30027 (review by A. F. Grishin); cited in arXiv:1205.2773 ref [7].
notes: I could not read the paper, so I cannot confirm that Hinkkanen's A_n are the repo's K_ij at the same nodes and normalization. The repo does not cite Hinkkanen. This is the earliest Pick-matrix RH criterion for xi I found.

verification.evidence: zbMATH 0905.30027 (Complex Variables Theory Appl. 34 (1997), no. 1-2, 119-139) review: 'Using the classic interpolation Pick theorem, the author proves that the hypothesis of Riemann is equivalent to the statement that the special matrix A_n, n=1,2,..., defined by him is positive semi-definite.' MSZ 1205.2773 section 2 (ref [7]) says Re(xi'/xi)>0 for sigma>1, and its RH-equivalence for sigma>1/2, 'also appears in the 1999 paper of Lagarias [9] and the 1997 paper of Hinkkanen [7]'. Goldstein-Grigutis cite Hinkkanen for the sigma>1 statement. Grep of the repo finds no citation of Hinkkanen. I could not read the paper or check the DOI, so whether A_n equals the repo's K_ij remains unverified. The cautious 'closely_analogous' label is appropriate.

repo_statement: R_T(x)=Re(xi'/xi)(1/2+x+iT)>=0 is the scalar base of the secant, divided-difference and Pick tests; R_T(x)=d/dx log|xi(1/2+x+iT)|.
literature_result: Thm 1: |xi| is strictly increasing along every horizontal half-line in any zero-free open right half-plane. Cor 1: RH holds iff, for each fixed t, |xi(sigma+it)| is increasing on 1/2<sigma<inf (equivalently, decreasing on sigma<1/2). MSZ 2014 give a one-line proof via Re(f'/f) and note Polya 1927 (Jensen condition I': d^2/dy^2|xi(1/2+y+ix)|^2>=0) as an anticipation.
citation: J. Sondow, C. Dumitrescu, A monotonicity property of Riemann's xi function and a reformulation of the Riemann Hypothesis, Period. Math. Hungar. 60 (2010) 37-40, arXiv:1005.1104, Thm 1 and Cor 1; Y. Matiyasevich, F. Saidak, P. Zvengrowski, Horizontal monotonicity of the modulus of the zeta function, L-functions and related functions, Acta Arith. 166 (2014), arXiv:1205.2773, Thms 1.1, 1.3, 1.4 and Cor 2.5.
notes: Equivalent at the scalar (order-one) level: 'R_T(x)>0 for all x>0 and all T' is the same as Sondow-Dumitrescu Cor 1(i). The repo's higher-order tests strengthen it. MSZ Thm 1.4 is an unconditional sigma<=0, |t|>=8 monotonicity result for zeta, eta and xi.

verification.evidence: Full text of 1005.1104: Theorem 1 (xi strictly increasing in modulus on horizontal half-lines in any zero-free open right half-plane) and Corollary 1 ((i) increasing for 1/2<sigma<inf for each t; (ii) decreasing for sigma<1/2; (iii) RH, all equivalent). Period. Math. Hungar. 60 (2010) 37-40 is confirmed by Zbl 1218.11079, whose review notes the RH-conditional version is Montgomery-Vaughan Exercise 13.2.1(e). MSZ full text: Thm 1.3 (|t|>=8, sigma<1/2 inequality chain), Thm 1.4 (eta, zeta, xi decreasing in sigma<=0, |t|>=8, unconditional), Cor 2.5, and the Polya 1927 condition I' (d^2/dy^2|xi(1/2+y+ix)|^2>=0) as an anticipation. Acta Arith. 166 (2014) 189-200 is confirmed by Zbl 1319.11055. R_T(x)=d/dx log|xi(1/2+x+iT)| holds because Re f'/f is the sigma-derivative of log|f|.

repo_statement: Real-node safe-axis matrix H_ij=(F(x_i)+F(x_j))/(x_i+x_j), F=Xi'/Xi on (0,inf) (ORDER_THREE_CANONICAL.md; X8). All-order positivity is RH-equivalent (L-91904). Order-3 determinant factorization into [.](1/p) and [.](tp) (L-92000); 'reciprocal Loewner-Hankel congruence' (OPERATOR.XI.LOEWNER_LOW_ORDER).
literature_result: H_ij is exactly the 'anti-Loewner' (Kwong) matrix K_g of g=F. Thm 2.1: if g is anti-Loewner of order 2N on (a,b), then x->sqrt(x) g(sqrt x) is matrix monotone of order N and x->g(sqrt x)/sqrt(x) is matrix monotone decreasing of order N on (a^2,b^2). The proof rests on exact identities: K_g+L_g equals 2 times the Loewner matrix of sqrt(x)g(sqrt x) at the points x_i^2, and K_g-L_g equals -2 D L[g(sqrt x)/sqrt x] D. Corollary (eq. 2): g is anti-Loewner of all orders on (0,inf) iff g(x)=alpha/x+beta x+Integral x/(t+x^2) dmu(t) with mu>=0. Prop 2 and Thm 2.2: the sign of det[(s_i g_i+s_j g_j)/(s_i x_i+s_j x_j)] does not depend on the signs s_i. Kwong 1989 had proved sufficiency for nonnegative operator monotone functions.
citation: K. M. R. Audenaert, A characterisation of anti-Loewner functions, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 139 (2011) 4217-4223, arXiv:1008.2943, Thm 2.1, Thm 2.2, Prop 2, eq. (2); M. K. Kwong, Some results on matrix monotone functions, Linear Algebra Appl. 118 (1989) 129-153.
notes: With g=F, sqrt(t)F(sqrt t)=t p(t) and F(sqrt t)/sqrt t=p(t). The all-order criterion is therefore Audenaert's representation (2) with alpha=beta=0 and mu=Sum 2m delta_{gamma^2}, plus the identity theorem. Audenaert gives an exact order-transfer: Pick order 2N implies tp N-monotone and p N-monotone decreasing. He states that sufficiency at fixed N is open. The repo's 3x3 factorization is consistent with this framework, but I found no literature statement of that factorization.

verification.evidence: Full text of arXiv:1008.2943v2 read; PAMS 139 (2011) 4217-4223 confirmed by Zbl 1298.15030. Thm 2.1: anti-Loewner of order 2N on (a,b) implies sqrt(x)g(sqrt x) is N-monotone and g(sqrt x)/sqrt x is N-monotone decreasing on (a^2,b^2). Eq. (2) gives the all-order representation alpha/x+beta x+Integral x/(t+x^2)dmu. Prop 2 and Thm 2.2 give sign-independence and its block form. Eq. (3) is the partial elimination X=DYD. The proof of Thm 2.1 displays exactly the K+L and K-L identities quoted, and I re-derived both algebraically. Kwong, LAA 118 (1989) 129-153 (Zbl 0679.15026), is credited for sufficiency for nonnegative operator monotone f. In repo notation, x p(x^2)=F(x), so X8's K_ij is literally K_g with g=F. Under RH, F(x)=Sum 2m x/(x^2+gamma^2), which is eq. (2) with alpha=beta=0 and mu=Sum 2m delta_{gamma^2}. I also checked the repo's 3x3 factorization (X8.2) exactly in rational arithmetic on random triples: it holds.
verification.correction: 'repo_is_special_case' applies only to the all-order criterion L-91904 / PICK_ORDER4_PLUS taken over all orders. The order-3 determinant factorization (L-92000) and the 'reciprocal Loewner-Hankel congruence' are not in Audenaert. For those the relation is at most 'consistent with / complementary to' his fixed-N order transfer. Audenaert does not literally say sufficiency at fixed N is 'open'. He writes that there 'seems to be no obvious approach even to the sufficiency part in the more general setting of fixed N'. The repo's canonical safe nodes are x_i>1/2, not (0,inf). Thm 2.1 still applies on (1/2,inf), but the all-order equivalence then goes through Loewner's theorem on (1/4,inf) plus analytic continuation, not through eq. (2) directly.

repo_statement: Derivative-free packet sections 2-3: alternating divided differences of J_T, and total nonnegativity of cross-Loewner minors (Cauchy-Binet plus Cauchy determinants).
literature_result: Under RH, J_T(u)=Sum u/(u+a_gamma) is a complete Bernstein (operator monotone) function on (0,inf) and H_T=J_T/u is a Stieltjes function. Divided differences of Bernstein functions alternate in sign. The Loewner kernel Integral a/((u+a)(v+a))dmu(a) is a composition of the strictly totally positive Cauchy kernel 1/(x+y), so it is TP by Karlin's basic composition formula.
citation: R. L. Schilling, R. Song, Z. Vondracek, Bernstein Functions, 2nd ed., de Gruyter 2012, Chs. 3, 6, 7; S. Karlin, Total Positivity Vol. I, Stanford 1968, Ch. 3 (basic composition formula) and Cauchy determinant; K. Loewner, Math. Z. 38 (1934).
notes: The algebra is classical once the resolvent representation is granted. Sra 2026 cites Schilling-Song-Vondracek for the CBF and Stieltjes facts used here. What appears new in the repo is the packaging as finite directed disproof witnesses (barycentric localizers, matched-pole annihilator), not the inequalities themselves.

verification.evidence: I checked the mathematics directly. [u_0..u_n](u/(u+a)) = (-1)^{n-1}a/prod(u_k+a). Bernstein functions have (-1)^{n-1}f^(n)>=0, so the mean-value form of divided differences gives alternating signs. Sum u/(u+a) has the complete Bernstein form lambda/(lambda+t). Integral a/((u+a)(v+a))dmu = P C Q^T with Cauchy kernels, so Cauchy-Binet plus Cauchy determinants give total nonnegativity, which is exactly the repo's proof in derivative-free-pick-loewner.md sections 2-3. Sra 2611.02944 (section 2.3, Prop A.1) cites Schilling-Song-Vondracek Chs. 3 and 6 for the Bernstein/CBF facts. The textbooks themselves were not opened.
verification.correction: In SSV 2nd ed. (de Gruyter Studies in Math. 37, 2012), Stieltjes functions are Ch. 2. Bernstein functions are Ch. 3 and complete Bernstein functions Chs. 6-7, so the H_T Stieltjes claim should cite Ch. 2. Full Loewner citation: Math. Z. 38 (1934) 177-216. The Karlin chapter number for the basic composition formula is unverified. Evidence remains textbook-level (not opened), but the mathematical content is verified.

repo_statement: Critical-reserve budget and low-order safe-axis positivity: Sum_{b_i>H} m_i/b_i^2<=2(log H+1)/H from N_+(T)<=T log T, H=3000175332800 (Platt-Trudgian); one low critical orbit absorbs every off-line contribution (L-92101/L-92102, X3/X5).
literature_result: Lemma 2.2 ('one retained real zero') and eq. (2.2): N(Y)<=Y log Y for Y>=U and Sum_{gamma>U} gamma^-2<=2(log U+1)/U<1 for U>=100. One low real zero (q=gamma_1^2) dominates all tail oscillations, giving H(t)>0 and -H'(t)>0 for all t>0 unconditionally (Thm 1.1, using zeros only through height 100). Thm 1.2 then gives Theta and Lambda in PF_{k*} with k*=1,810,540,931,075, using U_PT=3000175332800. Polson 2026 (arXiv:1804.10043v9) independently proves W(t)=(1/2)Sum exp{(rho-1/2)^2 t} positive and strictly decreasing.
citation: S. Sra, On some positivity properties of the Riemann Xi function, arXiv:2611.02944v1 (2 Nov 2026), Lemma 2.2, eq. (2.2), Thm 1.1, Prop 2.3, Thm 1.2, Thm 3.4; N. G. Polson, arXiv:1804.10043v9 (17 Sep 2026) abstract, and arXiv:1708.02653v24 Prop 6.5 (as described by Sra section 2.2).
notes: The tail budget is identical in form, and the input (Platt-Trudgian height 3000175332800) is identical. The repo's xi_pick integration (2026-08-22) predates Sra v1 (Nov 2026; author commit 11 Sep 2026) and Polson v24/v9 (Sep 2026), so this is parallel work, not prior art in the priority sense. I derived the following myself; Sra does not state it. Since p=2*Integral e^{-su}H(u)du, H>0 gives p'<0. H'<0 gives (sp)'=-2*Integral u e^{-su}H'(u)du>0 (boundary term uH(u)->0 because H is positive, decreasing and integrable) and (sp)''=2*Integral u^2 e^{-su}H'(u)du<0. So Sra/Polson Thm 1.1 implies the repo's order-2 Pick theorem (PSD, indeed strict for distinct nodes) and the tp-curvature half of order 3 (L-92001), using only zeros up to height 100. It does NOT imply reciprocal concavity pp''-2p'^2>=0: positive decreasing H=1_[0,1] gives 1/p proportional to s/(1-e^-s), which is convex.

verification.evidence: Full text of arXiv:2611.02944v1 (2 Nov 2026) read. Lemma 2.2 retains one zero q=gamma_1^2 in (196,225) with U>=100. Eq. (2.2) gives N(Y)<=Y log Y and Sum_{gamma>U} gamma^-2 <= 2(log U+1)/U < 1. Thm 1.1 gives H>0 and H'<0 using zeros through height 100. Prop 2.3 gives B'(s)=Integral e^{-st}H(t)dt with H(t)=Sum_{Z+} e^{-t(gamma-i delta)^2}. Thm 1.2 gives k*=1,810,540,931,075 with U_PT=3,000,175,332,800. Thm 3.4 is confirmed. The footnote records the author's commit eae8e7e0154b on 11 Sep 2026. Polson 1804.10043v9 (17 Sep 2026) abstract: 'For xi we prove, unconditionally, that the heat trace W(t)=(1/2)Sum exp{(rho-1/2)^2 t} is positive and strictly decreasing'. The repo xi_pick integration commit 75796e7 is dated 2026-08-22. I re-derived the bridge's implication: p=2B', (sp)'=-2Integral u e^{-su}H'(u)du>0, and (sp)''=2Integral u^2 e^{-su}H'(u)du<0. With X8.1 this gives strict order-2 positivity and the tp-concavity half of order 3. The H=1_[0,1] example gives 1/p proportional to s/(1-e^{-s}), which is convex, so reciprocal concavity is not implied. A small positive smooth perturbation keeps H>0 strictly decreasing.

Sra's Lemma 2.2 controls oscillation of e^{-t lambda_rho} in the Laplace/time variable through the delay e^{-gamma} (Sum e^{-gamma}<U^2 e^{-U}). The repo allocates constant curvature shares epsilon_i ~ 9m_i/b_i^2 of R in the s-variable. 'Closely_analogous' is right, but the novelty_assessment's 'mechanism is the same' overstates it.
