repo_statement: OPEN.OPERATOR.XI.PICK_ORDER4_PLUS / L-91904: all-order safe-axis Pick positivity is RH-equivalent.
literature_result: Prop A.1: RH <=> H completely monotone <=> H(t)/t^alpha completely monotone <=> [H(u_i+u_j)] PSD in every size <=> B=log h is a complete Bernstein function <=> Theta in PF_inf <=> Lambda in PF_inf. Zhang (2023, Lemma 3): RH <=> complete monotonicity of H. Zhang's abstract also gives a Widder-type criterion: f has only negative zeros iff order <1, the root sequence is real-part dominating, and (-1/x)^m d^k/dx^k(x^{k+m} d^m/dx^m(f'/f)) is completely monotone on (0,inf) for all k. Grochenig 2020 gives the Schoenberg PF_inf form.
citation: S. Sra arXiv:2611.02944 Prop A.1; R. Zhang, On certain genus 0 entire functions, arXiv:2206.05104v8 (2023), Lemma 3 and abstract; K. Grochenig, Schoenberg's theory of totally positive functions and the Riemann zeta function, arXiv:2007.12889 (2020); N. G. Polson arXiv:1804.10043v9 Thm 26.
notes: Sra's text read in full; Zhang and Grochenig at abstract level. Because p=2B', B in CBF <=> p Stieltjes <=> (Audenaert) Kwong matrices of F PSD in all orders. These are the same RH-equivalent property of the same function h=G/G(0), so the hypotheses match. The repo's all-order criterion is therefore known in at least three equivalent forms.

verification.evidence: Sra Prop A.1 (full text) lists (i) RH, (ii) H CM, (iii)-(iv) H/t^alpha CM, (v) [H(u_i+u_j)] PSD in every size, (vi) B in CBF, (vii) Theta in PF_inf, (viii) Lambda in PF_inf. Sra section 5.4 states that 'The equivalence of RH with complete monotonicity of H is a special case of Zhang (2023, v8, Lemma 3)' and cites Polson 1804.10043v9 Thm 26. Zhang 2206.05104v8 full text: Lemma 3 (lambda_n positive iff Sum e^{-lambda_n t} CM, under order<1 and real-part domination) and the abstract criterion with 'there exists a nonnegative integer m'. Polson v9 has Thm 26, 'The Riemann hypothesis as complete monotonicity'. Grochenig 2007.12889 abstract confirms an RH-equivalent condition from Schoenberg's theory (published in a Birkhauser 2024 volume, pp. 193-210).
verification.correction: 'B in CBF <=> p Stieltjes' is not an abstract equivalence. p=2B' Stieltjes implies B-B(0) is CBF, but a CBF need not have a Stieltjes derivative (B(lambda)=lambda/(1+lambda) gives B'=1/(1+lambda)^2). For this particular h, both are separately RH-equivalent, so the chain is valid only through RH. With that caveat, the link to all-order Kwong positivity (via Audenaert eq. (2): g anti-Loewner of all orders iff g(sqrt t)/sqrt t is Stieltjes) and the 'equivalent_reformulation' label are correct. Zhang's criterion needs 'for some m', and his Thm 1 assumes order<1 and real-part domination as hypotheses.

repo_statement: Order-2 and order-3 unconditional safe-axis positivity for actual xi; first open order is four.
literature_result: For the same G (GORZ eq. (1): (-1+4z^2)Lambda(1/2+z)=Sum gamma(n) z^{2n}/n!, i.e. 8 xi(1/2+z)), the Jensen polynomials J^{d,n} are hyperbolic for all n when d<=8 (GORZ Thm 2) and for n>=N(d) for every d (Thm 1). d=2 is Csordas-Norfolk-Varga (Turan inequalities via log-concavity of K(t)=Integral_t^inf Phi(sqrt u)du). d=3 is Dimitrov-Lucas (higher-order Turan). Chasse proved J^{d,0} hyperbolic for d<=2*10^17.
citation: M. Griffin, K. Ono, L. Rolen, D. Zagier, Jensen polynomials for the Riemann zeta function and other sequences, PNAS 116 (2019) 11103-11110, arXiv:1902.07321, Thms 1-2 and footnote 1; G. Csordas, T. S. Norfolk, R. S. Varga, Trans. AMS 296 (1986) 521-541 (zbMATH 0602.30030); D. K. Dimitrov, F. R. Lucas, Proc. AMS 139 (2011) 1013-1022 (zbMATH 1214.11092); M. Chasse, Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. 58 (2013) 875-885.
notes: Same function, different finite truncation of the same RH-equivalent property (G in Laguerre-Polya with negative zeros). Jensen tests use Taylor coefficients at t=0 (s=1/2); the repo's tests use Kwong/Loewner matrices of G'/G on t>0. No implication between the hierarchies is known to me. The Jensen hierarchy is unconditionally known at d<=8 (all shifts), well beyond the repo's order 3. CNV and Dimitrov-Lucas are verified from zbMATH reviews only.

verification.evidence: Full text of GORZ arXiv:1902.07321. Eq. (1) is (-1+4z^2)Lambda(1/2+z)=Sum gamma(n)z^{2n}/n!. Thm 1 (d>=1, hyperbolic for n large), Thm 2 (1<=d<=8, every n>=0), and footnote 1 ('hyperbolicity for J^{d,0} has been confirmed for d <= 2*10^17 by Chasse (Theorem 1.8 of [4])'). The text adds that d<=3 was previously known (CNV; Dimitrov-Lucas). I checked algebraically that (4z^2-1)Lambda(1/2+z)=8xi(1/2+z)=8G(z^2). Zbl 0602.30030 (CNV, Trans. AMS 296 (1986) 521-541) proves the Turan inequalities by strict log-concavity of K(t)=Integral_t^inf Phi(sqrt u)du. Zbl 1214.11092 (Dimitrov-Lucas, PAMS 139 (2011) 1013-1022) covers degree 3. Zbl 1291.30032 (Chasse, CVEE 58 (2013)) covers degree up to about 10^17.

repo_statement: High-derivative entry: Xi^(m) has only real simple zeros in |Re z|<=c sqrt(m/log m), |Im z|<=H (F02). The older fixed-rectangle normalized conclusion is also recovered.
literature_result: Kim (1996): if f is real entire of order <2 with all zeros in a strip |Im z|<A, then for each fixed R, f^(n) has only real zeros in |z|<R for all large n. This applies to Xi unconditionally. Ki (2006): there are A_n and C_n->0 with A_n Xi^(2n)(C_n z)->cos z uniformly on compacts, as conjectured by Farmer-Rhoades. Conrey (1983): a proportion 1-O(n^-2) of the zeros of Xi^(n) are real.
citation: Y.-O. Kim, Critical points of real entire functions and a conjecture of Polya, Proc. AMS 124 (1996) 819-829 (stated in Farmer arXiv:2008.07206 section 2); H. Ki, The Riemann Xi-function under repeated differentiation, J. Number Theory 120 (2006) 120-131 (zbMATH 1217.11075); J. B. Conrey, Zeros of derivatives of Riemann's xi-function on the critical line, J. Number Theory 16 (1983) 49-74 (as summarized in Farmer section 2); D. W. Farmer, R. C. Rhoades, Trans. AMS 357 (2005) 3789-3811, arXiv:math/0310252.
notes: For the specific function Xi the repo's window is growing (|Re z| up to c sqrt(m/log m)), whereas Kim gives fixed R and Ki's window shrinks (C_n->0). The repo result is therefore a quantitative strengthening for Xi; its fixed-rectangle corollary is a special case of Kim 1996. Novelty of the exact sqrt(m/log m) window is uncertain: O'Sullivan arXiv:2007.13582 and Coffey (Math. Comp. 2009) give detailed asymptotics that may already contain it. I did not read those in full.

verification.evidence: Farmer 2008.07206 section 2 (full text) states Kim's theorem: real entire of order <2 with zeros in |Im z|<A implies f^(n) has only real zeros in |z|<R for n large. Farmer notes it applies to Xi, which has zeros in |Im|<1/2. Ki's theorem is Zbl 1217.11075, JNT 120 (2006) 120-131: C_n->0 and A_n Xi^(2n)(C_n z)->cos z on compacts. Farmer also gives Conrey's 100-O(1/n^2) percent and Farmer-Rhoades (math/0310252). The repo's F02 window is |Re z|<=c/a with a^2 ~ w/(2m) and w ~ (1/2)log m, i.e. c sqrt(m/log m), with fixed H. Ki's window in the original variable is C_n R, which contains only a bounded number of zeros for fixed R.
verification.correction: Kim, Proc. AMS 124 (1996) is 819-830 per zbMATH 0848.30019 (Farmer prints 819-829). Farmer adds that Ki's theorem 'also follows from a proposition of Coffey [5]' (Math. Comp. 2009). The repo's window is the natural saddle-point scale (1/a) of the Ki/Coffey analysis, so 'repo_stronger' is fair as a quantitative statement for Xi, but novelty should stay hedged until Coffey 2009 and O'Sullivan 2020 are read. Kim's statement is verified only through Farmer's summary.

repo_statement: Fifth-derivative Conrey trial: phi(x)=1-x, m=5 gives F<e^{1/50}, hence alpha_5>49/50 conditional on the published Conrey functional (S04).
literature_result: Conrey 1983 proves, by Levinson's method applied to xi^(m), that a proportion alpha_m=1-O(m^-2) of the zeros of xi^(m) lie on the critical line, with explicit numerical proportions for small m.
citation: J. B. Conrey, J. Number Theory 16 (1983) 49-74 (zbMATH 0502.10022; content as summarized in Farmer arXiv:2008.07206 section 2).
notes: The repo replays one trial evaluation inside Conrey's framework; the analytic input remains Conrey's. The repo notes that Conrey's optimized 0.9970 input must not be swapped for this weaker trial without re-budgeting. I could not access Conrey's original table to cross-check alpha_5.

verification.evidence: Zbl 0502.10022 confirms Conrey, J. Number Theory 16 (1983) 49-74 (no review text available). Farmer section 2 states Conrey's result that Xi^(n) has (100-O(1/n^2)) percent of its zeros real. Repo S04 replays a finite trial phi(x)=1-x, m=5 with F<e^{1/50}. It says the conclusion alpha_5>49/50 is conditional on Conrey's functional, and that the stronger 'optimized 0.9970 input' must not be replaced by this 0.98 result.
verification.correction: The 'explicit numerical proportions for small m' were not verified. By the repo's own S04 account, the published optimized fifth-derivative input (0.9970) is stronger than the repo's 0.98 trial. The relation is better described as 'repo re-evaluates a weaker instance inside Conrey's framework' (repo_weaker / special case) than as 'partial_overlap'.

repo_statement: Reverse-Rolle identity (F01): N_nr(p)-N_nr(p')=2E(p) for real polynomials, where E counts wrong-sign interior extrema; plus the corrected Bezoutian inertia.
literature_result: Fourier-Polya critical-point counting. A 'critical point' of f^(l) is a real zero of f^(l) at which f^(l-1)f^(l+1)>0 (a positive minimum or negative maximum of f^(l-1)). Polya (1930) conjectured that a real entire function of genus 0 has exactly as many critical points (over all derivatives) as pairs of nonreal zeros. Ki-Kim (2000) proved this Fourier-Polya conjecture and gave a new proof of the Polya-Wiman theorem (Craven-Csordas-Smith 1987). Kim (1996) proved it under strip and order conditions.
citation: H. Ki, Y.-O. Kim, On the number of nonreal zeros of real entire functions and the Fourier-Polya conjecture, Duke Math. J. 104 (2000) 45-73 (zbMATH 0957.30019 review); Y.-O. Kim, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 204 (1996) 472-481 and Proc. AMS 124 (1996) 819-830; T. Craven, G. Csordas, W. Smith, Ann. of Math. 125 (1987) 405-431; G. Polya, Quart. J. Math. 1 (1930) 21-34.
notes: Summed over derivative orders, the one-step polynomial identity gives the Fourier-Polya total count. E(p) is exactly a violation of the first Laguerre inequality at a critical point. Kim's strip theorem needs the convergence exponent of the nonreal zeros to be <1-rho/2 (=1/2 for Xi), so it does not cover Xi with dense hypothetical off-line zeros. The entire-function extension is the hard part.

verification.evidence: zbMATH reviews. Zbl 0957.30019: Ki-Kim, Duke Math. J. 104 (2000) 45-73, gives a new proof of Polya-Wiman and proves the Fourier-Polya conjecture (Thm 4.1, with extensions 4.2-4.3); Fourier-Polya says a real entire function of genus 0 has as many critical points as couples of nonreal zeros. Zbl 0848.30019: Kim, PAMS 124 (1996) 819-830, proves it under order <=2/3 plus zeros in a strip; per the JMAA review, it also proves it for zeros in a strip with convergence exponent of nonreal zeros <1-rho/2. Zbl 0870.30023: Kim, JMAA 204 (1996) 472-481, removes the exponent condition for genus 0 with zeros in a strip. Zbl 0625.30036 confirms Craven-Csordas-Smith, Ann. Math. 125 (1987) 405-431. I checked the repo's polynomial identity on x^2+1 and x^4+x^2+1, and in general it follows from r=k+1-2E for simple critical points.
verification.correction: The note understates Ki-Kim 2000. The Fourier-Polya conjecture is proved for every real entire function of genus 0, with no strip or convergence-exponent hypothesis, so 'the entire-function extension is the hard part' is already done in genus 0. Xi is genus 1, so it is not covered directly. However, h(s)=xi(1/2+sqrt s)/c0 is real entire of order 1/2 (genus 0), so Ki-Kim applies to h unconditionally: #nonreal zeros of h = 2 x #(Fourier critical points of h and its s-derivatives), i.e. RH iff h has no critical points. This is in the s-variable, not the z-derivatives Xi^(m) of the repo's descent. For polynomials, N_nr(p)-N_nr(p')=2E(p) is the classical one-step Fourier count (E(p)=K(p') in Kim's notation), so the relation is closer to 'identical/classical' than 'partial_overlap'. The corrected Bezoutian inertia is the classical Hermite/Krein-Naimark inertia theorem: each real pole contributes the sign of its residue and each conjugate pair contributes one negative square. This prior art was missed.

repo_statement: Derivative-descent framing: a high-order Hermite-Biehler-type entry (safe-ray E_{r,lambda}) that must be transported down to xi; 'raw xi innerness may already imply RH'.
literature_result: Lemma 6.1: E_h(z)=xi(1/2+h-iz) is a de Branges (Hermite-Biehler) structure function unconditionally for h>=1/2, and for every h!=0 under RH. The averaged and differenced functions A_h, B_h=(xi(s+h)-+xi(s-h))/(2 or 2i) then have only real, simple, interlacing zeros whose normalized spacings tend to 1. Lagarias 2006 builds de Branges spaces that exist iff RH holds for the given L-function.
citation: J. C. Lagarias, Zero spacing distributions for differenced L-functions, Acta Arith. 120 (2005) 159-184, arXiv:math/0601653, Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.2 (de Branges 1959 Lemma 5), Thm 2.1, Lemma 6.1; J. C. Lagarias, Hilbert spaces of entire functions and Dirichlet L-functions, in Frontiers in Number Theory, Physics and Geometry I, Springer 2006, 365-377 (as summarized in the 2005 paper section 6).
notes: This is a shift ('differencing') analogue of the repo's derivative entry: an unconditional Hermite-Biehler regime at h>=1/2, and descent h->0 is RH. Since B_h/h -> xi' as h->0, the two families meet at small h. Innerness of E_h^#/E_h for all h>0 is RH-equivalent, which matches the repo's warning about raw innerness.

verification.evidence: Full text of math/0601653v2; Acta Arith. 120 (2005) 159-184 confirmed by Zbl 1120.11037. Abstract: A_h, B_h have only simple zeros on the critical line for |h|>=1/2 (all h!=0 under RH), with normalized spacings tending to 1. Lemma 2.1(1) h>=1/2 unconditional, (2) h>0 under RH. Lemma 2.2 is de Branges [1, Lemma 5]. Thm 2.1 is confirmed. Lemma 6.1: (i) E_h(z)=xi(1/2+h-iz) is a de Branges structure function for h>=1/2; (ii) under RH, for all h!=0. Section 6: the Lagarias 2006 Frontiers paper (ref [16]) gives a de Branges space that 'exists if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds for the corresponding L-function'. Section 6 also cites Conrey-Li on the failure of de Branges's conditions.
verification.correction: Minor: B_h/h tends to -i xi' (B_h=(xi(s+h)-xi(s-h))/(2i)), not xi'. This does not affect the analogy.

repo_statement: Witness-basin geometry: a hypothetical off-line zero creates open regions of negative secant, Pick or channel values; finite positive boxes exclude only themselves.
literature_result: These papers give explicit lower bounds for the critical-zero sum Re Sum_{rho on line} 1/(s-rho), for 1/2<sigma<1 and large t (2022) and for 1/2+1/sqrt(log t)<sigma<1 (2025). Assuming hypothetical off-line zeros, they map the regions where Re(xi'/xi) could still be positive or turn negative.
citation: E. Goldstein, A. Grigutis, On a positivity property of the real part of logarithmic derivative of the Riemann xi-function, arXiv:2201.08599 (2022); A. Grigutis, L. Turcinskas, Note on the positivity of the real part of the log-derivative of the Riemann xi-function near the critical line, arXiv:2509.18963 (2025).
notes: Scalar (order-one) analogue of the repo's finite witness-basin geometry. I read only the introduction and statement sections. Neither paper uses Pick or Loewner matrices.

verification.evidence: 2201.08599 abstract and Thm 4: explicit upper and lower bounds for Re Sum_{rho on line} 1/(s-rho) for 1/2<sigma<1 and large t, plus positivity checks assuming off-line zeros. 2509.18963 abstract: the same in the region 1/2+1/sqrt(log t)<sigma<1. Neither uses Pick or Loewner matrices. 'Scalar analogue of witness geometry' is a fair description. 'closely_analogous' is generous, since these papers map scalar positivity regions rather than negative higher-order basins, but it is acceptable with the stated caveat.

repo_statement: Complex-center Li coefficients refuted; a replacement generalized Li theorem would need a real symmetrized generating function (proof-boundary-corrections.md section 4).
literature_result: For any real a!=1/2, RH holds iff the sums k_{n,a}=Sum_rho [1-((rho-a)/(rho+a-1))^n] are all >=0, equivalently iff certain derivatives of (z-a)^(n-1) log xi(z) at z=1-a have a fixed sign. Bombieri-Lagarias give the multiset version. Sekatskii 2014 also shows that for each n there is b_n such that the first n generalized Li inequalities hold unconditionally for every center b>b_n.
citation: S. K. Sekatskii, Generalized Bombieri-Lagarias' theorem and generalized Li's criterion, Ukrainian Math. J. 66 (2014) 371-383, arXiv:1304.7895; S. K. Sekatskii, arXiv:1404.7276; E. Bombieri, J. C. Lagarias, Complements to Li's criterion for the Riemann hypothesis, J. Number Theory 77 (1999) 274-287; X.-J. Li, J. Number Theory 65 (1997); J. B. Keiper, Math. Comp. 58 (1992).
notes: This supplies the real-center (v=0) generalized Li theorem the repo says is missing. A complex-center symmetrized version is not covered by these abstracts. Sekatskii's unconditional finite-order result at far real centers is another instance of 'low-order positivity on the safe axis'.

verification.evidence: 1304.7895 abstract: the sums k_{n,a}=Sum_rho (1-((rho-a)/(rho+a-1))^n) are nonnegative for any real a!=1/2, as are the derivatives of (z-a)^{n-1} ln xi(z) at z=1-a for a<1/2 (nonpositive for a>1/2), iff RH. The generalized Bombieri-Lagarias theorem is also included. 1404.7276 abstract: for any n there is b_n such that for all m<=n and b>b_n the inequalities hold unconditionally. Zbl 0972.11079 confirms Bombieri-Lagarias, JNT 77 (1999) 274-287. The repo's proof-boundary-corrections.md section 4 refutes the complex-center (v!=0) family. Its map s(z)=1/2+(a+conj(a)z)/(1-z) with v=0 is exactly Sekatskii's real-center Mobius map with a=1/2+u.
verification.correction: The English version is Ukrainian Math. J. 66 (2014) 415-431 (Zbl 1352.11080); 371-383 is the Ukr. Mat. Zh. pagination. The repo does not say a real-center theorem is missing. It says a replacement for the refuted complex-center coefficients would need a real symmetrized generating function. Sekatskii supplies only the v=0 specialization, which is classical in form, and does not address the refuted object. Related missed items: Freitas, J. London Math. Soc. 73 (2006) 399-414 (Li-type criteria for zero-free half-planes) and F. Brown, JNT 2005.

repo_statement: F13: the negative index of the Nevanlinna kernel of -f'/f equals the number of distinct nonreal zero locations; (z^2+1)^m has index one.
literature_result: Krein-Langer theory of generalized Nevanlinna functions N_kappa. A meromorphic function belongs to N_kappa iff its Nevanlinna kernel has kappa negative squares; for real entire f, -f'/f is in N_kappa with kappa the number of distinct nonreal zero pairs. For analytic kernels the negative-square count is the same on any open subset of the holomorphy domain.
citation: M. G. Krein, H. Langer, Uber einige Fortsetzungsprobleme ... I, Math. Nachr. 77 (1977) 187-236; D. Alpay, A. Dijksma, J. Rovnyak, H. de Snoo, Schur Functions, Operator Colligations, and Reproducing Kernel Pontryagin Spaces, OT 96, Birkhauser 1997, Ch. 1.
notes: Not verified from full text this session. If confirmed, it also explains why the real-node safe-axis hierarchy is all-order RH-equivalent: a negative square cannot hide from a uniqueness set.

verification.evidence: Both citations exist: Krein-Langer, Math. Nachr. 77 (1977) 187-236 (Zbl 0412.30020), and Alpay-Dijksma-Rovnyak-de Snoo, OT 96 (1997) (Zbl 0879.47006). I checked the claim directly. For real entire f, -f'/f has only simple poles with residue -m, whatever the zero multiplicity. A pole at b in C+ contributes exactly one negative square, while the conjugate pole in C- and real poles are Nevanlinna. So kappa is the number of distinct C+ zero locations, matching F13 and its (z^2+1)^m example. The repo already invokes Krein-Langer in safe_line L-91034 ('krein-langer-cauchy-source-critical-port-decomposition').
verification.correction: The 'open subset' invariance lemma for holomorphic kernels does not literally cover restriction to a real interval. For the real safe axis, one needs the Taylor-coefficient (confluent) argument for sesqui-analytic kernels, or more directly Audenaert's theorem. The recommendation should be a cross-reference to the existing L-91034, not a new import. Related literature: Bhatia-Jain, 'Inertia of Kwong matrices' (arXiv:2307.16007). The ADRS theorem number was not opened.

obstruction: Matrix-monotone classes have strict gaps P_{n+1}(I)⊊P_n(I) for every n and every interval, so positivity at a fixed finite order never implies the next order abstractly.
citation: F. Hansen, G. Ji, J. Tomiyama, Gaps between classes of matrix monotone functions, Bull. London Math. Soc. 36 (2004) 53-58, arXiv:math/0204204 (introduction read); W. F. Donoghue, Monotone Matrix Functions and Analytic Continuation, Springer 1974.
how_it_constrains: Loewner-hierarchy counterpart of the repo's 'order three does not bootstrap abstractly' and of the X9 countermodel. Via Audenaert's order transfer (Kwong order 2N implies Loewner order N for tp and p), any order-4 proof must use source-specific information, as the order-3 proof did, not an abstract extension lemma.

verification.evidence: Full text of math/0204204; Bull. LMS 36 (2004) 53-58 confirmed by Zbl 1047.26008. The introduction defines P_{n+1}(I) subset of P_n(I). The paper shows 'a gap between P_n(I) and P_{n+1}(I) for any positive integer n and any nontrivial interval I different from the whole real line' (Thm 2 and corollaries).
verification.correction: The gap result is stated for intervals other than R, not for 'every interval'. This is harmless here, since the relevant intervals are (0,inf) or (1/4,inf). Loewner-class gaps do not by themselves give Kwong (anti-Loewner) class gaps, because Audenaert's transfer goes one way only (Kwong 2N to Loewner N). The direct evidence that order 3 does not bootstrap is the repo's own X9 countermodel. The 'source-specific information' conclusion is a heuristic, not a theorem.

obstruction: Information dispersal in finite-order hierarchies. Chasse: if all zeros with |gamma|<T are on the line, then J^{d,0} has only real zeros for d<T^2. Farmer's model X_10 (cos z with two zero pairs moved to ±10±i) has hyperbolic J^{d,0} for d<=118, and all zeros of its first derivative are real.
citation: D. W. Farmer, Jensen polynomials are not a plausible route to proving the Riemann Hypothesis, Adv. Math. 411 (2022) 108781, arXiv:2008.07206, sections 2, 4.1, 4.2 and Table 4.1; M. Chasse, Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. 58 (2013).
how_it_constrains: The repo's X9 model already shows safe-axis order 3 cannot see an off-line quartet at height 1025. It is unknown whether the safe-axis Kwong hierarchy disperses information like Jensen polynomials (order ~T^2) or concentrates it like Sra's PF orders (PF_k forces RH up to height Y with N(Y)<=k+1). Under Farmer's criteria (A/B/C), OPEN_CUTS section 3 is a repackaging of RH whose usefulness depends on that rate. X_10 is also an explicit counterexample to naive derivative descent: f has nonreal zeros while f' is real-rooted.

verification.evidence: Farmer 2008.07206 full text. Section 4.2 gives Chasse: 'if all zeros with |gamma|<T are on the line, J^{d,0} has only real zeros for d<T^2'. X_10 = cos z with the zeros at +-5pi/2 and +-7pi/2 moved to +-10+-i. Table 4.1 and the text: J^{d,0}_{X10} is real-rooted for d<=118. Farmer states 'all zeros of the first derivative X10' are real' from inspecting the graph. Section 4.1 gives the (A)/(B)/(C) taxonomy and the concentrated-versus-dispersed criterion. Sra Cor C.12 confirms 'PF_k and N(Y)<=k+1 imply RH through height Y'. Farmer is published in Adv. Math. 411 (2022) 108781.

obstruction: High-derivative behaviour is universal and RH-blind. Kim 1996 (fixed windows become real-rooted for any real entire function of order <2 with zeros in a strip), Ki 2006 (cosine limit), Gunns-Hughes 2019 (the same limit in the extended Selberg class, which contains RH-violating functions), Pemantle-Subramanian 2017 (random Poisson zeros) and Campbell-O'Rourke-Renfrew 2024 (cosine universality via finite free probability).
citation: Farmer arXiv:2008.07206 section 2 (summarizes Kim 1996, Ki 2006, Gunns-Hughes J. Number Theory 194 (2019) 30-43); R. Pemantle, S. Subramanian, Trans. AMS 369 (2017) 8743-8764, arXiv:1409.7956; A. Campbell, S. O'Rourke, D. Renfrew, arXiv:2410.06403.
how_it_constrains: The repo's high-derivative entry and safe-ray theorems sit in a regime that holds whether or not RH is true. All RH content must therefore be carried by the descent step (OPEN_CUTS section 4). This is consistent with the repo's own scope statements and makes clear that the entry regime cannot help with the descent loss budget.

verification.evidence: Farmer section 2 summarizes Kim (any real entire function of order <2 with zeros in a strip), Ki 2006, and Gunns-Hughes, J. Number Theory 194 (2019) 30-43 (arXiv:1803.10001). Farmer: the extended Selberg class 'includes many examples that do not satisfy the analogue of the Riemann Hypothesis'. Pemantle-Subramanian, Trans. AMS 369 (2017) 8743-8764, is confirmed by Zbl 1380.30002. The Campbell-O'Rourke-Renfrew 2410.06403 abstract proves cosine universality 'for a class of even entire functions with only real roots'.
verification.correction: The RH-blindness evidence is Kim's theorem and Gunns-Hughes. Pemantle-Subramanian (random Poisson real zeros) and Campbell-O'Rourke-Renfrew (only real roots) show universality only within real-rooted classes, not RH-blindness. Farmer also notes that Coffey's proposition implies Ki's limit.

obstruction: Monotonicity of the de Bruijn-Newman constant along derivatives, and Lambda>=0. The constants lambda^(m) for Xi_lambda^(m) are nonincreasing in m with limit <=0, and for every lambda>0 all but finitely many zeros of Xi_lambda are real and simple (Ki-Kim-Lee). Rodgers-Tao prove Lambda>=0.
citation: H. Ki, Y.-O. Kim, J. Lee, On the de Bruijn-Newman constant, Adv. Math. 222 (2009) 281-306 (zbMATH 1175.30023 review); B. Rodgers, T. Tao, The de Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative, Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020), arXiv:1801.05914.
how_it_constrains: Differentiation can only improve real-rootedness, so descent runs against the monotone direction. If RH holds, Lambda^(0)=0 exactly: there is no uniform positive margin at the base level. A descent or perturbation argument with a fixed strict margin at order 0 cannot exist; losses must be quantified down to zero margin.

verification.evidence: Zbl 1175.30023 (Ki-Kim-Lee, Adv. Math. 222 (2009) 281-306) review: Lambda<1/2; the sequence lambda^(m) for Xi_lambda^(m) is nonincreasing with limit <=0; for every lambda>0, all but finitely many zeros of Xi_lambda are real and simple. Rodgers-Tao arXiv:1801.05914 abstract: Lambda>=0, and RH is equivalent to Lambda<=0, so RH implies Lambda=0.
verification.correction: Use KKL's normalization, Lambda=4 lambda^(0), not 'Lambda^(0)'. The 'zero margin' is in the de Bruijn-Newman heat-flow parameter. Transferring it into a ban on fixed-margin arguments in the repo's derivative-order descent is a heuristic reading, not a theorem.

obstruction: de Branges's positivity conditions for the space H(xi(1-iz)) are not satisfied; Conrey-Li show this for zeta and for the real character chi_-4.
citation: J. B. Conrey, X.-J. Li, A note on some positivity conditions related to zeta- and L-functions, IMRN 2000 no. 18, 929-940, arXiv:math/9812166 (abstract); discussed in Lagarias arXiv:math/0601653 section 6.
how_it_constrains: Bears on the 'direct infinite canonical/Hermite-Biehler system for xi' that integration notes list as a live direction. Any such route must avoid de Branges's specific sufficient conditions, which are known to fail.

verification.evidence: Conrey-Li, math/9812166 introduction: they 'give examples showing that de Branges' positivity conditions, which imply the generalized Riemann hypothesis, are not satisfied' for the spaces of zeta(s) and L(s,chi_4). Published in IMRN 2000, no. 18, 929-940 (Zbl 0966.11039). Lagarias math/0601653 section 6 discusses the same point. The repo's integration/2026-08-11 OPEN_HINGES A6 lists a 'direct infinite canonical/Hermite-Biehler' construction as live, so the constraint is relevant.

obstruction: Positive definite real Hankel matrices are exponentially ill-conditioned: the spectral condition number grows at least geometrically in the order (Tyrtyshnikov; Beckermann).
citation: B. Beckermann, The condition number of real Vandermonde, Krylov and positive definite Hankel matrices, Numer. Math. 85 (2000) 553-577; E. E. Tyrtyshnikov, How bad are Hankel matrices?, Numer. Math. 67 (1994).
how_it_constrains: The GAP_BLOCKED growing-order claim (eventual matrix monotonicity of the Xi impedance to growing order) cannot be closed by additive perturbation of Dobsch-Hankel matrices with order-independent error. The relative margin of the model shrinks geometrically, so a normalized moving frame (as in Sra Thm C.9) or a structural argument is required.

verification.evidence: Zbl 0797.65039 (Tyrtyshnikov, Numer. Math. 67 (1994) 261-269): the spectral condition number of any real positive definite Hankel matrix of order n is at least 3*2^{n-6}. Zbl 0965.15003 (Beckermann, Numer. Math. 85 (2000) 553-577) gives geometric upper and lower bounds. Evidence upgrades from memory to zbMATH reviews. The inference (additive error must be geometrically small relative to the Hankel norm) is sound.

obstruction: Pole obstruction for PF orders: if Theta or Lambda is PF_k, every zero below roughly the (k+2)-nd ordinate is on the line, i.e. PF_k and N(Y)<=k+1 imply RH through height Y. Unconditional PF orders are therefore bounded by what zero verification has certified.
citation: S. Sra arXiv:2611.02944, Thm C.11 and Cor C.12.
how_it_constrains: Benchmark for the Pick programme. Any unconditional finite-order safe-axis Kwong theorem is bounded by the verified height if the hierarchy concentrates information; if it disperses (OB2), finite orders cost nothing but say little. The repo should determine which regime applies before investing in order >=4.

verification.evidence: Sra 2611.02944 full text. Theorem C.11 (first nonreal pole with multiplicities, bounds d_Theta and d_Lambda) and Corollary C.12 (f in PF_k and N(Y)<=k+1 imply beta=1/2 for every zero with 0<gamma<=Y). The abstract says that if either density is PF_k, every zero lower than the (k+2)-nd lies on the line.

tool: Signed-perturbation scheme with an order-independent bound. Replace each unverified squared rate lambda_rho=(gamma-i delta_rho)^2 by gamma^2; this gives an exact PF_inf (here: Stieltjes) model times a signed factor M_U with weighted variation epsilon_U(Q)<1 (Lemma C.4). Then use a moving lower-triangular frame C_x with C_x H_m[f](x) C_x^T = J_m and ||C_x H_m[f](x-u) C_x^T||<=e^{Qu} (Thm C.9), so all determinant signs up to order m reduce to scalar inequalities (Thm 3.4: n>=8m verified factors with rates <=Q).
citation: S. Sra arXiv:2611.02944, Lemma C.4, Thm C.9, Thm 3.4, eq. (3.2), Appendix C.10.
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS section 3 / OPEN.OPERATOR.XI.PICK_ORDER4_PLUS at each fixed order N>=4, and OPERATOR.XI.FRACTIONAL_STRING_GROWING_ORDER (GAP_BLOCKED: 'supply quantified moving-band Vandermonde and perturbation bounds uniform in order').
precise_next_step: Step 1: write p=p_real+p_corr, with p_real(t)=Sum_{all rho} 2m/(t+gamma^2), which is exactly Stieltjes and hence Kwong-PSD in every order, and p_corr the sum over unverified orbits of 2Re[2m/(t+lambda_rho)-2m/(t+gamma^2)], each term O(m gamma/(t+gamma^2)^2). Step 2: take the Dobsch-Hankel matrices M_N(t;tp) (Heinavaara) or, directly, the Cauchy-Gram form of the Kwong kernel, Sum c_l Re[v_l v_l^*] with v_l=(1/(x_i+i sqrt(a_l))). Orthonormalize them in a frame built from n>=8N verified atoms with a_l<=Q. Step 3: prove an analogue of (C.19), i.e. a bound on the frame-normalized p_corr contribution that is uniform in t>0 and in N, compared against Sum_{gamma>U} gamma^-2<=2(log U+1)/U. Start with N=4 as a bounded contribution.
risk: Pick/Kwong kernels are Cauchy-type, not translation-invariant Toeplitz, so Sra's e^{Qu} shift bound has no direct analogue; the natural variable is multiplicative. Audenaert's order transfer goes only from Kwong order 2N to Loewner order N, so proving N-monotonicity of tp and p alone does not give Kwong order N; a direct Kwong-kernel argument may be needed. Large-t behaviour (t>>H^2, where the verified atoms degenerate toward a=0 in rescaled coordinates) may break uniformity.

tool: Audenaert's exact anti-Loewner/Loewner correspondence: K_g+L_g = 2 Loewner[sqrt(x) g(sqrt x)](x_i^2) and K_g-L_g = -2 D Loewner[g(sqrt x)/sqrt x] D, together with the sign-independence of det[(s_i g_i+s_j g_j)/(s_i x_i+s_j x_j)] (Prop 2, Thm 2.2, proved by partial Gaussian elimination X=DYD).
citation: K. M. R. Audenaert, Proc. AMS 139 (2011) 4217-4223, arXiv:1008.2943, Prop 2, Thm 2.1, Thm 2.2, eq. (3).
target_gap: Order-4 factorization attempt (L-92000 generalization); pinning OPERATOR.XI.LOEWNER_LOW_ORDER ('reciprocal Loewner-Hankel congruence') to a citable identity; precise statement of the all-order criterion L-91904.
precise_next_step: Apply Audenaert's elimination (eq. 3) to the 4x4 Kwong matrix of F with g_i=x_i p(x_i^2). Compute the Schur complement Y symbolically and test whether det K_4 factors into divided differences of 1/p and tp, as the 3x3 case does, or into 2x2 Loewner determinants of tp and p. Then record in the xi_pick packet: Kwong order 2N implies tp N-monotone and p N-monotone decreasing.
risk: The 4x4 determinant may not factor into scalar curvatures. Audenaert notes that no sufficiency argument at fixed N is known.

tool: Dobsch-Donoghue local characterization as proved by Heinavaara: f in C^{2n-1} is n-monotone on (a,b) iff M_n(t)=[f^(i+j-1)(t)/(i+j-1)!]_{i,j<=n} is PSD for every t (similarly for n-convexity with the Kraus/Hankel matrix). The proof uses integral representations linking Loewner matrices to Hankel matrices; n-monotonicity is a local property.
citation: O. Heinavaara, Local characterizations for the matrix monotonicity and convexity of fixed order, Proc. AMS 146 (2018), arXiv:1608.07516, Thms 5 and 7; Donoghue 1974 Chs. 7-8.
target_gap: OPERATOR.XI.FRACTIONAL_STRING_FIXED_ORDER (state 'eventual n-monotonicity on [T_n,inf)' as pointwise Hankel positivity with explicit T_n) and the growing-order GAP_BLOCKED row.
precise_next_step: Write tp(t)~c sqrt(t) log t plus zero corrections. Express M_n(t;tp) relative to the beta-Hankel matrix of t^{1/2}, which is positive definite with a known Hilbert-type structure, and give explicit T_n with M_n(t)>0 for t>=T_n. Because n-monotonicity is local, gluing [T_n,inf) with a separate certificate on (0,T_n] would give global n-monotonicity of tp. That is a necessary condition for Kwong order 2n.
risk: Gives Loewner (not Kwong) positivity. Explicit T_n may grow very fast (OB6). It controls tp only; p (monotone decreasing) needs a parallel argument.

tool: Height-to-order calibration: Chasse's theorem (verification to T gives Jensen hyperbolicity for d<T^2) and Sra's pole obstruction (Thm C.11/Cor C.12), combined with Krein-Langer negative-square counting.
citation: Farmer arXiv:2008.07206 section 4.2; Sra arXiv:2611.02944 Thm C.11 and Cor C.12; Krein-Langer 1977.
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS section 3: determine whether finite-order safe-axis Pick positivity carries RH information (OB2 versus OB7).
precise_next_step: For the X9-type model (critical pair at gamma0=1, one off-line quartet (a,b,m)=(1/4,b,1)), compute with exact rational arithmetic the minimal packet size N(b) at which some real-node Kwong matrix has a negative eigenvalue, for b=2^k up to about 2^12. A logarithmic N(b) means the hierarchy concentrates information (worth pursuing); a polynomial N(b) means it disperses (deprioritize per Farmer).
risk: This is a diagnostic, not a theorem. Ill-conditioning (OB6) requires certified linear algebra; the repo's LDL^* / moat pipeline can be reused.

tool: Sra's all-order zero-exclusion principle (Lemma 4.2): for real entire f of genus <=1 and an interval I where |x-Re zeta|>=|Im zeta| for every nonreal zero, the generalized Laguerre coefficients L_n[f](x) (coefficients of y^{2n} in |f(x+iy)|^2) are >=0 for all n. Consequently RH verified to height T gives L_n[Xi]>=0 for all n on |x|<=T-1/2 (Thm 1.3).
citation: S. Sra arXiv:2611.02944, Lemma 4.2, Thm 1.3; G. Csordas, R. S. Varga, Adv. Appl. Math. 11 (1990) 328-357, Thm 2.9; Csordas-Ruttan-Varga 1991.
target_gap: safe_line OPEN.OPERATOR.RADIAL_CURVATURE; the general-height RH-necessary tests (CURRENT_RESULTS section 6) as a locality/complement theorem; and derivative descent, where a Fourier critical point of f^(n) is exactly a violation of L_1[f^(n-1)]>=0 at a zero of f^(n).
precise_next_step: (a) Check whether radial curvature (T-91002) is a reparametrization of Jensen's convexity criterion d^2/dy^2|Xi(x+iy)|^2>=0 (Polya 1927 condition I'). If so, cite Jensen/Polya and import Sra Thm 1.3 for the verified range. (b) Test whether the product-coefficient argument of Lemma 4.2 adapts to show: for |T|<=H-c, all-order Pick positivity at height T holds whenever the nodes keep a geometric separation from every unverified zero. This would be a genuine locality theorem for the finite Pick boxes.
risk: Pick positivity, unlike Laguerre positivity, is not local (a negative square is visible from any open set, PA15). So (b) likely gives only an 'approximately local' statement with exponentially small, not zero, error.

tool: Fourier-Polya critical-point theory: the number of nonreal zeros equals twice the total number of critical points over all derivatives (Ki-Kim 2000 for genus 0; Kim 1996 for zeros in a strip with convergence exponent of nonreal zeros <1-rho/2).
citation: H. Ki, Y.-O. Kim, Duke Math. J. 104 (2000) 45-73 (Thms 4.1-4.3, per zbMATH review); Y.-O. Kim, Proc. AMS 124 (1996) 819-830 and J. Math. Anal. Appl. 204 (1996) 472-481.
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS section 4 (derivative descent) and F01 (reverse-Rolle inertia).
precise_next_step: Restate descent as: RH holds iff Xi^(n) has no Fourier critical points for every n>=0, valid in any class where the Fourier-Polya count is proved. Check whether Ki-Kim Thm 4.2/4.3 covers order-1, genus-1 functions with zeros in |Im z|<1/2, such as Xi or G(t)=xi(1/2+sqrt t) after the change of variable. If not, record exactly which hypothesis fails (e.g. Kim's convergence-exponent<1/2 condition). That gives the repo's 'nonreal-critical block' a classical frame and a sharp boundary.
risk: The general Fourier-Polya theorem may not cover Xi without a sparsity hypothesis on off-line zeros. If it does, the reformulation is still RH-equivalent, not a proof.

tool: Lagarias's Hermite-Biehler shift family E_h(z)=xi(1/2+h-iz) and de Branges's Lemma 5 (|E(s)|>|E(1-conj s)| on Re s>1/2 implies A and B have only real, interlacing zeros).
citation: J. C. Lagarias, arXiv:math/0601653, Lemmas 2.1, 2.2 and 6.1.
target_gap: OPEN_CUTS section 4: an alternative entry regime to high derivatives, and a test of the remark that raw innerness implies RH.
precise_next_step: Prove or cite the equivalence 'E_h is Hermite-Biehler iff xi has no zeros with Re s>1/2+h'. If it holds, shift descent h->0 is exactly the zero-free half-plane problem (cf. Freitas arXiv:math/0507368, a Li-type criterion for zero-free half-planes). Compare its loss budget with the frozen-lambda safe-ray E_{r,lambda} to decide which entry regime has the better descent algebra.
risk: Likely shows only that shift descent is equivalent to classical zero-free-region improvements, a known hard problem. Its value is clarifying, not resolving.
